devotionals.memoryVerse: Hebrews 13:1 KJV - "Let brotherly love continue."
devotionals.devotional:
I once read an article on the current state of decadence of the church and, alongside with the writer, I wondered if the events written in Acts 2:44-46 were real, compared to what we currently observe in Christendom. Unfortunately, Christians today behave like communist Stalin who was quoted as saying that the greatest thrill to him was to win someone's trust and when he lays his head on his chest, stab him to death.

Love, and indeed trust, is a lost virtue among Christians today. One of my friends said that he would rather do business with an unbeliever than with a so called 'born-again' today because they are swindlers. Another said he will quickly be on alert if anyone introduces himself-herself to him as a 'born-again'. We have so quickly lost our salinity. Where is our impact to win our society and change the world for the better?

Jesus prayed '... that they may be one ...' John 17:11. When we live in distrust, rancour, backbiting and disharmony, we cannot influence our society for Christ but when there is true love among us, we can make a positive impact both in the life of our fellow Christian and the society and the dirty stories that emanate from our churches today will be much abated, 1 Peter 4:8 and only then can we really prove to be truly Christ's disciples.

Lesson: True brotherly love is the hallmark of genuine Christianity. Without it, we lose our impact on society and cannot be recognised as Christ's disciples.

Action: Reach out to a fellow believer you have been distant from. Forgive any offence and restore the bond of brotherly love today.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Help me Lord to forgive and love my brother just like Jesus did.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Philippians 4:19 KJV - "But my God shall supply all your need according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus."
devotionals.devotional:
In almost all religious forums today, we are compelled to give. We are promised a well of divine blessings if we do. All sort of antics and mantra are employed to get us to part with our hard-earned resources. Miracles, breakthrough, success and the like are only for those who give. Different bible verses are quoted to brainwash us into giving all we have. Prosperity prayers, good visions and prophecies are exclusively reserved for those who donate large sums of money 'willingly'. Many have stolen or have committed heinous crimes in order to give and receive blessings.

The abuse of this opportunity to serve the Lord with our resources have made many of us indifferent to such calls and preachers, especially when the preachers are living in affluence and the bulk of their followers are struggling to eke out a living. The media is awash with reports of pastors who are living big at the expense of their congregants, who are always compelled to give with promises of divine blessings that never come while many have given themselves into penury.

Are we to shy away from this divine mandate because of these reasons? The answer is no. There are still so many who are genuinely in need of help. Liberality is enshrined in scripture and a lot of promises-blessings go with it. Apostle Paul prayed for the Philippian church in our text for God to supply all their need because they gave to him. However, he did not have to depend on them for his livelihood.

Lesson: True liberality is not about being manipulated into giving but about genuinely helping those in need. Ask God for discernment to know where to sow your seeds.

Action: Identify one genuine need today and give cheerfully, trusting God to supply your own needs in return.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord give me the discerning heart and the grace to help someone in need today.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 John 4:8 KJV - "He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love."
devotionals.devotional:
The word "love" is a mystery. I have heard it defined several times, in several ways and in diverse contexts. Each speaker tries to convince us that his-her conception of the word is the ultimate but the true definition of the word, somehow, seems elusive and its application tends to generate more questions than answers. If anyone is asked to define love, he-she will give different definitions depending on his-her age, environment, state of mind and exposure.

Regardless of what we make out love to be, this chapter of the Bible, popularly known as the "love chapter" gives us a graphic description of the attributes of love and tells us it is more than all spiritual gifts combined. That is to say, even if we are endowed with ALL spiritual gifts but is lacking in love, we are not Christians! Verses 4-8 tells us the attribute of love: Longsuffering, kindness, does not envy, humility, is self abased, behaves right, is self sacrificing, patient, shows charitableness, is discrete, forbears, believes, hopes, endures and has faith.

Can these characteristics be said to be true in your life? Defining the word aright is not the essence but living out the life. No matter how we try, verses 12 and 13 tell us we cannot perfectly understand what true love is, at least not in this life. Perfection in life is when we live out the true life of love. That notwithstanding, we should strive to live a life of love as we strive for perfection in all we do.

Lesson: Love is not defined by words but by actions. The attributes of love in 1 Corinthians 13 are the standard for every believer's life.

Action: Choose one attribute of love from 1 Corinthians 13:4-8 and practise it intentionally today with everyone you meet.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Help me Lord to show a true picture of Your love to anyone who I come across.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Galatians 4:6 KJV - "And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of His Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father."
devotionals.devotional:
When I was much younger, there was a delicious pear tree besides our house. I came home one day to meet our neighbour's children harvesting the pears. When they were done, they gave other children very few each and gave me a bag full of pears – so big for a child like me then. I was so excited. I had never had such amount of pears as mine. When my dad came home that evening, I could not wait to show him my pears. He asked me where the pears came from and I told him everything but he was not excited as I was. He asked me how I could be so foolish and why I would allow somebody to give me what is mine. He said that the pear tree belongs to me!

Likewise, often, we let the Devil dictate to us because we do not know our rights in Christ! Just like the prodigal son's elder brother who did not know his rights (Luke 15:30-32), some Christians do not know their rights in Christ. The father said '... all I have is yours.' All that God has is ours because Christ has paid it all.

Some of you who are meant to be employers are applicants today - CLAIM YOUR RIGHTS! Some of you reading this are meant to be landlords but are living as tenants - CLAIM YOUR RIGHTS! Some of you reading this ought to be married by now but are still single - CLAIM YOUR RIGHTS! Some of you are meant to be rich but live as paupers - CLAIM YOUR RIGHTS! Jesus has paid for all of it!

Lesson: As a child of God, you have rights and privileges in Christ. Ignorance of these rights allows the enemy to rob you of what is rightfully yours.

Action: Identify one area where you have been living below your inheritance in Christ. Declare your rights based on God's Word and take a step of faith to claim them.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Say every morning that "I am what God says I am, I have what God says I have and I will be what God says I will be."

devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 1:3 KJV - "And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper."
devotionals.devotional:
I have observed that lies have wings and fly but truth have legs. Lies go faster than the truth. This was the case with the story of Joseph. The brothers deceived the father to believe that he was dead. The devil is not actually fighting you. He is attacking your dreams. NB: What would become of your dreams is in your hands. The devil cannot determine that.

Joseph's brothers brought evidence to the father that Joseph is already dead. Some lies have evidence. No matter the evidence, lies are lies. Evidence or no evidence, the truth must surely surface. Another evidence is coming! Lies might go faster than truth, but the truth must prevail. The devil might have said that your business is dead, but God is saying that He will restore all the things that cankerworm have eaten over the years. Joel 2. A righteous might fall seven times but he shall rise again.

There is somebody whose business is dead, your business will be raised. Your womb might have been declared dead, but the word of God is saying in Psalm 1:1-3 that you are like a tree planted by the rivers of water. You might be sick in your body. Though doctors are used by God, but their words are not final. There is hope for that part of your body. It is declared alive. Wombs are declared alive. Dead business will rise again. Visions will be fulfilled. Dreams will be fulfilled.

Lesson: Lies travel faster than truth, but truth always prevails. What the enemy has declared dead in your life, God is declaring alive again.

Action: Identify one area where the enemy has spoken death over your life. Stand up and declare today: "My Joseph is alive!"
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I declare that every dead dream, vision, or situation in my life is alive again by Your power. My Joseph is alive!

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 John 4:4 KJV - "Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is He that is in you, than he that is in the world."
devotionals.devotional:
Scarecrow is an effigy, typically made of straw and dressed in old clothes, fixed to a pole in a field to deter birds from eating seeds or crops planted there. Are you paralysed by fear? Learn how to turn your fear into faith.

A wise bird knows that a scarecrow is simply an advertisement. It announces that some very juicy and delicious fruit is to be had for the picking. There are scarecrows in all the best gardens. If I am wise, I too shall treat the scarecrow as though it were an invitation. Every giant in the way which makes me feel like a grasshopper is only a scarecrow beckoning me to God's richest blessings. Faith is a bird which loves to perch on scarecrows.

All fears are groundless. What is your scarecrow today? Difficult circumstances? Personal inadequacy? Uncertainty? The enemy of your soul wants to keep you away from the place of Gods' blessing. Perch on scarecrow by faith, start singing, and expect an abundant feast!

Lesson: The giants and obstacles in your path are not there to stop you but to announce that there is rich blessing beyond them. Turn your fear into faith.

Action: Identify your "scarecrow" today. Instead of running from it, perch on it by faith, praise God, and move forward toward your promised land.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I refuse to be paralysed by fear. Every giant in my path is just a scarecrow. I perch on it by faith and move forward to my blessings.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Philippians 4:6 KJV - "Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God."
devotionals.devotional:
You may have played the game when you were a child. You interlace your fingers with someone else's and try to bend the other's hands back until one or the other cries "Mercy!" The winner is the one who gets the other person to surrender.

Sometimes we try to play "Mercy" with God when we pray. We have a request that we desperately want answered in a certain way, so we try to "bend His fingers back" and get Him to give in. When it seems we aren't winning, we try a little harder to convince Him by begging or bargaining. We may even give up grudgingly and say, "Lord, You always win! That's not fair!"

God does want honesty of heart. But occasionally in our honesty a demanding spirit comes out. Deep down we know that prayer is not meant to be a contest with God that we try to win. In our wiser moments, we make our requests known to our Lord, surrender them to Him, rely on His grace, and wait for His answers. Instead of praying with grudging resignation, "Lord, You always win", surrender to Him. Say "Mercy!"

Lesson: Prayer is not a contest to bend God's will to ours but a surrender of our will to His. Stop fighting and start trusting.

Action: Identify one prayer request you have been demanding from God. Surrender it to Him today, say "Mercy!", and trust His perfect will.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Help me Lord to prayerfully make my requests known to You and then trust Your perfect answer.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Proverbs 15:1 KJV - "A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger."
devotionals.devotional:
It has been observed that the way a person was addressed determined to a large extent the kind of response he would make. For example, when an individual was spoken to in a soft voice, he would answer in a similar manner. But when he was shouted at, his reply came back in the same sharp tone. This was true whether the communication was given face-to-face, over the intercom, or by telephone.

Proverbs 15:1 says 'A soft answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.' What we say and how we say it not only makes a difference in the reaction we receive, but it also determines whether conflict or peace will result. How many arguments could be avoided and tense situations relaxed if we practised the truth of this verse!

The next time someone speaks to you in a harsh or angry tone, reverse the trend by expressing meekness, quietness of spirit, and loving concern. What a difference a soft answer can make in our relationships!

Lesson: Your response determines the outcome of any conversation. A soft answer disarms anger and opens the door for peace.

Action: The next time someone speaks harshly to you, intentionally respond with a soft and gentle answer. Watch how it changes the atmosphere.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, help me to respond with soft answers even when provoked. Let my words bring peace, not conflict.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 50:15 KJV - "Call upon Me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify Me."
devotionals.devotional:
Sometimes bad news catches us totally off guard and reduces us to tears. We hurt so badly that we need time to nurse the hurt; we need time away from distractions; we shun even physical sustenance. News about the destruction of Nehemiah's beloved homeland evoked such a response in him. His feelings of patriotism, of concern for the Jews in Jerusalem, made him heartsick. As a royal cupbearer, Nehemiah was living a comfortable life in the palace of the king of Persia, far away from the strife and violence that ripped Jerusalem. Yet, he chose not to ignore the situation. He did not turn a deaf ear nor shrug his shoulders at the news. In his distress he wept bitterly and went to God in prayer for solace.

We don't have to search the media for bad news about our city. It is there, up front and personal, all around us. God expects us to be concerned. He wants our hearts to be broken as we consider those who are less fortunate and are experiencing pain and suffering. God wants us to act, but he desires that we come to him first, in prayer, for guidance and direction.

What is your typical reaction to bad news? Think about your city. Have you ever felt particularly moved by its conditions? What situations triggered this feeling and how did you respond? Did you pray? Ask God to direct you to a particular troubling issue in your city. Spend time praying and fasting for its resolution.

Lesson: Bad news should drive us to prayer, not despair. God is looking for people whose hearts are broken enough to pray and act.

Action: Identify one troubling issue in your community or city. Commit to praying specifically about it every day this week.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, thank You that I can come boldly to Your throne of grace. Make me sensitive to the needs of others, and let me seek Your loving support through the gift of prayer.

devotionals.topic: Let Us Keep to the Point
devotionals.memoryVerse: Philippians 1:21 KJV - "For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain."
devotionals.devotional:
We will all feel very much ashamed if we do not yield to Jesus the areas of our lives He has asked us to yield to Him. It's as if Paul were saying, 'My determined purpose is to be my utmost for His highest—my best for His glory.' To reach that level of determination is a matter of the will, not of debate or of reasoning. It is absolute and irrevocable surrender of the will at that point.

An undue amount of thought and consideration for ourselves is what keeps us from making that decision, although we cover it up with the pretence that it is others we are considering. When we think seriously about what it will cost others if we obey the call of Jesus, we tell God He doesn't know what our obedience will mean. Keep to the point—He does know. Shut out every other thought and keep yourself before God in this one thing only—my utmost for His highest. I am determined to be absolutely and entirely for Him and Him alone.

Paul was determined that nothing would stop him from doing exactly what God wanted. But before we choose to follow God's will, a crisis must develop in our lives. This happens because we tend to be unresponsive to God's gentler nudges. He brings us to the place where He asks us to be our utmost for Him and we begin to debate. He then providentially produces a crisis where we have to decide—for or against. That moment becomes a great crossroads in our lives.

Lesson: Surrender to God's will is not a debate but a decision. Do not let concern for what others think keep you from obeying God.

Action: If a crisis of decision has come to you, stop debating and surrender your will to Jesus absolutely and irrevocably today.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, forgive my tardiness; it takes me so long to awaken to some things. I surrender my will to You absolutely and irrevocably.

devotionals.topic: The Voice of the Nature of God
devotionals.memoryVerse: Isaiah 6:8 KJV - "Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for Us? Then said I, Here am I; send me."
devotionals.devotional:
When we talk about the call of God, we often forget the most important thing, namely, the nature of Him who calls. There are many things calling each of us today. Some of these calls will be answered, and others will not even be heard. The call is the expression of the nature of the One who calls, and we can only recognise the call if that same nature is in us. The call of God is the expression of God's nature, not ours.

God providentially weaves the threads of His call through our lives, and only we can distinguish them. It is the threading of God's voice directly to us over a certain concern, and it is useless to seek another person's opinion of it. Our dealings over the call of God should be kept exclusively between ourselves and Him.

The call of God is not a reflection of my nature; my personal desires and temperament are of no consideration. As long as I dwell on my own qualities and traits and think about what I am suited for, I will never hear the call of God. But when God brings me into the right relationship with Himself, I will be in the same condition Isaiah was. Isaiah was so attuned to God, because of the great crisis he had just endured, that the call of God penetrated his soul.

Lesson: You will never hear God's call as long as you are focused on your own abilities and preferences. Get into right relationship with God, and His call will penetrate your soul.

Action: Spend time alone with God today, shutting out every other voice. Ask Him to speak, and say with Isaiah, "Here am I; send me."
devotionals.prayerConfession: "Let me hear Your voice"—that is my prayer. I am willing beyond all my expression to hear You, to perceive You, to be thrilled with Your presence.

devotionals.topic: Don't Just Stand There, Pray Something
devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Chronicles 7:14 KJV - "If My people, which are called by My name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek My face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land."
devotionals.devotional:
Nehemiah does not seek counsel from outside sources but goes directly to God in prayer. Here, he pours out his heart, acknowledging God as mighty and sovereign and one who is faithful in upholding the covenants he makes. Like a priest atoning for the sins of the people, Nehemiah begs for mercy as he confesses that all of Israel, including him and his family, has wilfully disobeyed God's commands.

In similar fashion, our own cities lie in ruins. Some of it is structural decay where buildings are burnt out, vandalised and unoccupied. At other times, it is moral and spiritual bankruptcy where godly living, ethics, morality and civility have morphed into everyone doing what is "right" in his or her own eyes. We have moved far away from the tenets upon which the Founding Fathers established our beloved country.

Note, Nehemiah says the people sinned by "choosing to disobey" God's laws. Can you see areas in which the leaders in our cities have chosen to disobey God's laws? Like Nehemiah, we must unequivocally address our sin and disobedience as we come before God. What responsibility do you take for the shape the city is in? When was the last time you earnestly prayed for the spiritual health of your city?

Lesson: Prayer is not a last resort but the first response. Before you act, pray. Before you speak, pray. Don't just stand there—pray something.

Action: Confess your own sins and the sins of your community before God today. Ask friends to join you in regular prayer for your city.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord God, I acknowledge You as supreme ruler over all. My heart bleeds for all of us in our communities. We, too, have ignored Your commands. Forgive us, Lord, as only You can, and put us back on the path of righteousness.

devotionals.topic: The Call of the Natural Life
devotionals.memoryVerse: Galatians 1:15-16 KJV - "But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother's womb, and called me by His grace, to reveal His Son in me, that I might preach Him among the heathen..."
devotionals.devotional:
The call of God is not a call to serve Him in any particular way. My contact with the nature of God will shape my understanding of His call and will help me realise what I truly desire to do for Him. The call of God is an expression of His nature; the service which results in my life is suited to me and is an expression of my nature.

The call of the natural life was stated by the apostle Paul—'When it pleased God to reveal His Son in me, that I might preach Him among the Gentiles.' Service is the overflow which pours from a life filled with love and devotion. But strictly speaking, there is no call to that. Service is what I bring to the relationship and is the reflection of my identification with the nature of God. Service becomes a natural part of my life.

God brings me into the proper relationship with Himself so that I can understand His call, and then I serve Him on my own out of a motivation of absolute love. Service to God is the deliberate love-gift of a nature that has heard the call of God. Therefore, when I receive His nature and hear His call, His divine voice resounds throughout His nature and mine and the two become one in service.

Lesson: True service flows naturally from a life that has been transformed by encountering God. It is not forced but flows from love.

Action: Stop trying to serve God out of obligation. Spend time today in His presence until His nature becomes yours, and service becomes your delight.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, take me as Your servant. Let Your nature become my nature, and let service flow naturally from my love for You.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Acts 1:8 KJV - "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto Me."
devotionals.devotional:
Jesus said to her, 'Give Me a drink' (John 4:7). How many of us are expecting Jesus Christ to quench our thirst when we should be satisfying Him! We should be pouring out our lives, investing our total beings, not drawing on Him to satisfy us.

'You shall be witnesses to Me' (Acts 1:8). That means lives of pure, uncompromising, and unrestrained devotion to the Lord Jesus, which will be satisfying to Him wherever He may send us. Beware of anything that competes with your loyalty to Jesus Christ. The greatest competitor of true devotion to Jesus is the service we do for Him. It is easier to serve than to pour out our lives completely for Him.

The goal of the call of God is His satisfaction, not simply that we should do something for Him. We are not sent to do battle for God, but to be used by God in His battles. Are we more devoted to service than we are to Jesus Christ Himself?

Lesson: The greatest competitor to devotion to Jesus is often the service we do for Him. Never let service replace intimacy.

Action: Examine your heart today: Are you more devoted to doing things for God than to knowing God Himself? Repent and return to intimacy first.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I realise that I owe nothing to Your severity but all to Your love. Let Your love and gentleness and patience toward me be expressed through me to others.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 27:1 KJV - "The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?"
devotionals.devotional:
Have you ever wondered why it seems that the longer you remain in the dark, the clearer things become? It is awesome how God causes this to be so in the natural as well as in the spiritual. 'The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The Lord is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid'? The most spiritual insight are gained during times of deep despair. Not only will you learn how faithful God is, but how and why He orchestrates these situations.

Scripture clearly says: 'And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are called according to His purpose' (Romans 8:28). 'In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you' (1 Thessalonians 5:18). God is a loving and merciful Father, and everything we encounter in our lives is because of His love. It causes us to grab hold of Him, exercise our faith, and mature into vessels fit for His service.

Whenever you find yourself in the dark, do not be afraid. Remember this: 'Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path' (Psalm 119:105). God wants to use us to light the pathway for others in darkness so they can find their way to Him. Being in the dark is not a bad thing; it can be a time to grow in God, a time to learn to trust God, and a time to be thankful for all God has done for us.

Lesson: Dark times are not punishments but classrooms. In the dark, God gives you spiritual insight that you cannot gain any other way.

Action: Instead of complaining about your current difficulty, ask God: "What are You teaching me in this darkness?" Trust that He is preparing you for greater light.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, even in the dark, You are my light. Teach me what I can only learn in difficulty. Prepare me for greater service through this trial.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Proverbs 16:27 KJV - "An ungodly man diggeth up evil: and in his lips there is as a burning fire."
devotionals.devotional:
Arson is a senseless crime. It can cause loss of lives and property. Slander is a verbal arson. Lies about a person's character or actions are extremely destructive. They consume reputations and destroy relationships.

In Shakespeare's play Othello, the character Iago mapped out the damage slander does: Who steals my purse steals my trash; 'tis something, nothing. 'Twas mine, 'tis his, and has been slave to thousands. But he who filches from me my good name robs me of that which not enriches him and makes me poor indeed.

King Solomon warned that a scoundrel has evil 'on his lips like a burning fire' (Prov. 16:27). In contrast, he said that pleasant words are instructive and soothing, promoting spiritual health. When you are tempted to set a match to your brother's reputation with fiery words, stop! Ask God to help you speak words that build up instead of destroy. Don't be a verbal arsonist.

Lesson: Your words have the power to destroy reputations and relationships. Slander is verbal arson—it burns what you cannot rebuild.

Action: Before you speak about someone today, ask yourself: Are these words building up or burning down? Choose to be a builder, not an arsonist.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, set a watch over my mouth. Help me to speak words that build up, not words that burn down. Make me a healer of reputations, not a destroyer.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Romans 11:33 KJV - "O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are His judgments, and His ways past finding out!"
devotionals.devotional:
After Elijah had experienced some especially trying times, the Lord told him to flee to Zarephath where he could find food and shelter. Imagine Elijah's surprise when he discovered that the widow who was to provide for him was extremely poor! In fact, she expected that she and her son would soon die of starvation. How often God delights to astonish us by the wonder of His ways!

Our limited understanding of Him can be likened to a fly crawling on one of the pillars of a multi storied building. What does the tiny insect know about the architect's magnificent design? It sees only the little space of stone on which it moves. The beautiful carvings and ornamental work would seem like towering mountains and deep valleys that only impede the progress and obscure the view.

We as Christians often see only immediate circumstances and perceive but a glimmer of God's marvellous purpose. The obstacles that block our vision and get in the way of our plans are actually part of the beautiful designs of divine grace. Our heavenly Father knows exactly what He is doing. Although His ways are unsearchable, He assures us that all will work out for our good if we trust Him.

Lesson: God's ways often seem illogical to our limited understanding. But the obstacles you face may be the very things God is using to build something beautiful.

Action: Trust God even when you cannot trace Him. Thank Him today for the obstacles that are actually part of His beautiful design for your life.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I trust Your ways even when I do not understand them. Thank You that the obstacles in my path are part of Your beautiful design.

devotionals.memoryVerse: John 1:12 KJV - "But as many as received Him, to them gave He power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on His name."
devotionals.devotional:
The status update on facebook made me laugh. The man had written 'This usher will not let me sleep in my Father's house.' Two things struck my mind immediately – the story in Acts 20:9 of the young man whose sleep in his Father's house, like my friend wanted, resulted to his death and his assurance of knowing God as his Father and asserting his right in His house.

As Christians, many of us go to church and almost everyone claim to be a child of God but if you go to the street with the question, 'how do you know you are a child of God?' you will get as many diverse answers as the people you ask. We also revere church buildings and always refer to them as God's house. So when we are in the vicinity of a church, we always try to 'behave' ourselves so as not to offend God but if we truly have a personal knowledge of God as our Father, our view and outlook about church will be modified.

So long as we do not have this personal knowledge about God as our Father, we will always be 'slaves' or 'aliens' from Him. Having a personal knowledge of Him is only through the finished work of Jesus on the cross. If you open your heart to Him and accept Him as your Lord and saviour, then you can have that privilege of adoption as a son and become an heir of God. Which would you rather be?

Lesson: There is a difference between knowing about God and knowing God as Father. One makes you a slave; the other makes you a son.

Action: If you have never received Jesus as Lord, do so today. If you have, live today as a son, not a slave—boldly approaching your Father.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord Jesus, I accept You as my Lord and Saviour. Come into my heart, transform my life and give me the privilege of sonship.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Corinthians 2:9 KJV - "But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love Him."
devotionals.devotional:
We marvel at the various wonders of our world that God has created for us as our home in time. Though it is full of pain and evil, yet the earth is without doubt full of beautiful scenery that leaves us awestruck. Take a walk through a hooded brush in the early morning and watch the sun break out or in the wee-hours of the day and see the dusk set in. For all its beauty, it is but a veil of heaven's splendour.

Years ago, I had the opportunity to stand on the peak of Kainji dam and had a view of the surrounding scenery and the breath-catching rush of the water as it cascaded down the tunnel and the huge aquatic life the water supports. I was overwhelmed by the scenic view and the wonders of architectural technology. Yet still, it is but just a glimpse of heaven's glory.

Jesus assured us that He was returning to His Father to prepare a place for us and that He will return to take us to Himself, '... that where I am, there you may be also.' John 14:3. Have you ever imagined how glorious heaven will be? It will be a place of such splendour that no place on earth, no matter how beautiful, can compare with it!

Lesson: The most beautiful places on earth are only a dim reflection of the glory that awaits us in heaven. Keep your eyes on eternity.

Action: Are you ready for heaven? The only requirement is accepting and trusting Jesus as God's perfect sacrifice for your sins. Do that now.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Help me never to lose sight of heaven Lord, as I live my daily life.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Ephesians 4:32 KJV - "And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you."
devotionals.devotional:
'I am not on talking terms with him', she said. 'I've tried everything I could to get him to talk to me and have apologised several times to him but he still refuses to recognise my person.' This is a 'faithful' brother, who is always the first to come to church. She raved and cursed, was very abusive and challenged the other sister to come out for a fight outside the church. She refused to listen to anyone, shouted down those who asked her to forgive. This was a leader of women who had just said the closing prayer in church.

You, perhaps, may have experienced at least one of the above scenarios. It makes you wonder what type of Christianity we tend to profess these days. As Christians, we are allowed to be angry but not to sin, using our emotional state as an excuse. We are also enjoined to forgive one another and to use words that soothe the mind knowing that words can kill.

Being a Christian means to live a distinct lifestyle that will encourage our neighbours to follow after Jesus. Endeavour to live the Christ-like life that will win others over to Him.

Lesson: Your anger and unforgiveness are not excuses for un-Christlike behaviour. Live a life that makes others want to follow Jesus.

Action: Examine your relationships today. Is there anyone you have not forgiven? Choose forgiveness and let Christ's love flow through you.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I am sorry for living a life that does not reflect Your life. Help me henceforth to always live a life that will be pleasing to You.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Job 19:25 KJV - "For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that He shall stand at the latter day upon the earth."
devotionals.devotional:
How we understand God goes a long way to determine how we relate with Him as well as our fellow man. Obviously, biblical characters in the Old Testament had a deep knowledge of God. Our text today, especially our memory verse, remains one of the most challenging verses of the Bible to me. Can you imagine a man who physically had no hope of living till the next second saying that even after worms had destroyed his body, that in his flesh he will see God? What it implied was that Job was not expecting the sickness and disease that was ravaging his body to kill him. He believed this and told his friends so. Job finally did not die of the ailment that afflicted his body.

Job was able to trust God this much because he understood who God is and what God could do. Do you have a full knowledge of who God is? Do you believe that God can and will rescue, heal, and provide for you as well as take care of that challenge you are facing now? God has not disappointed anyone that believes and trusts in Him. He has always come to their salvation.

I want to assure you that if you can trust God and believe that He is bigger than all your problems and challenges, He will surely come to you as God, your redeemer.

Lesson: Your redeemer lives! No matter how hopeless your situation appears, God is bigger. Trust Him, and He will come to your rescue.

Action: Identify one hopeless situation you are facing. Declare aloud: "My Redeemer lives!" and trust Him to act on your behalf.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Dear God, even in the midst of my hopeless situation, I am looking up to You and trusting You for my salvation.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Matthew 6:5 KJV - "And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward."
devotionals.devotional:
I was in the church and overheard the prayers of two persons. A young lady knelt in the last pew and with tears cascading her face, she confessed her wrong doings to the Lord. She was indifferent if anyone overheard her or not. Hearing her, you could discern her brokenness and anguish. I am not God but my heart went out to her. I felt like picking her up and wiping her tears. At the other end, towards the altar, a man stood praying. He was conscious of his environment and mouthed appropriate words, seemingly to protect his reputation. With this experience, I fully understood what Jesus meant in this parable.

How do you approach God in prayers? Is it a routine stuff that you do to fulfil all righteousness or a period when you communicate with God with no holds barred? Do you pray as if your life is dependent on it or do you apply prayer as a cosmetic so people will see you as being prayerful? It is said that a prayerless Christian is a powerless Christian. If Jesus, who is God, still spent time in prayer, how much more do you think you can make it if you neglect to seek God's face in prayers?

It is important to know that we are not justified before God by our acts of righteousness but through the finished work of the cross. When we come before Him, let us learn to humble ourselves and communicate with Him in all seriousness. Do not use prayer as a cosmetic to dress yourself.

Lesson: God despises cosmetic prayers—prayers offered to impress men rather than to connect with God. Pray in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.

Action: Find a private place today. Pray with brokenness and honesty, not caring who hears or sees. Let your prayer be between you and God alone.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, forgive my pride and haughtiness when I pray. May I receive refreshing and justification in Your presence today. Amen.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Proverbs 31:30 KJV - "Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised."
devotionals.devotional:
Each time I read the story of Esther, I am struck by God's wonderful provisioning for His people. This is because, by Divine providence, Vashti was dropped as the queen for doing the right thing – upholding the dignity of womanhood by refusing to display her nakedness to drunken ministers of state. I often wonder what would have happened had she obliged the king's request. I guess she would have still being dropped for the act when the euphoria of drunkenness had abated from the king.

Let us take a look at Esther's preparedness for the office. We read that she was an orphan, lovely and beautiful but still a virgin and above all humble, homely, obedient, intelligent and God-fearing. I begin to wonder if such a person can exist in the morally decadent society of ours today. How many of our beautiful girls and handsome young men can boast of retaining their virginity, piety and cool-headedness? Had Esther not possessed these qualities, she would not have being enthroned as queen.

As a Christian, your character is supposed to stand you out among the crowd. Don't be carried away by your status, physical attributes or attainment or allow yourself to be influenced by the negative lifestyle that is prevalent in our society today. Irrespective of societal pressure, maintain a godly character. This will get you prepared for the exalted office God is preparing for you.

Lesson: Your character, not just your credentials, prepares you for promotion. God uses people of godly character, not just gifted people.

Action: Identify one area of character you need to develop. Commit to working on it this week, asking God to shape you into a vessel He can use.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, help me retain the qualities of Christ in my life and stand out among the crowd.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Revelation 2:10 KJV - "Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life."
devotionals.devotional:
Tears misted my eyes. My heart was heavy and pounding as I read the story. How can people be this heartless? A man died after a long drawn battle with an illness that drained the family resources. In the evening of the day he was buried, his siblings ganged up against the wife, who was nursing a baby, and beat her up because she refused to follow the tradition of shaving her head for the dead and going into seclusion for 28 days, which she explained her faith forbids. The baby died and the woman died some days later from the injuries she sustained. The three little surviving children were thrown out of the family house.

St. Peter warned us to 'Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil walks about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour. Resist him steadfast in the faith, knowing that the same sufferings are experienced by your brotherhood in the world.' 1 Peter 5:8-9. The afflictions and troubles we pass through in life are some of the theatrics the devil employs to get us distracted so that he can easily win us. We need to be watchful and prayerful and endeavour to entrust everything to our Lord Jesus.

Though some situations can be really upsetting and demanding like the temptations of Job, but if you determine to look up to God and never waver, He will see you through.

Lesson: The enemy uses trials to distract you and make you lose focus. Stay watchful, prayerful, and fixed on Jesus.

Action: Identify a current trial that is distracting you from God. Deliberately set your eyes back on Jesus today and refuse to be moved.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, help me to stand firm and be focussed, no matter the temptations the devil brings my way today. Amen.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Philippians 4:19 KJV - "But my God shall supply all your need according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus."
devotionals.devotional:
In almost all religious forums today, we are compelled to give. We are promised a well of divine blessings if we do. All sort of antics and mantra are employed to get us to part with our hard-earned resources. Miracles, breakthrough, success and the like are only for those who give. Different bible verses are quoted to brainwash us into giving all we have. Prosperity prayers, good visions and prophecies are exclusively reserved for those who donate large sums of money 'willingly'. Many have stolen or have committed heinous crimes in order to give and receive blessings.

The abuse of the opportunity to serve the Lord with our resources have made many of us indifferent to such calls and preachers, especially when the preachers are living in affluence and the bulk of their followers are struggling to eke out a living. The media is awash with reports of pastors who are living big at the expense of their congregants, who are always compelled to give with promises of divine blessings that never come while many have given themselves into penury.

Are we to shy away from this divine mandate because of these reasons? The answer is no. There are still so many who are genuinely in need of help. Liberality is enshrined in scripture and a lot of promises-blessings go with it. Apostle Paul prayed for the Philippian church in our text for God to supply all their need because they gave to him. However, he did not have to depend on them for his livelihood.

Lesson: True liberality is not about being manipulated into giving but about genuinely helping those in need. Ask God for discernment to know where to sow your seeds.

Action: Identify one genuine need today and give cheerfully, trusting God to supply your own needs in return.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord give me the discerning heart and the grace to help someone in need today.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Revelation 12:11 KJV - "And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death."
devotionals.devotional:
Whenever the word 'confession' is used, we often think of confession of sins, weaknesses and failures. This is not always so. Confession here implies saying what God has said in His word about certain things. It is agreeing with God, saying the same thing scriptures say. 'Therefore hold fast your confession...' according to our text, is to say what God has said until the thing desired in your heart and promised in His word is fully manifested.

Many times, we fail when things become difficult because we have lost our confession. When things are going very well, our confession is very strong, vigorous and clear but when the storms and testing comes, we give up our testimonies forgetting that '...they overcame him ... by the word of their testimony.' When we confess diseases, weaknesses and failures, we magnify the adversary above the Father and destroy our confidence in the word of God.

The big question is how much of the word of God do you know? You cannot confess what you do not know. It is what you know personally about Jesus Christ that counts. Remember that there is no faith without confession. Our faith can never grow beyond our confession. We will never enjoy the riches of God's grace until we confess them.

Lesson: Your confession shapes your reality. Stop confessing your problems and start confessing God's promises. You overcome by the word of your testimony.

Action: Write down three promises from God's Word. Confess them aloud every morning this week, and watch your faith grow.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, help me to confess Your Word, not my fears. My help comes from You. You keep me in perfect peace. The Lord is my Shepherd; I shall not want.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Lamentations 3:22-23 KJV - "It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is Thy faithfulness."
devotionals.devotional:
Parents expect their children to do things according to their instruction but most times, we discover that children still do things just as they wish. Our children discourage us sometimes with their actions and attitude by doing things that will not benefit them. Sometimes we threaten not to buy them new clothes or even pay their school fees just to make them understand that it is not good to disobey us. But these end up being empty threats because we know that if we fail to train or take good care of our children, they may end up becoming nuisance to the society.

In Lamentations 3:22, Prophet Jeremiah tells us that God's unfailing love never ends. We know that our being alive today is because God abundantly showers us with His mercies. Jeremiah also told us that God's faithfulness to us is new every morning. God can never change. Whatever promise He made to us, He is able to do no matter how long it takes. When we wait, seek and trust Him, He will show us His salvation.

Jeremiah continued to tell us that now that we are still young (alive), we should submit ourselves to God in accordance to His words because no matter the challenges we face today, God will not abandon us forever. Finally, even if our present circumstances try to make us think that God brings grief, just know that God will also show us His compassion according to the greatness of His unfailing Love. Always remember that God is an ever faithful God.

Lesson: God's faithfulness is new every morning. No matter what happened yesterday, today His mercies are fresh and His promises still stand.

Action: Thank God today for one specific way He has been faithful to you this week. Write it down as a reminder for difficult days.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Help me Lord to always believe and trust You.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 37:4 KJV - "Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart."
devotionals.devotional:
The traditional head of an African village sent his son to Europe to further his studies. While there, he fell in love with a lady from his country but from another tribe. They got married, despite their parent's objection, and had a son. When they returned after their studies, the lady and her son were rejected by her husband's family and were ostracised from the village. She went to live in the city with her son while the man remarried and was crowned the traditional head of the village when his father passed on.

Several years later, the boy went to a camping trip with his friends and got lost. A massive search for him began. After many twists and turns, the boy ended up in his father's village. It happened that her husband had died but could not be buried because the heir apparent must see the body last. The boy, in his wanderings, came upon the open casket, closed it and called for burial. The bewildered villagers crowned the estranged child as the traditional head of the village.

Similarly, Jephthah's family and community rejected him but difficult circumstances forced them to go back to him for reconciliation and they made him their head. You shall attain whatever God has destined for you. No plans to abort it shall succeed. Are you facing rejection or suffering estrangement? Don't despair; don't give up. God will navigate you back on course and your people will return to appreciate you. Keep faith!

Lesson: Rejection is not the end of your story. God can turn the same people who rejected you into those who celebrate you. Keep faith!

Action: If you are facing rejection today, do not despair. Declare that God will navigate you back on course. Keep believing.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Are you facing rejection or suffering estrangement? Receive grace to keep the faith.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Exodus 15:11 KJV - "Who is like unto Thee, O LORD, among the gods? who is like Thee, glorious in holiness, fearful in praises, doing wonders?"
devotionals.devotional:
Life is not a bed of roses. We face diverse challenges and difficulties in it. Sometimes it seems as if we have gotten to the end of the road. We may have fasted and prayed and still fail to get the needed results. Being in a dilemma and confused, we wonder if God is still there. Jehoshaphat faced such a dark situation but rather than give up, and being encouraged by the man of God, praised God. Praising God, especially during dark moments of life, does not come easy. It takes a disciplined, determined effort to do so.

In Exodus 15:11, God is described as being fearful in praises. When we praise Him, He does fearful things that people will hear and wonder the possibility of such happening. The ancient wall of Jericho crashed down and God's people had victory as a result of a shout of praise (Joshua 6:1-21). The prison doors shook open when Paul and Silas praised God (Acts 16:25-26).

Praise is what we offer in acknowledgement of God's excellent being. It is offered to God for who He is. It can be expressed through songs, hymns and in prayers and it is to be done continuously. As we cultivate the habit of praising, we are guaranteed of God's presence in our life every day.

Lesson: When you don't know what else to do, praise. God inhabits the praises of His people, and in His presence, problems dissolve.

Action: In your next difficult moment, instead of complaining or panicking, start praising. Let praises go first, and watch God move.
devotionals.prayerConfession: "I will praise You Lord in every situation."

devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Corinthians 12:9 KJV - "My grace is sufficient for thee: for My strength is made perfect in weakness."
devotionals.devotional:
While addressing us during the send off party organised for us when I passed out of Secondary School, one of my teachers said "the bible says we should resist the devil and he will flee but when it comes to our libidinous emotions, it says we should flee, not resist, because He who put the feelings there know how powerful the urge is. Had Joseph not fled, he will invariably have fallen to his mistress' lure."

Some of us battle with emotions and urges we may not be bold enough to disclose. It may not be nymphomania but it can be anything not dignifying the name of Christ that we bear such as gluttony, kleptomania, drunkenness, lying, anger, unforgiveness, wealth craze, etc. We may have prayed often times for God to take it away and may have applied all the necessary steps we may have been counselled to apply without success.

Do not be consumed with self-guilt or give up. You are not in the battle alone. Jesus experienced it too but He never sinned – Hebrews 4:15. It is a vicious hold by the devil to stake a claim in your life but the power in the name of Jesus can break it. Totally submit to His Lordship over your life and receive grace to overcome as He did. Whenever the urge comes, tell yourself that "God's grace is sufficient for me and His strength is made perfect in my weakness!" You will overcome!

Lesson: Your weakness is not a reason for despair; it is an opportunity for God's strength to be displayed. His grace is sufficient.

Action: Identify one recurring weakness. Instead of fighting it in your own strength, surrender it to God and declare His grace sufficient over that area today.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, grant me Your grace and strength to overcome this weakness of my body. I cannot do it on my own. Help me to live a victorious life always in Jesus' name.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Habakkuk 2:3 KJV - "For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry."
devotionals.devotional:
As the choir were about to sing in church one day, the leader asked if there is anything God cannot do. While the congregation thundered a resounding "no!", I shrilly shouted "yes!". To those who looked at me in amazement, I explained that God cannot lie. God promised Abraham, an old man well over 75 years of age and whose wife was over 65 years, of seeing a child. This promise was absurd because the man and his wife were past the reproductive age. I suppose Abraham could have reasoned "but God, why did You not do this all these past years we were virile?" but he did not do this, rather he believed God.

To make matters worse, the fulfilment of this promise took another 25 years! By this time, they had taken such talk in their stride and were no longer looking forward to it. They laughed over it (Genesis 18:10-15) because it just was no longer "scientifically, humanly or naturally" possible but God kept His word - (Genesis 21:1-2).

What did God promise you? The events around you are dictating otherwise or the promise has taken too long to be fulfilled and you have come to the stage where you laugh it off? You believed God until people made a mockery of your belief and faith? Never mind them and never give up. God cannot lie and even though the fulfilment of His promise to you tarries, yet wait for it. He will surely visit you and fulfil His promise to you.

Lesson: God cannot lie. What He has promised, He will fulfill—even if it takes longer than you expect. Don't give up.

Action: Write down one promise from God that you are still waiting for. Thank Him today that He cannot lie and that promise will surely come to pass.
devotionals.prayerConfession: "Lord, I believe Your words and promises. Help my unbelief!"

devotionals.memoryVerse: Hebrews 13:15 KJV - "By Him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to His name."
devotionals.devotional:
Have you ever been in difficulty and you were asked to praise God? It rather seems absurd and is most difficult to do so, especially when we have prayed out our hearts without results. Take a look at it this way: prayer is a request, a petition. If you go to someone with a request, he-she will consider the request on its merit and may turn it down but if you go to the same person with flattering praise, he-she will respond to your request.

Also consider this: Jesus said if we pray with faith and don't doubt, we can command a mountain to move to the sea and it will obey us (Matthew 21:21). That is, we are shifting the problem through time and space but have not solved the problem but when we praise, God inhabits our praises (Psalm 22:3) and in His presence, mountains melt like wax (Psalm 97:5)! We are commanded to come before God's presence with singing and into His courts with praise (Psalm 100:4) and to pray with thanksgiving (Philippians 4:6).

Scripture records a number of outstanding miracles which took place when praises took the place of prayers such as the felling of the wall of Jericho (Joshua 6:20); Jehoshaphat's victory in war (2 Chronicles 20:22); Paul and Silas' deliverance from prison (Acts 16:25-26). It is said that prayers move mountains but praises move God. Whenever you pray, garnish your prayers with praise.

Lesson: Prayer moves mountains, but praise moves God. When you have prayed without results, shift from petition to praise.

Action: In your next prayer time, spend the first half purely in praise—no requests, just adoration. Watch how the atmosphere changes.
devotionals.prayerConfession: "O Lord, open my lips and my mouth shall show forth Your praise." Psalm 51:15.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Isaiah 43:2 KJV - "When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee."
devotionals.devotional:
Can you imagine a baby abandoned all to itself, crying its heart out and the mother sitting close by but snoring away? "Impossible!" you said? A mother's winsome attitude, care and love for her young ones have endeared her to hearts. Many musicians have sung songs extolling this wonder of "mama's love" which is quite incomparable. In our text today, God also compared His love and care for us to "mama's love" and promised that even if a mother can forget and overlook her tender, wailing child, yet He cannot forget us.

To engrave means "to cut, carve or etch into a hard surface." This implies that anything engraved on a surface is indelible. God declared that He has engraved us on His palms. As such, our lives have been insured by Him. If this is so, what flood of insecurities released against us by the kingdom of darkness can swallow us? Since we are under God's protective custody, we have no need to fear because whatever God does not permit cannot happen in our lives.

When we are faced with difficulties, we may feel that God has forgotten us and has left us to our woes. God never promised us a trouble-free life but the bible is replete with His promises to be with us through all trouble and deliver us from same. He promised to restore to us all we may have lost. With that difficulty, God is passing you through the furnace of purification, to remove the dross and announce your greatness. When you emerge, you will be better and fitter to occupy the position God has destined for you.

Lesson: Even if a mother could forget her child, God cannot forget you. You are engraved on His palms. Your difficulty is not abandonment; it is preparation.

Action: Thank God today that He has not forgotten you. Trust that He is using your current challenge to prepare you for greater things.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Thank You Lord for the assurance of Your restoration in my life. Amen.

devotionals.memoryVerse: John 13:34 KJV - "A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another."
devotionals.devotional:
The parable of the Good Samaritan teaches us that true love is not measured by words or feelings but by action. The priest and the Levite saw the wounded man and passed by on the other side. They had religious knowledge but no compassionate action. But the Samaritan, the one least expected to show love, was moved with compassion and took action. He bound up the man's wounds, took him to an inn, and paid for his care.

True love expressed is costly. It requires time, resources, and sometimes inconvenience. The Samaritan did not just feel sorry; he sacrificed his own comfort and resources to help someone in need. This is the kind of love Jesus commands us to have—not just for our friends and family but for our neighbours, including those who are different from us or even considered enemies.

How are you expressing love to those around you? Are you passing by on the other side when you see someone in need? Are you only loving those who can love you back? True love expressed is the evidence of a heart transformed by God's love. Go and do likewise.

Lesson: Love is not a feeling; it is an action. True love expressed costs something and often goes to those who cannot repay you.

Action: Identify one person in need today—practical, emotional, or spiritual need. Take a concrete action to express love to them, even if it costs you.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, teach me to love not just in word but in deed and truth. Help me to be a Good Samaritan to those in need around me.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Proverbs 1:10 KJV - "My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not."
devotionals.devotional:
I answered the phone. The caller identified himself as a businessman from Pretoria. He was trying to locate a contact and was given my number by the Nigerian embassy who said that I am the only Nigerian who will tell him the truth. I was miffed and told him off but he assured me he was not dubious. On his sixth call, I became fed up with his insistence and lied that I had located the man. He replied "I am disappointed. They told me you are an honest person who I can trust but now I don't know who to trust in Nigeria!"

Several months later, I ran into a friend who expressed extreme disappointment with me on the issue and said the call was for real, that he gave an international company my details and assured them I was someone they could rely on. When I narrated how the man pressurised me into giving him that false response, he replied "I thought you are a bible-man. You were to be tried seven times but you failed on the sixth."

Samson was pressurised into telling the answer to his puzzle. It is ironic that he did not learn from that experience and when Delilah pressurised him later, he also revealed the secret of his strength. This led to his death. How do you resist pressure? Even if it is pressure to sin, how you go about it determines your success or failure. Integrity demands that you stay on the course of truth.

Lesson: Pressure reveals what is really inside you. Repeated pressure is a test of character. Don't give in—stay true to your integrity.

Action: Identify one area where you feel pressured to compromise. Decide today that you will not give in, no matter how many times you are pressed.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, help me never to succumb to the pressures of life and sin against You.

devotionals.topic: What to Do in the Middle of a Storm
devotionals.memoryVerse: Matthew 14:30 KJV - "But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me."
devotionals.devotional:
When you are going through a storm, God is not distant or uninvolved. He is "I Am" and He is working in your life for your good. But there are some things He wants you to do. First, have courage because Jesus is with you. Don't ever argue with a fear. Just tell it where to go! Tell it to go talk to Jesus. Second, take a risk in faith. Don't ask God to bless what you are doing. Do what God is blessing. Stay focused on Jesus. The moment you take your eyes off the Lord, you will go under.

When you focus on the wind and the waves – your circumstances – you are going to sink, just like Peter. If you look at the world, you will be distressed. If you look within, you will be depressed. If you look at Christ, you will be at rest. Third, don't doubt. You don't need great faith to make it through the storm in your life. You just need faith in the right person. Fourth, praise God! Even in the storm, even when you feel like you are sinking, even when you are scared to death, praise Him all the time. Thank God in the middle of the storm.

Why do you think God is letting you go through this storm? He is letting you go through this storm to say, "I'm all you need. I can handle anything. I will come to you walking on the very thing that scares you the most. You need to stop being afraid, and you need to totally trust Me in faith."

Lesson: Storms are not signs of God's absence but opportunities for His presence to be revealed. Keep your eyes on Jesus, not on the waves.

Action: In your current storm, stop looking at the circumstances. Fix your eyes on Jesus, praise Him, and take a step of faith today.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, help me to trust You totally to see me through this storm.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 50:15 KJV - "Call upon Me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify Me."
devotionals.devotional:
The book of Job tells of the woes Job faced. He lost everything he had in a day. This was too much for him to bear so he became mad at God. He thought it was God who brought the entire calamity to him. Have you ever been mad at God? Most of us have because, in a sense, at times, when we lose the light to our path, we, like Job, lose all that we feel we have laboured for. In days like these we look at God in the face and ask Him questions we would not dare to ask our President. At times like this we are mad at God.

Being mad at God will not solve any problems for you, it will only compound them. He is too big to be figured out and that is why He is God. There is no instruction found in the Bible that encourages us to be angry at God. The object of our anger should never be God, it should be Satan. God requires worship from us not unnecessary questions. To be angry at God is really ridiculous. It is like kicking against a rock. You falsely accuse God for your predicaments. This is absolutely wrong. God does not cause evil and cannot be accused of it.

The prescription God has given to us is to "call upon Me, in the time of trouble and I will deliver you." Instead of getting angry at God, why not genuinely call upon Him today in faith hoping that in His nature He will answer you?

Lesson: Anger at God is misplaced. God is not your enemy; the devil is. Call upon God in your trouble; He promises to deliver you.

Action: If you have been angry at God, repent. Turn that anger into prayer. Call upon Him today and trust Him to deliver.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, forgive me for being so arrogant and rude towards You. I ask that You remember me in this time and rescue me in Jesus' name. Amen.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Mark 5:36 KJV - "Be not afraid, only believe."
devotionals.devotional:
Life is full of challenges, worries and problems. They are so complex and perplexing and tend to overwhelm us. We are often exasperated, seeking for a solution. How do we come out of the problems we are in? How do we weather the storm? We fast and pray, sow seeds, go to "renowned and acclaimed men of God" all to no avail. Our family, friends and neighbours may then advice us to let go, "... you have tried, this is how God wants it." Failing to see a solution in the horizon, we may give up.

Jairus faced such a monumental challenge. His little daughter was very sick and "lies at the point of death." He besought the Master for help and earnestly prayed but before Jesus could respond, news came that the little girl has passed on and he should let the Master be. Jairus was completely devastated. Note who Jairus was: a ruler of the synagogue, that is, a pastor. Problems and difficulties do not mind our personality or our spirituality. In fact, the higher our level of spirituality, the more complex challenges we face.

But just as Jesus encouraged Jairus, so He speaks to us today not to lose hope and give up but to believe. Though the matter may have gone out of hand and may have lost life, keep looking up for the Master is coming with life in His hands.

Lesson: Just when it seems too late, Jesus shows up. Don't let bad news make you give up. Keep believing; the Master is on His way.

Action: Is there a situation where you have been tempted to give up? Hear Jesus say to you today: "Be not afraid, only believe." Keep trusting.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Help me Lord to continue trusting, no matter how rough the ride may have become.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Jeremiah 29:11 KJV - "For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end."
devotionals.devotional:
Jeremiah prophesied about the release of the children of Israel from captivity in Babylon. God's people had sinned and were carried away to Babylon. The situation seemed hopeless but God had other plans. His plans were plans of good and not of evil to give the Hebrews an expected end. This He assured them through His prophet Jeremiah.

You may be in a form of captivity. At this point, it may be too complex that you cannot boast of any plan or line of action to get out of the challenge. However, the word of the Lord is that your captivity will not last forever. Even if you have exhausted your escape plans, God who is never confused has a plan for you. He has declared the end from the beginning and assuredly, He has a plan to see you through the hurdles you face. Your responsibility is to hold on until He comes to your rescue. Weeping may endure for the night but joy definitely comes in the morning.

What are God's plans for your life? What has He told you about your situation? You may well keep it in mind and watch out for its manifestation because heaven and earth will pass away but God's word will remain.

Lesson: God has a plan for your life—a plan of peace, not evil, to give you a future and a hope. Your captivity is temporary.

Action: Write down Jeremiah 29:11 today. Meditate on it. Trust that God's plan for you is good, even when circumstances suggest otherwise.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Oh Lord teach me how to keep my eyes on the promises You have made to me until I see their manifestation.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Romans 8:14 KJV - "For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God."
devotionals.devotional:
Several women claimed to have been put in the family way by late M. K. O. Abiola and many children were born to him. Though he accepted all and took charge of their welfare, yet before his death, he added a clause to his will that only those who were medically proven to be his children will partake in his estate. Many of those that claimed to be his children were not sired by him.

Similarly today, so many people claim to be God's children. They can quote several bible passages and tell you categorically that they are born again. They go to church regularly and are active in their local assembly. They may even ream off various scriptural texts to you and can pray and prophesy but when you x-ray their lives in the light of God's word, you really begin to wonder.

Our bible text today tells us the attributes of God's children: They live not according to the flesh. By the enabling power of the Holy Spirit, they put to death the deeds of the flesh. They are led by the Spirit of God. They received the Spirit of adoption to call God "Abba Father!" The Holy Spirit bears witness with their spirit that they are children of God. They are joint heirs with Christ. They suffer with Christ and will be glorified with Him.

Lesson: Being a child of God is not about claiming it but about being led by the Spirit. The Holy Spirit bears witness with your spirit.

Action: Examine your life against the attributes in Romans 8. Ask the Holy Spirit to give you the assurance of sonship and to lead you daily.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord Jesus, I'm sorry for all my sins. I know You died to redeem me. Wash me with Your blood. Come into my heart; be my Lord and my Saviour and give me the power to live a righteous life from now. Amen.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Romans 1:16 KJV - "For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth."
devotionals.devotional:
The word of God in your mouth has inherent power to produce what it says. When spoken with the boldness of the Holy Spirit, things change. In Acts 4:31, the Apostles, filled with the Holy Ghost, spoke the word with boldness. Peter's words were so impregnated with Divine energy that it pricked the hearts of his audience and three thousand of them yielded to the gospel.

Never be timid about the word. Declare it at all times with boldness. Be bold to say what God has said in His word. Do not be intimidated by any audience or circumstance. The power to heal, deliver and save is impregnated in the word. The power to turn hopeless situations around is in the word. With the enabling grace of the Holy Spirit, we can win our world for Christ if we declare His word with all boldness.

You can also speak into your life with the word. Be bold to say what God has said about you in His word. Speak boldly in consonance with the word, declaring that you are a product of the word. You live and move and have your being in Christ. You reign with Him in the realms of glory. You are victorious over death, hell and the grave. Make bold confessions over your life today. Remember that the word of God in your mouth is what produces result. Speak to yourself and your situation will change.

Lesson: The word of God in your mouth has power. Speak it boldly—not timidly—and watch things change.

Action: Identify three promises from God's Word. Speak them aloud with boldness today, refusing to be intimidated.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, give me the enabling grace to declare Your word with all boldness today.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Mark 14:9 KJV - "Verily I say unto you, Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached throughout the whole world, this also that she hath done shall be spoken of for a memorial of her."
devotionals.devotional:
One thing that encourages the heart of leaders is when they are honoured. I have discovered that people tend to think that leaders do not need to be honoured with gifts because it is assumed that they have all they need. But we fail to know that leaders are just like any of us. Jesus found himself in this position when He was with His disciples. The disciples were more concerned about their own needs that they forgot that Jesus Christ, their leader, has needs too. Even when Mary Magdalene showed Him some honour by pouring the keg of alabaster oil on Him, His followers considered it a waste.

The greatest sign of love you can show to anyone is to honour him-her. As you go out to your place of business, school, office or workplace, try and show honour to your boss or leader with a pleasant and surprising gift. Maybe an encouraging text message, a flower or anything you can afford. No matter how little, it might be the touch he-she needs to have a very good day.

Always remember that our honour is embedded in the honour we show to someone else. Mary Magdalene is remembered today because she honoured the Lord. That little act of honour which she showed Jesus Christ was enough to make her to be remembered anytime Jesus Christ is mentioned.

Lesson: Honour is not about the size of the gift but the size of the heart behind it. Your act of honour could be remembered forever.

Action: Identify one person today who deserves honour—a parent, a leader, a teacher, or a mentor. Show them honour in a tangible way.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, help me to honour someone today.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 150:6 KJV - "Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD. Praise ye the LORD."
devotionals.devotional:
Have you ever witnessed a masquerade dancing to the rhythm of its praise by a praise singer or a man of means or in a position of authority doing the unheard of when being praised? What about you – have anyone praised you for an effort or for flattery? How did you feel? Having these scenarios in mind, how do you think God will feel when we erupt in spontaneous praises to Him? Praise means to commend, applaud or magnify. To God, this is done when we humble ourselves and centre our attention on Him with heartfelt expressions of love, adoration, thanksgiving, worship, lifting up and glorifying Him.

Praise elevates us into God's presence and causes Him to manifest His power on our behalf. It is a vehicle to enter into His presence. God craves our praise and worship to Him and commands us to praise Him, even in our darkest hour. In the scriptures, David won God's heart because He was a man of praise. God fought for Israel when they went to fight a war with an "army" of praise-singers (2 Chronicles 20:21-22). He delivered Paul and Silas from prison and possible death because of their praises (Acts 16:25-26).
