Are you facing a difficulty and have prayed without success? Why not try praise?

Lesson: Prayer moves the hand of God, but praise moves God Himself. When you don't know what else to do, praise.

Action: Set aside five minutes right now to do nothing but praise God. No requests, no complaints—just praise.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Reflection: Prayer moves the hand of God but praises move God! Which would you rather do?

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Thessalonians 5:18 KJV - "In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you."
devotionals.devotional:
God wants us to be intentional about our thankfulness every day. He wants us to develop this spiritual habit, one that is reflected in the life of a radical believer. The truth is that the more deeply you understand God's love, the more grateful you are going to be. In all circumstances give thanks because it is God's will for you.

It is a lot easier to give thanks when everything is going on fine, when you just received a cheque or received a gift. It is however harder to say "thank you" when everything is not going on well. However, the scripture requires us to give thanks in all things. You can thank God in every circumstance because God is in control. He can bring good out of evil. He can turn around the stupid mistakes you made. No matter what happens, God is not going to stop loving you. There are a hundred things to be thankful for in any circumstance, even when the circumstance stinks.

Being thankful in all circumstances is God's will because it creates fellowship. Gratitude always builds deeper relationships between you and other people and between you and God. Whoever you want to get closer to, start expressing gratitude to that person. As you develop an attitude of gratitude, you will see changes in your life and relationships.

Lesson: Gratitude is not a feeling; it is a command. Give thanks in everything—not for everything, but in everything—because God is with you in it.

Action: Write down three things you are grateful for today, even if your circumstances are difficult. Thank God specifically for each one.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, help me to develop the spirit of gratitude and learn to give You thanks always.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Isaiah 40:29 KJV - "He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might He increaseth strength."
devotionals.devotional:
I had to make use of Google translator to find the Hebrew word for "The Lord our Strength" and it gave me two words - Jehovah Chayil and Jehovah T'Sur. Chayil was explained to mean the strength of an army or persons and I found it too humiliating to use for God so I went with T'Sur. Our God cannot be described as Jehovah Chayil because even the most elite forces are overwhelmed and call for reinforcement but our God never grows weary!

The strength of man is finite. Even when doing things we enjoy, we still get tired and grow weak after some time and would need some rest to get resuscitated. We need good food and a good sleep to get the most from our body and this, even with the most arduous training at the peak of youth, lasts only a few hours but our God is infinitely strong and powerful. He never sleeps neither does He need rest to regain strength.

Life can be an arduous journey at times and just like Elijah, we may give in to despondency. At such times, it is comforting to know that our God who never grows weary is ever ready to replenish our strength to forge on. Knowing our frailty and the limits of our ability, He promised never to let what we cannot handle befall us and even when we face such arduous difficulties, to make a way of escape. When swimming through the murky waters of despair, remember Jehovah T'Sur!

Lesson: Your strength will fail, but God's strength never will. He is Jehovah T'Sur—the Lord your Strength—ready to replenish you.

Action: When you feel weak or weary today, stop relying on your own strength. Call upon Jehovah T'Sur and receive His supernatural strength.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Give me strength for everyday, Lord, imputing Your strength to me in my weakness.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Matthew 25:13 KJV - "Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh."
devotionals.devotional:
Do you love weddings – the beauty and the fun of it? Have you wedded or been part of a bridal train? If no, you must have had a very close family member who wedded which you were part of the preparation. Did you notice the frenzy, euphoria, anticipation and insomnia that went with it? Oh, weddings are beautiful and signify the beginning of another phase of life, especially for the bride and groom. I simply love them.

Jewish marriages were often contracted at night. The ten virgins made up the bridal train waiting for the arrival of the groom and his entourage. They were expected to conduct them in with fanfare and with lamps lighting up the way. However, for inexplicable reasons, the groom and his entourage delayed in coming and after a very tedious day of preparation, the bride and her train collapsed to tiredness and slept. Five were prepared for any eventuality and came with extra oil while the other five did not.

This tells the state of the church who is Christ's bride. As it seems that the promise of His return is being delayed, so many of us have fallen asleep, that is, we have lost our first love and commitment and our lamps have gone out. Note also the time of His coming – at midnight – when we least expect Him to come. However the clarion call is being made now, so loud and clear: Wake up! Behold Him coming! Trim up your lamp, add more oil, and be ready to receive Him.

Lesson: The bridegroom is coming. Don't be caught asleep and unprepared. Wake up, trim your lamp, and add the oil of the Holy Spirit.

Action: Examine your spiritual readiness today. Have you lost your first love? Repent, wake up, and prepare for His coming.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, help me to wake up from my spiritual slumber and be ready for Your coming.

devotionals.topic: In Such a Time as This
devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Corinthians 3:5 KJV - "Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God."
devotionals.devotional:
Our text contains one of the most profound statements in the book of Esther. Mordecai, Esther's uncle, brings a new dimension to the royalty of Esther into the picture. At a time like that, with the crisis the Jews faced, God had already positioned Esther to be the solution her people would need to solve their problem. Her task was to stand and deliver her people but she did not realise this at first, until her uncle pointed it out to her.

The question to ask is "why am I living in such a time as this?" If you look around you, you will notice a certain degree of abnormality in your family, the church and in the society. Can you do anything about the said abnormalities? Has God equipped you in any way to solve the problems that face your family in such a time as this? Do you realise that the destiny of an entire race could be dependent on your single action? Have you thought about the consequences of you keeping quiet in such a time as this?

Every day, in various degrees, life brings all manner of challenges our way, which are really opportunities to glorify God. Just like Esther, we are required to take the bull by the horn and seek to proffer solutions to the challenges we have around us, for that is why God created us and placed us where we are in such a time as this. Do not hesitate to do what you have been called to do. Take responsibility; take action; make that move and watch God come to the rescue of a people through you.

Lesson: You are not where you are by accident. God positioned you for such a time as this. Don't keep quiet; take responsibility and act.

Action: Identify one problem in your sphere of influence that you have been ignoring. Take one step today toward being part of the solution.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Oh Lord forgive me for not taking responsibility where I am meant to take responsibility. Grant me boldness to do all I should do to bring glory to Your name.

devotionals.memoryVerse: James 4:7 KJV - "Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you."
devotionals.devotional:
I read the story of Daisy sometime ago. She was caught in a web of spiritual conflict and suffered from demonic influences. She was a Christian and a university graduate but she had severe mental and emotional problems which developed after her parents divorced. Within a period of five years, Daisy had been institutionalised three times as a paranoid schizophrenic. She did not have the nerve to report the nocturnal visits of snakes that crawl on her when she lies in bed.

The counsellor did a good thing for Daisy, as he was a fine, Christian psychologist. He suggested "Why don't you try something different? When you're in bed and the snakes come, say loudly, 'In the name of Christ, I command you to leave me!'" Daisy retorted "I can't do that; I'm not mature or strong enough." What Daisy did not know was that it was not a matter of her maturity rather it's a matter of her position in Christ. You have as much right to resist Satan as any other Christian does.

Apostle James wrote "Resist the devil and he will flee from you" but if you do not resist him, he will not go. If you pull the covers over your head in fear and expect God to do something about the demonic influences, the evil spirits will not leave. Resisting the devil is your responsibility based on the authority you possess in Christ.

Lesson: Your authority over the enemy is not based on your maturity or strength but on your position in Christ. Resist the devil—he must flee.

Action: If you have been living in fear of the enemy, today take your authority. Speak directly to any spiritual oppression and command it to leave in Jesus' name.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Dear Father, thank You for providing me with such wonderful power. Help me not to be afraid to use it for my sake and others.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 37:4 KJV - "Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart."
devotionals.devotional:
The traditional head of an African village sent his son to Europe to further his studies. While there, he fell in love with a lady from his country but from another tribe. They got married, despite their parent's objection, and had a son. When they returned after their studies, the lady and her son were rejected by her husband's family and were ostracised from the village. She went to live in the city with her son while the man remarried and was crowned the traditional head of the village when his father passed on.

Several years later, the boy went to a camping trip with his friends and got lost. A massive search for him began. After many twists and turns, the boy ended up in his father's village. It happened that her husband had died but could not be buried because the heir apparent must see the body last. The boy, in his wanderings, came upon the open casket, closed it and called for burial. The bewildered villagers crowned the estranged child as the traditional head of the village.

Similarly, Jephthah's family and community rejected him but difficult circumstances forced them to go back to him for reconciliation and they made him their head. You shall attain whatever God has destined for you. No plans to abort it shall succeed. Are you facing rejection or suffering estrangement? Don't despair; don't give up. God will navigate you back on course and your people will return to appreciate you. Keep faith!

Lesson: Rejection is not the end of your story. God can turn the same people who rejected you into those who celebrate you. Keep faith!

Action: If you are facing rejection today, do not despair. Declare that God will navigate you back on course. Keep believing.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Are you facing rejection or suffering estrangement? Receive grace to keep the faith.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Exodus 14:14 KJV - "The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace."
devotionals.devotional:
Have you been mocked because of your faith and dependence on God? Have you been despised, oppressed and made caricature of or have you been denied judgement and challenged to call on your God to save you? History is replete with many such stories of man's wickedness to his fellow man and his blatant defiance of God's judgement, especially if the victim lacks the capacity to fight back. Even our Lord Jesus Christ was denigrated as well (Matthew 27:43).

David faced such challenges and denigration in his lifetime but for once, he never took vengeance for himself. Once, when he was pushed to the wall and decided to fight for himself, he was dissuaded by a woman (1 Samuel 25:21-26). He was so reliant on God that twice, when he had the opportunity to kill his arch-enemy Saul, he refrained and left him to God. Again, when a palace coup was plotted against him by his own son, he refrained from fighting his cause so much that he was accused by his commander as loving his enemies and hating his friends. But did God vindicate him? Sure, He did!

When facing oppression, trusting God does not mean sitting down to do nothing but when you are overwhelmed and incapable of defending yourself, wait patiently on God. Surely, He will come to defend your cause.

Lesson: Waiting on God is not passivity; it is active trust. When you cannot fight for yourself, trust the One who fights for you.

Action: Identify a battle you have been trying to fight on your own. Surrender it to God today and wait patiently for Him to act.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I lift up my eyes to You, from whence my help comes.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 John 1:9 KJV - "If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness."
devotionals.devotional:
One problem I have with the doctrine of penance is that it makes the forgiveness of our sins an outcome of our effort which directly negates the inspired word of God. Arguing it out with some of my friends who are of the Roman Catholic faith, I pointed out that if this were so, then the death of our Lord Jesus Christ is futile. I make bold to say that it is a doctrine from the pit of hell to trivialise the work of the cross and a continuation of the Old Testament sacrifices for sin.

Just as Jesus pointed out to the Scribes in our text, so the Holy Spirit emphasises today: "... the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins." And as He forgave the paralytic without any special obligation of his, so He will forgive us if we simply open up ourselves to Him. He is the fulfilment of the law and through His death, fully paid the price, once and for all, for the forgiveness and remission of our sins. No other price needs be paid or any other effort need to be made.

Are you struggling with a weight of sin? Do you want to drop that load? Jesus is the perfect sacrifice. He is ever ready to forgive you and wash you clean, no matter how grievous the sin you may have committed. Confess your faults to Him right now, right where you are. He is there with you and ever ready to listen to you and forgive you. No other thing need be done and there is no protocol.

Lesson: Your forgiveness was purchased at the cross. Nothing you do can earn it; you only need to confess and receive it. Jesus paid it all.

Action: If you have been carrying guilt, stop. Confess your sins to God right now, receive His forgiveness, and walk in freedom.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord Jesus, I know I am a sinner. I confess my sins to You and ask that You forgive me. Come into my heart, wash me clean, be my Saviour and Lord and give me the power to live above sin. Amen.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Deuteronomy 31:6 KJV - "Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the LORD thy God, He it is that doth go with thee; He will not fail thee, nor forsake thee."
devotionals.devotional:
If we know by faith that God is with us, we can take on any challenge with confidence and courage. We may not always feel God's presence but we can always trust His Word and remember that He said He would never leave us nor forsake us. Remember that it was God who asked Moses to lead the children of Israel out of Egypt and it was also God who called Joshua to a great challenge of leadership – taking the children of Israel into the Promised Land.

The Bible tells us in this passage that Moses had died and Joshua was going to take his place as the leader of God's people. As soon as God gave this directive to Joshua, He immediately assured him: "No man shall be able to stand before you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you; I will not fail you or forsake you. Be strong and of good courage..."

One of the promises of God to his children is that He will be with them. Assuredly, if you have God by your side, then to fear is to be foolish. In the Bible, the basis for not fearing is simply that God is with us. And if we know God's character and nature, we know He is trustworthy. We do not have to know what He is going to do. Simply knowing He is with us is more than enough.

Lesson: You don't need to know what God is going to do; you just need to know that He is with you. If God is for you, who can be against you?

Action: Face your biggest fear today with this confession: "God is with me. I will not be afraid."
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, help me to face today with courage, knowing that You are with me. Amen.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Isaiah 43:2 KJV - "When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee."
devotionals.devotional:
Most times when we face one challenge or the other, we ask questions like "... where is God..." or we remind God of His numerous promises. Sometimes, succumbing to fear and doubt, we resort to self-help and try to find answers and solutions where none exists. However, going through the scriptures, I am yet to find a place where God promised us we would never have difficulties in this life but the scriptures are replete with several promises of His help during times of difficulty and challenges.

In our text, God speaks to us not to be afraid when we come up against difficulties neither will it do if we give up hope on Him. He promises to pour water to quench our thirst as well as flood our dry grounds, pour out His Spirit on our offspring and people shall subscribe to our God because of His blessings on our life. And maybe we are doubtful of His fulfilling these promises? Then He challenges us "Who can proclaim as I do? Then let Him declare it and set it in order for me ... Is there a God besides me? Indeed there is no other rock, I know not one."

Sometimes, even when we have applied all the bible principles, we still fail to overcome our challenges or the situation gets out of hand and gets worse. In such circumstances, several questions arise but I can only answer like worship leader Don Moen: "I know you might have questions ... I have questions but it doesn't change the fact that God said He's a healing God!"

Lesson: You may not understand your situation, but God is still God. Trust His promises even when you don't have all the answers.

Action: Write down one promise of God that applies to your current situation. Meditate on it whenever doubt arises.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Help me Lord to trust in Your promises during times of difficulty.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Ecclesiastes 3:1 KJV - "To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven."
devotionals.devotional:
Change, they say, is the only constant factor in life. We are all familiar with the changes in weather at different times of the year and the physiological and phenotypical changes in our body as we grow up and age. We troop out to vote for a change in our government and clamour for a change of unfavourable conditions. Every day, we observe how improvement and changes in technology affect both our lives and our world. Yet for all this, man is most afraid of changes.

Nothing, under heaven, is permanent. No situation, no matter how good or bad will last forever. In light of this, some advertorials say to live life in enjoyment because we only have one life and someone wrote that "we should do all the good we can, while we can, where we can, when we can and how we can." The knowledge that no condition is permanent will help us hold on even when we are passing through difficult circumstances. No matter how long it takes, it will surely fizzle out.

Our physical life is temporal and will end one day. The only thing that will count is what we achieved with it. How will you be remembered? Are we full of the cares of life and over-burdened with meeting up with our needs that we fail to make an impact in the lives of people around us? Those things we are struggling for will fade away one day. Our youthfulness and strength will soon end and we will become frail and weak. Only one thing counts – what you achieved for Jesus Christ here and how many souls you pointed to the Saviour.

Lesson: No condition is permanent. Your difficult season will pass, but what you do for Christ lasts forever.

Action: Today, do something that has eternal value—share your faith, show kindness, or invest in someone's spiritual growth.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, help me to use what little time I have here in this life positively for You.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Jeremiah 1:5 KJV - "Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations."
devotionals.devotional:
The UN estimated the world population to be over 7 billion people. In today's world of computed figures, we may not fully appreciate this gargantuan number but if everyone were to pass at a point at the rate of two persons per second, it will take over 116 years for us all to pass that point! Now, pause and consider your unique identity in this mammoth crowd. Do you know that there is nobody who has the same characteristics as you, even if you are an identical twin? Apart from your DNA that is peculiar to you, you have some unique physiological characteristics such as your voice, your eye lens, your gait, your finger prints, your calligraphic style, your tongue print. There is no other person that has any of these characteristics as you.

God created you special. David said "I will praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made..." God made each one of us unique and has a definite purpose for each person that is quite distinct from that of any other person. Our everyday experiences are specially made purpose-driven vehicles that God is using to bring us to that special place He has destined for us. And though the path He steers us through be dark and rough, yet all He demands from us is to trust Him as He says "For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, says the LORD, thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give you a future and a hope."

You are not a mistake. You are not an accident. You are uniquely designed by God for a specific purpose that no one else can fulfill. Do not compare yourself to others. Do not despise your uniqueness. Trust the One who formed you.

Lesson: You are fearfully and wonderfully made. No one else has your exact design or purpose. Embrace your uniqueness and trust God's plan.

Action: Thank God today for the unique way He created you. Ask Him to reveal the specific purpose He has for your life.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, help us to keep praising and trusting You, no matter the circumstances of life that we are facing even as Your unique purpose for us is being unveiled in our life.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Philippians 2:3 KJV - "Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves."
devotionals.devotional:
Any child who passed through Sunday school will know the first three verses of our text today by heart but when his parents sorely provoked him one day, my friend protested "but why does no one talk about or teach parents the fourth verse? The first three verses are always taught in the children church and when you come to the adult church, they teach from verse five!"

One of the greatest challenges of parenthood is proper child upbringing. We have different schools of thought on the subject today that range from one extreme to the other. Filial relationships can range from being extremely strained to very jovial. This is akin to master and servant relationship. How we deal with these issues will go a long way to really prove if we are truly children of God or not and can bring about mutual respect and binding affection.

Parents, masters, bosses, how do you deal with your children or subordinates? Do you give them a listening ear, are passionate about their needs and exhibit understanding or do you boss them around? Children, servants, workers, are you obedient to your parents or bosses? Do you serve and obey them with your whole heart and strength or with eye-service? True obedience is submission to authority without question or protest. It is the pathway to greatness. Whichever category you fall into, exemplify Christ in all you do.

Lesson: Healthy relationships require mutual respect, obedience, and love—whether between parent and child, boss and worker, or leader and follower.

Action: Identify one relationship in your life that needs improvement. Take a step today to exemplify Christ in that relationship.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Help me Lord to be an embodiment of Your love and grace to all I relate with in Jesus' name.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Philippians 4:19 KJV - "But my God shall supply all your need according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus."
devotionals.devotional:
I read a book in which the author listed the need of man in order, from the most important, according to him, to the least. They are: air, water, food, clothing and shelter. He argued that if you cannot breathe, nothing else matters. Somebody gasping for air cares less about water, food and other things. You can survive long without shelter or clothing; you can survive few months without food, few days without water but seconds without air. I am not surprised why the wonderful creator made us to breathe without even struggling to do so.

Some people are comfortable with their struggle to buy food and clothes or pay for rents thinking that that is what life is all about but our text today says "...having all self-sufficiency, you may abound to every good work." That is possessing enough to require no aid or support and furnished in abundance for every good work and charitable donation. Someone who is struggling to get money to buy food or clothes or to pay for rent will not find it easy to give to charity. God does not want us to struggle for these things. His idea is for us to have these things without struggle, just like we breathe without being conscious of it.

If we spend our time struggling for these, then we will not do His work and won't even enjoy the life He gave us. He wants us to move beyond these levels and live in abundance in order to help others and move the gospel forward. Reject poverty. It is not of God. Exercise faith in His promises and be diligent in what you are doing. Tell yourself everyday what God has said in His word about you. As you prayerfully confess His word over your life, you will have a change of level.

Lesson: God does not want you struggling for basic needs. He wants you to have abundance so you can be a blessing to others and advance His kingdom.

Action: Identify one area where you have accepted struggle as normal. Confess God's promises over that area and take a step of faith toward abundance.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I declare Your promises over my life and I believe that You are changing my level to the better from today in Jesus' name. Amen.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Philippians 4:9 KJV - "Those things, which ye have both learned, and received, and heard, and seen in me, do: and the God of peace shall be with you."
devotionals.devotional:
The children were playing outside and, unfortunately, one of them bucked his toe. As blood oozed from the wound, his Uncle offered to take him to a chemist shop to treat the wound but the boy disagreed. He said he should be prayed for first because the bible says the Lord God is our healer. This challenged the Uncle who marvelled at such faith expressed by a little boy of three. This prompted him to surrender his life to Christ.

The primary purpose of the word of God is not to provide information but to transform lives. No matter how much of the word of God you have heard and know, if it does not produce effective results in your life, it does you no good. Conversely, if you do not listen to and study the word of God, you will be bereft of the benefits of its enabling power and grace to live an effective Christian life.

However, as powerful as the word of God is, it will not produce results if there is no corresponding faith. Faith in the word of God means to put it into practice. "For indeed the gospel was preached to us as well as to them; but the word which they heard did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in those who heard it." (Hebrews 4:2). Practising the word of God actually keeps us spiritually fit and alert and helps us overcome the enemy when he comes.

Lesson: Hearing the Word is not enough; you must live it out. Faith without action is dead. Mix what you hear with faith and put it into practice.

Action: Choose one verse you read today and deliberately put it into practice before the day ends.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, help me not just to hear Your Word but to live it out. Let Your Word transform my life today.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Timothy 6:12 KJV - "Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses."
devotionals.devotional:
Righteousness is the nature of God that is imputed to anyone who believes in Jesus and surrenders to His Lordship over their life. Once this is done, God does not see the person as a sinner but sees the righteousness of Christ in him-her. Thus this righteousness cannot be obtained by our works or efforts. It is a gift of God and it makes us stand before God without condemnation (Romans 8:1).

Having been counted righteous through Christ, we have eternal life. Eternal life is not just living forever but it is having the nature of God, the life of God in us. Having this nature of God in us, we are not expected to continue to live a life of sin and lawlessness but a life of holiness and purity before God. And some might ask if this is possible, going by the treacherous temptations we face every day and the answer is a resounding yes! This is achievable by a constant study and meditation of the word of God (Joshua 1:8).

Don't sell your coat for a piece of smelly rag! Your righteousness before God is not by your making (Isaiah 64:6). Remember that as a slave of righteousness, you do not have a choice of your own. Even if everyone does as they like, maintain and live a life of righteousness.

Lesson: You are not saved by your righteousness, but you are saved to live righteously. Your lifestyle should reflect the gift you have received.

Action: Today, choose holiness over compromise. In one area where you have been compromising, take a stand for righteousness.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord I receive abundance of grace to live a life of righteousness before You and never to smear my life with sin. Amen.

devotionals.memoryVerse: John 3:14-15 KJV - "And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have eternal life."
devotionals.devotional:
A proverb in Igbo language posits that if you do not study history, take cognizance of what killed your father and take precaution against it, you stand a big chance of suffering the same fate. This perfectly describes the recorded life and times of the people of Israel in the scriptures as it is replete with stories of the rebellion of the Israelites against God and against their leaders, for which God disciplined them severally. The most curious aspect is that they always fail to learn from the failures of their forebears as they almost always repeated the same mistake.

In our text today, the people of Israel rose up again against God and against their leader, Moses because of the difficulties they were experiencing in their journey. God judged them for this by sending poisonous snakes against them which bit many to death until they cried out in remorse and repentance. God, in His mercy, set up a progenitor of the crucified Christ for their salvation with the condition that all a bitten victim needed to do was just to look at the hanging, bronze serpent and live. Just to look! Unfortunately, some scorned and disregarded this and died. What obstinacy!

Does this not tell the same story about us today? We live in rebellion and disobedience to God and His word and call it modernity and human rights. For this, God has sent several sicknesses and diseases against us yet we disregard His warning. He said that our eternal salvation is only in looking up to the crucified Christ and believing in Him but so many of us spurn that. The facts of the matter remain unchanged today. The only hope for the eternal salvation of mankind is the crucified Christ.

Lesson: The cure is simple: look and live. Look to Jesus, believe in Him, and you will have eternal life. Don't let stubbornness cost you your soul.

Action: If you have never looked to Jesus for salvation, do it today. If you have, help someone else look to Him.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord Jesus, I come to You today. I accept Your finished work on the cross for my salvation. Forgive my sins, wash me clean and make me Your child today. Amen.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Matthew 17:20 KJV - "If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you."
devotionals.devotional:
Hidekichi Miyazaki is a 105-year-old Japanese with the Guinness world record for the oldest man who ran a track race. Despite his age, Miyazaki has the ambition to race against the fastest man on the planet earth today, Usain Bolt. He expressed hope of its possibility in the coming years and declared that he will win him in the race. What a tall dream!

Zacchaeus had such a tall dream. He had a very strong desire to see the Saviour but he was of so little a stature that he could not bulldoze his way through the surging crowd. He, however, did not give up because of his limitations. He thought ahead, observed the Master's route and propelled by his strong desire, ran ahead, climbed a tree along the route and waited for Him to pass. Jesus honoured his faith and ambition. Zacchaeus only wanted to see the Saviour but he got more than he ever imagined – he was offered the opportunity to host the Master and he was saved, and his house.

What is the dream you have which both circumstances and people tell you it is not possible because you don't have the talent, resources or charisma to achieve it? Don't be discouraged and give up. Take a cue from Zacchaeus; look, observe, think and apply that little you think you can do. All God needs from you is for you to take a step of faith. People may make caricature of you when you take that step but if you can hold on and persevere, God will honour your faith and fulfil your desire.

Lesson: Faith is not about having all the resources; it is about taking the first step. Your little step of faith can lead to a great breakthrough.

Action: What step have you been afraid to take? Take it today—even if it seems small. God will honour your faith.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Help me Lord never to give up on my dreams. Give me the grace to keep on working at it even as You grant me breakthrough in Jesus' name.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Proverbs 21:2 KJV - "Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but the LORD pondereth the hearts."
devotionals.devotional:
On 12th January 2016, the social media was awash with pictures of a governor giving one thousand naira to an old, indigent woman while sitting in the comfort of his SUV. The pictures went viral with the claim that the governor was caring but social critics accused him of pride, lack of empathy and disrespect for elders. They claimed that the money was too insignificant to make an impact and that he should have come down from his car to show respect. They claimed he took the selfie to launder his image.

Sincerity of character is highly desired in the life of every Christian. It is easy to be smiling at a man while your heart is not smiling at him. That is hypocrisy. God detests it. It is not possible to deceive God because He sees the outward as well as the hidden intent of our hearts and He desires that as His children, we should not lead double lives.

Ask yourself why you are doing the things you do. Why do you dress the way you do? Is it to cover your nakedness and glorify God or to show off your attributes and get attraction? Why do you give money publicly? To show you have made it or because you sincerely felt compelled to give? Whatever we do for God without the right motive is dead on arrival before Him, no matter how great it may be. Don't do things to please men or for men to praise you, rather develop a habit to do all things for the glory of God.

Lesson: God is not impressed by the size of your gift or the volume of your service; He looks at the motive of your heart. Do all things for His glory.

Action: Before you do anything today, ask yourself: "Why am I doing this? Is it for God's glory or for my own?" Adjust your motive accordingly.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, search my heart and reveal any wrong motive. Help me to do all things for Your glory, not for the praise of men.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Matthew 5:14 KJV - "Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hid."
devotionals.devotional:
John the Baptist was a man who carried both fire and light. Jesus described him as "a burning and a shining light." There is a significant difference between burning and shining. A torchlight can shine brightly, but it cannot ignite another flame. However, a piece of burning wood can set nearby wood on fire. God does not want you only to shine; He wants you to burn as well. When you burn, you have the power to ignite passion for God in the lives of others. This is how revival begins—when one burning heart sets another on fire.

Our lives have the power to prepare the way of the Lord when we are truly burning and shining. People were drawn to John in the wilderness because his life carried both light and heat. He did not just speak about God; his life demonstrated a fervent, passionate devotion that compelled others to repent and turn to God. Romans 12:11 reminds us not to be slothful in business but fervent in spirit, serving the Lord. God is looking for men and women who carry this kind of spiritual fire.

Proverbs 4:18 declares that the path of the just is like the shining light that shines more and more unto the perfect day. Your life is meant to grow brighter each day, not remain stagnant. It is not about your past or what you have done before. God expects you to keep improving, to keep burning brighter. In this generation, we need Christians who constantly seek to grow, to be better today than they were yesterday.

Lesson: Being a burning and shining light means your life not only reflects Christ but also ignites passion for Him in others. You are called to be a catalyst for revival, not just a spectator.

Action: Examine your spiritual temperature today. Are you merely shining, or are you also burning? Ask God to reignite His fire in your heart so that through you, others may catch the flame of His love and salvation.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, set my heart on fire for You. Let me not only shine but also burn with such passion that others are drawn to You through my life. Revive me again, that Your people may rejoice in You.

devotionals.topic: Walking with the Lord and One Another
devotionals.memoryVerse: Romans 12:18 KJV - "If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men."
devotionals.devotional:
The first thing every believer must do is agree to walk with the Lord. Before we can work in the church or serve in any capacity, we must first learn to walk with God. Our work with God is deeply personal, and each of us will give an account individually. Paul reminds us that we are workers together with Him, but this partnership begins with a personal relationship, not with religious activity.

However, walking with God is not enough. We are also called to walk with one another. This means we must avoid offending our brothers and sisters. Proverbs 18:19 warns that an offended brother is harder to win than a strong city. We must also avoid bitterness, envy, and grudges. Division is another enemy of our walk together. Jesus said in Matthew 12:25 that a house divided against itself will not stand.

What should we do instead? We must value peace and live peaceably with all men as much as it depends on us. We should accept people as God made them and receive one another as Christ received us. We must be self-controlled—swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to wrath. Most importantly, we must pray for one another and forgive anyone we have anything against. This is the pathway to unity and victorious Christian living.

Lesson: Walking with God and walking with fellow believers are inseparable. You cannot claim to love God whom you have not seen while hating your brother whom you have seen.

Action: Identify one person you have offended or who has offended you. Take a step today toward reconciliation. Forgive, pray for them, and restore the bond of peace.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, help me to walk faithfully with You and lovingly with my brethren. Remove every root of bitterness, envy, and offence from my heart, and make me an instrument of Your peace.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Numbers 14:24 KJV - "But My servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed Me fully, him will I bring into the land whereinto he went; and his seed shall possess it."
devotionals.devotional:
God is looking for men, women, and youths who will overcome challenges and take mountains for Him. Mountains represent any place or situation that needs transformation—difficult circumstances, impossible dreams, or territories that seem unconquerable. Many of us feel uncomfortable with where we are, but God wants us to rise, overcome, and take mountains in this new season. Your attitude toward the things of God should be different from the crowd.

Caleb is our example. He had righteous desires; he longed to see God's promises fulfilled. He was a man of faith who boldly believed in God's ability to deliver the land into his hands. When others saw giants, Caleb saw victory. He was fully committed to God, not casual about his relationship. God testified that Caleb had "another spirit" and followed Him fully. At eighty-five years old, Caleb was still a warrior. He said, "I am as strong this day as I was in the day Moses sent me."

Those who see problems and take action to address them are the ones who move mountains and make progress. Jesus taught that if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you can say to this mountain, "Move from here to there," and it will move. The mountain in your life is not there to stop you; it is there to show the world what your God can do.

Lesson: Your attitude toward challenges determines your altitude in God's kingdom. Caleb inherited his mountain because he had a different spirit—a spirit of faith, commitment, and courage.

Action: Identify one "mountain" in your life today—a challenge, a dream, or a God-given vision. Refuse to be intimidated. Speak to that mountain in Jesus' name, and take one practical step toward conquering it.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, give me the spirit of Caleb—a spirit of faith, full commitment, and holy courage. I will not be afraid of the giants. Give me this mountain, for You are with me.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Corinthians 3:9 KJV - "For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry, ye are God's building."
devotionals.devotional:
Building is a strategy for welfare, but due to worldly perspectives, many misunderstand its true purpose. Building is not a waste of time; rather, those who build are respected and valued. God is looking for builders in this generation. There are three categories of people: the builders, the users, and the destroyers. The producers—the builders—are always wealthier than those who merely consume. If you desire to find favor with God, be a builder. We are born again to build, not just to use or destroy.

There are two key areas we must build. First, the house of God. Jesus said, "I will build My church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it." God is building His house through us. We are God's building, and He develops our character, finances, health, and ministries to strengthen His church. Our work in God's house is a lifelong commitment. Second, we must build ourselves. Jude 1:20-21 instructs us to build ourselves up in our most holy faith. If you fail to invest in your spiritual and personal growth, you will lack value in both God's sight and the eyes of men.

Kingdom builders are not confused or unstable; they are focused and purpose-driven. Why do people fail to build? Many are deceived by their own thinking. Wisdom is required for effective building. Cooperation and perseverance are necessary. A well-built life has something to offer.

Lesson: You were born again to build—God's house and your own life. Building requires wisdom, commitment, and perseverance, but it yields eternal rewards.

Action: Ask yourself today: What am I building for God's kingdom? What is my contribution to my local church? Take one concrete step this week to invest in either God's house or your own spiritual growth.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, give me the grace to build and to finish. Make me a Kingdom builder, not a user or destroyer. Establish the work of my hands for Your glory.

devotionals.topic: The Force to Take the Kingdom
devotionals.memoryVerse: Matthew 11:12 KJV - "And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force."
devotionals.devotional:
For God's will to be done on earth, a specific force is required. Evangelism exists to advance the kingdom, but the devil opposes everything we do for God. The enemy seeks to weaken our faith and turn us into unbelievers. If we are to succeed, we must take the kingdom by force. Without the fire of God in our hearts, we become lukewarm. This force is not physical aggression but unwavering commitment to God and His work.

There are several forces we must employ. First, the force of commitment. Commitment keeps us going and ensures the church stands firm. A committed heart will never allow the church to die. Second, the force of zeal. Personal zeal is essential for advancing the kingdom. When zeal is absent, all that remains is fatigue, weakness, and a failed Christian life. Third, the force of faithfulness. Faithfulness is not ordinary; it is a spiritual force. Fourth, the force of loyalty. God desires us to serve according to His heart, not our own. Loyalty is a force that even the devil cannot hinder.

The enemy seeks to weaken our faith and turn us into unbelievers. That is why we must be violent in our pursuit of God's purposes—not violent toward people, but violent against every force that opposes the advancement of God's kingdom. We must refuse to be lukewarm. We must refuse to give up. The kingdom belongs to those who press in with holy determination.

Lesson: Taking the kingdom by force requires commitment, zeal, faithfulness, and loyalty. These spiritual forces empower us to overcome every opposition from the enemy.

Action: Identify one area where you have become lukewarm or complacent in your Christian walk. Reignite your zeal today by taking a specific action—pray longer, serve more, share your faith, or recommit to a neglected spiritual discipline.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, empower me with the forces of commitment, zeal, faithfulness, and loyalty. I refuse to be lukewarm. I will take Your kingdom by force and fulfill Your will in my generation.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 90:17 KJV - "And let the beauty of the LORD our God be upon us: and establish Thou the work of our hands upon us; yea, the work of our hands establish Thou it."
devotionals.devotional:
God is interested in our work and wants to help us—as long as we do good work. He is ready to establish the work of our hands. We must engage in legitimate businesses so that God will bless them. The Bible does not separate sacred work from secular work. Everything we do should give glory to God. Work is a gift from God. When He created man, He gave him the gift of work. Your business and skills are divine gifts. Since work is a gift, we must work in a way that honors Him.

Work is biblical. Second Thessalonians 3:10 teaches that work is not just for survival but for impacting society, the church, and future generations. Work is dignified. It brings honor, and the real profit is not just money but the value it creates for people. Work is a service to God and humanity, and we must strive to make our work acceptable to God. Work is also a place of discipleship. Even if we start without experience, we can learn and grow.

How should believers work? We must work wholeheartedly, giving our best effort. We must work with excellence, doing our work in a way that exceeds expectations. We must work with joy, serving gladly. We must work with integrity, being honest and sincere. When we work well, people will respect our faith and glorify God.

Lesson: Work is a gift and a divine mandate. When we work with excellence, integrity, and joy, our labour becomes an act of worship that glorifies God and impacts the world.

Action: Evaluate your work ethic today. Are you working wholeheartedly as unto the Lord? Choose one area where you can improve your excellence, integrity, or attitude, and commit it to God in prayer.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, establish the work of my hands. Help me to work with excellence, integrity, and joy, so that my labour brings glory to Your name and blessing to others.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Luke 18:27 KJV - "And He said, The things which are impossible with men are possible with God."
devotionals.devotional:
A cycle is something that happens repeatedly—a pattern of failure, stagnation, or misfortune that seems unbreakable. Many people suffer from what can be called "near-success syndrome," always close to the goal but never achieving it. Others experience year after year without progress, whether in their finances, family, or even their walk with God. But there is good news: Jesus is the Cycle Breaker. He has all power in heaven and on earth, and He is able to break every evil cycle in your life.

The story of Jabez in 1 Chronicles 4:5-10 gives us a powerful example. Jabez faced a generational problem—his name meant sorrow. But he refused to accept his fate. He cried out to God, "Oh that You would bless me indeed, and enlarge my territory, that Your hand would be with me, and that You would keep me from evil, that I may not cause pain!" And God granted his request. Jabez decided that the change would begin with him. You too can decide today that the cycle stops with you.

Faith is required to break cycles. In business, family, and life, we must exercise our faith. God Himself establishes some cycles, but He also empowers people to break the negative ones. God raises men and women to be vessels of honor, breaking cycles within His house and beyond. Avoid unbelief! Trust God completely and do not allow doubt to hinder His work.

Lesson: Jesus has the power to break every negative cycle in your life. Through faith and prayer, you can experience breakthrough just like Jabez did.

Action: Identify one recurring negative cycle in your life—a pattern of failure, sin, or stagnation. Bring it to Jesus today in prayer. Declare Him as your Cycle Breaker and take one step of faith to break that pattern.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Jesus, You are the Cycle Breaker. I bring every recurring negative pattern in my life to You. Break the cycle of failure, stagnation, and sorrow. Enlarge my territory and let Your hand be with me. Amen.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Judges 5:23 KJV - "Curse ye Meroz, said the angel of the LORD, curse ye bitterly the inhabitants thereof; because they came not to the help of the LORD, to the help of the LORD against the mighty."
devotionals.devotional:
To be a child of God is to be a soldier in His army. Every believer must be battle-ready because no victory comes without a fight. The Book of the Wars of the Lord records the battles fought by Israel to fulfill God's will. Even today, the Lord is still waging war. Zion is not a place of ease but a battlefield. If you refuse to join the Lord in the fight, He will still win, but you will miss out on His blessings. The city of Meroz was cursed because they refused to fight alongside the angels of the Lord, and that curse led to their complete extinction.

This is God's battle, and we must fight alongside Him with unwavering commitment. To be a Christian is to be a soldier of the Lord, fighting against Satan, evil, and the forces opposing God's kingdom. The battle is about control—will the Lord reign, or will the world dominate? It is a fight for the souls of men, and there is no excuse for refusing to engage. God allows us to face battles to teach us warfare and to prepare us for greater victories.

How do we fight the Lord's battle? First, with God's Word—the truth of Scripture is our greatest weapon. Second, with wisdom and strategy—using intelligence, connections, and opportunities to advance God's kingdom. Third, with our finances—supporting God's work financially is part of spiritual warfare. Much is required to fight the Lord's battle, and God is depending on you.

Lesson: Every believer is called to be a soldier in God's army. Refusing to join the battle brings a curse, but fighting alongside the Lord brings victory and blessing.

Action: Identify one way you have been passive in God's work. Today, take a step to actively engage—pray for a specific need, give to a ministry, share your faith, or serve in a neglected area of your church.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I answer Your call to battle. I will not be like Meroz. I will fight alongside You and Your angels for the souls of men and the advancement of Your kingdom. Use me as Your weapon of war.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Proverbs 11:30 KJV - "The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and he that winneth souls is wise."
devotionals.devotional:
Some people do not engage in evangelism because they do not truly understand its significance. But soul winning brings joy to the Father. When we buy a car or earn a degree, we rejoice, but what truly makes God happy is the salvation of a soul. The parable of the lost sheep shows that heaven rejoices over one sinner who repents. God's greatest desire is for all to come to repentance. If you are not spreading the Good News, you are not making God happy.

Soul winning makes us wise in God's eyes. Proverbs 11:30 says, "He that winneth souls is wise." The word "wins" suggests a continuous effort, not a one-time event. Just as a woman seeking a child is desperate, we should have the same urgency in winning souls. Daniel 12:3 reminds us that those who turn many to righteousness will shine like the stars forever. Soul winning has eternal value beyond earthly pursuits. It also beautifies our Christian life before God. Isaiah 52:7 says, "How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news!"

Soul winning leads to church growth. The early church grew both biologically and by multiplication through soul winning. A growing church is a soul-winning church. It is also a channel through which we receive grace. Finally, it qualifies us for a crown in heaven. Paul said, "I have fought a good fight." Soul winners will receive a crown of righteousness. Winning souls secures eternal rewards beyond anything this world offers.

Lesson: Soul winning is not optional—it brings joy to God, wisdom to us, growth to the church, grace to our lives, and eternal rewards in heaven.

Action: Before this week ends, share your faith with one person. It could be a friend, family member, or stranger. Pray for them, speak a word of encouragement, and invite them to know Jesus.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, give me urgency and boldness to win souls. Let me not keep the good news to myself. Use me to bring joy to Your heart and to gather eternal fruit for Your kingdom.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Genesis 15:6 KJV - "And he believed in the LORD; and He counted it to him for righteousness."
devotionals.devotional:
Many people live wasted lives with no record before God, but Abraham lived a life that was counted as righteous because he believed in God and trusted that His words are always true. For us today, if our lives are meaningful, they will be counted in heaven. God established a covenant with Abraham because he relied on Him. When God can count on us, He can make us great—just as He made Abraham and brought forth nations and kings through him. There are people whom God cannot count on, but if He can count on us, then heavenly blessings are sure.

There are steps to making your life count before God. First, salvation in Christ. No life will be counted before God unless the person has Jesus as their Lord and Savior. You must be born again for your life to matter in eternity. Colossians 1:27 tells us that without Christ, nothing works. There is no hope outside of Christ. Only in Him do our lives have meaning and value before God. Second, living by faith. Romans 1:16-17 declares that a life that counts before God is one lived by faith. Serving God in season and out of season makes our lives significant before Him. Third, making Jesus the Lord of your life. Jesus is the Master of the Church. He must be in full control of our lives.

When God can count on you, He will bless you abundantly. Abraham's life counted because he believed God. Your life can count too. It begins with salvation, continues with faith, and is sustained by surrendering to the Lordship of Jesus.

Lesson: A life that counts before God is built on salvation in Christ, lived by faith, and submitted to the Lordship of Jesus.

Action: Take inventory of your life today. Have you truly surrendered to Jesus as Lord? Are you living by faith? Make any needed adjustments and recommit your life to count for eternity.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I want my life to count before You. I believe in You like Abraham did. Be my Savior and my Lord. Help me to live by faith every day so that my life brings You glory.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Corinthians 15:57 KJV - "But thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ."
devotionals.devotional:
To walk in victory is the good Christian life to enjoy. It is not just a life of outside victory but a life of both outside and inward victory. Walking in victory is not a life that denies the challenge of temptations, obstacles, life's challenges, and trials. Rather, it is a life that overcomes and wins in all. Victory is our heritage in Christ. We must not live our lives in depression or despair. Hence, we are expected to walk constantly in victory.

Notice that this victory is not gained by human efforts. It is a gift from God, accessed through faith in Christ. First Samuel 2:9 reminds us that no man prevails by his own strength. First John 5:4-5 declares that whatever is born of God overcomes the world, and this is the victory that overcomes the world—even our faith. We can walk in victory through the redemption power of God, which is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all we ask or think.

We are called to live for Christ, to live a holy life and a life of obedience. We are to be the Lord's light in a dark world and to share His gospel and make disciples. We overcome obstacles and life's challenges by trusting that God will not allow us to be tempted beyond what we can bear, and He will with the temptation make a way of escape. Blessed is the man who endures temptation, for when he is tried, he will receive the crown of life.

Lesson: Victory is your heritage in Christ. It is not earned by human effort but received by faith. You are called to walk in victory daily, overcoming every challenge through His power.

Action: Identify an area where you have been living in defeat rather than victory. Declare God's promise of victory over that area today. Thank Him that the battle is already won through Christ.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, thank You for giving me victory through Jesus Christ. I refuse to live in depression or defeat. I walk in victory today—over sin, over fear, over every challenge. You have made me more than a conqueror.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Isaiah 40:31 KJV - "But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint."
devotionals.devotional:
What enables us to maintain our victory in the Christian journey is the renewal of our strength. The strength we need is not physical strength but spiritual strength that comes from God. It is enduring and lasting. God's desire is that we continually renew our strength so we can rise to the heights He has prepared for us. The Christian walk is not always easy. There are times of weariness and discouragement, but those moments call for a renewal of strength. If you feel you have come a long way, remember: the journey is just beginning. As Jeremiah 12:5 says, "If you have run with footmen and they have wearied you, then how can you contend with horses?"

How do we renew our strength? First, practise the presence of God. Be conscious that God is always with you. Practising His presence daily brings peace, assurance, and strength. Second, repentance. Even believers must repent when they sin. Unforgiveness and unconfessed sins block spiritual strength. Repentance brings restoration. Third, the Word of God. Spend quality time with the Word—read it, study it, meditate on it, and apply it. The more you align with God's truth, the more strength and clarity you receive. Fourth, fasting and prayer. Some challenges respond only to fasting and prayer.

When we renew our strength, there is a divine exchange. God replaces your weakness with His strength. People around you will be amazed at what you can handle through His power. You will do exploits. With renewed strength, you begin to accomplish things beyond human ability. Your light will shine. God will ignite your lamp, and your light will shine at home, in your community, and everywhere you go.

Lesson: Renewing your strength is not optional—it is essential for sustaining victory. Through God's presence, repentance, His Word, and prayer, you can rise higher and shine brighter.

Action: Choose one of the four strength-renewing practices today—practising God's presence, repentance, spending time in the Word, or fasting—and commit to it intentionally this week.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, renew my strength today. I am weary, but I wait on You. Replace my weakness with Your power. Let me mount up with wings as an eagle, run without weariness, and walk without fainting.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 John 3:8 KJV - "For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that He might destroy the works of the devil."
devotionals.devotional:
The victory of the cross is the greatest victory ever won in the history of mankind. Christ's suffering was not for His own sins but for ours. His vicarious death gave birth to a new people—Christians. It is through believing in Christ and His finished work on the cross that we are transformed and called saints. You are a Christian today because you believe in what Christ did for you. You are deeply loved, and the cross is the reason for your new identity.

Satan was dethroned by the power of the cross. The devil's authority was neutralised. 1 John 3:8 tells us that the Son of God was manifested to destroy the works of the devil. Notice that we are not fighting the devil—Christ has already fought and defeated him. The Bible simply tells us to resist the devil, because the battle has already been won. The victory of the cross has delivered us from the powers of darkness. Romans 5:8-9 shows that though every human being was once under God's wrath, Christ's sacrifice has set us free. That is why we are not meant to live a defeated life.

Through His death, Jesus destroyed the one who holds the power of death—the devil—and freed us from the fear and bondage of death. Faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the Word of God. As you hear and believe the message of the cross, you will walk in the reality of this victory. The cross is not just a historical event; it is the source of your daily victory over sin, Satan, and death.

Lesson: The victory of the cross is complete and final. Christ has defeated the devil, and you now share in that victory through faith. You are not fighting for victory; you are fighting from victory.

Action: Meditate today on the finished work of the cross. Thank Jesus for His sacrifice. Resist any lie of the enemy that tries to make you live as though the battle is still yours to win.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord Jesus, thank You for the victory of the cross. You have destroyed the works of the devil and set me free. I live from victory, not for victory. I am more than a conqueror through You.

devotionals.topic: The Stone Shall Be Rolled Away
devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 121:1-2 KJV - "I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help. My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth."
devotionals.devotional:
Easter is the message of God's supernatural power. It reminds us that no matter how impossible a situation seems, God is able to turn it around. Sometimes in life, we face challenges—delays, barriers, and various forms of hardship—and we find ourselves asking, "Who will roll away the stone?" That stone—whether it is a problem, stagnation, or hopelessness—can feel like a heavy seal over our destiny, just like the stone that was rolled over Jesus' tomb. But the message of Easter is a message of hope: you will come out of the grave.

The stone was rolled over Jesus' grave to stop Him from rising, but it could not succeed. If Jesus came out of the grave, then you too will come out of every grave-like situation. Nothing can stop you. God is giving you hope again, and the God who promised is faithful to fulfill what He has said. How was the stone rolled away? First, by divine intervention. God sent His angel to roll away the stone. There was supernatural intervention. In the same way, there shall be supernatural intervention in your life. Second, through the completed work of Christ. The Bible declares that the warfare has been accomplished. Because Jesus completed the battle, you will fulfill your purpose.

Until the stone is rolled away, there will be no manifestation of the sons of God. The battle has been fought and won—now is the time to manifest God's glory. What makes the stone roll away? Help from God, angelic assistance, God's power at work, and persistent prayer. God is interested in seeing you fulfill every divine goal. No matter how large or heavy the obstacle may seem, there is hope because of Easter.

Lesson: The same power that rolled away the stone from Jesus' tomb is at work in your life. No obstacle is too great when God intervenes.

Action: Identify the "stone" in your life today—the obstacle that seems impossible to move. Lift your eyes to the Lord. Ask for His help, and trust that He is rolling that stone away even now.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I lift my eyes to You. Roll away the stone that has sealed my destiny—every obstacle, every delay, every hopeless situation. I trust in Your supernatural power. My help comes from You.

devotionals.topic: Don't Gamble: Go for the Real Thing
devotionals.memoryVerse: Mark 8:34 KJV - "Whosoever will come after Me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow Me."
devotionals.devotional:
Many people come to church not for Jesus but for what they can get from Him. But we must not treat Jesus like a gamble. Don't come to church just for blessings—come to meet the God of the church. When Jesus was crucified, the soldiers cast lots for His clothing. That is what many still do today—they gamble for the things of Jesus without embracing Jesus Himself. People are interested in church activities, programs, and miracles, but they don't embrace the Christ of the cross. They want wealth, healing, or success, but they ignore the One who gives these things.

A person living this way cannot experience the true power of God that comes through a relationship with Jesus Christ. Yes, wealth, health, and prosperity are good. But when God blesses you with these, don't stop there—go deeper. Go for what is eternal. Embrace Jesus Christ. Everything we gain in this life will pass away, but only what has eternal value will count in the end. Mark 12:28-34 tells the story of a man who was close to the kingdom. Jesus told him, "You are not far from the kingdom of God." He had knowledge of the scriptures, but he had not entered the kingdom. Head knowledge is not enough. You must embrace the Christ of the cross.

Mark 8:34-38 reminds us what it means to truly be a Christian: "Whoever wants to be My disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross and follow Me." To be a Christian is to follow Christ, deny self, and live a life that pleases Him. The cross represents sacrifice, surrender, and commitment. You cannot identify with Christ and reject His cross. Many are active in church but not alive in Christ. Activity is not the same as intimacy. If you want to be alive in Christ, you must embrace Him fully—not just what He offers.

Lesson: Do not gamble with your soul by seeking only the blessings of God without embracing the God of the blessings. Christ and His cross are the real thing—nothing else matters.

Action: Examine your heart today. Are you pursuing Jesus or just His benefits? Repent if needed, and recommit to following Christ fully—cross and all.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, forgive me for seeking Your hand more than Your face. I embrace You, not just Your blessings. I take up my cross and follow You. You are the real thing, and nothing else matters.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Hebrews 7:25 KJV - "Wherefore He is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by Him, seeing He ever liveth to make intercession for them."
devotionals.devotional:
The resurrection of Jesus is the cornerstone of our faith. It is because He is risen that our faith is real. If Christ had not risen, our faith would be in vain. The angel called Jesus "Lord," affirming His authority both on earth and in heaven. The core of our proclamation is this: Jesus is risen! And because He lives, we can boldly declare Him everywhere. Hebrews 7:25 reveals what Jesus did for us, grounded in His divine nature and confirmed by His Lordship: "He is able to save to the uttermost those who come to God through Him."

What does the resurrection tell us? First, Jesus is alive. The tomb was empty—proof that Jesus has risen. The grave could not hold Him because He lives! Second, the finished work of redemption. On the cross, Jesus declared, "It is finished." This signifies that the redemptive work was completed. Through His death and resurrection, salvation is now available to all who believe. Third, the unfinished work of Christ. While redemption is complete, Christ continues His work through us. He has made us His ambassadors. Our ongoing mission is to bring souls to God. Second Corinthians 6:1 reminds us that we are "workers together with Him." Every believer is called to evangelism. Through us, Christ reaches the lost.

What is Jesus doing now? He ever lives to intercede for us. Christ is not only alive but actively interceding on our behalf. He has not abandoned us. He said, "I will never leave you nor forsake you." Every child of God is dearly loved and constantly supported by our risen Lord. He is able to save anyone. Jesus transforms sinners into saints. No one is beyond His saving grace. He receives all who come to Him and will raise us up at the last day. He is always available, present with us at all times.

Lesson: The risen Jesus is not just a historical figure; He is our ever-living Saviour, interceding for us, saving souls, and empowering His people.

Action: Live today with confidence in the risen Christ. Share the gospel with boldness and walk in the victory of the resurrection. He lives, and because He lives, you can face anything.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord Jesus, You are risen indeed! Thank You for living to intercede for me. I am never alone. I live with confidence because You live. Use me to share Your resurrection power with others.

devotionals.memoryVerse: James 4:7 KJV - "Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you."
devotionals.devotional:
In the face of crucifixion, Jesus submitted to the will of God, saying, "Not what I will, but what You will." This act of surrender reveals the lifestyle God desires for every believer—a life of submission. Through submission, we experience true victory in the Christian life. Christian submission is a voluntary act of surrendering one's will, desires, and authority to a higher authority. It is not forced—it is an intentional, humble obedience inspired by the Holy Spirit. God has a purpose for Christian submission: to transform us so He can work through us. Isaiah 55:9 reminds us that God's ways are higher than ours.

Jesus demonstrated submission in many ways. He became flesh and dwelt among us. He humbled Himself and became obedient unto death—even death on a cross. He suffered for us, leaving us an example to follow. There are dimensions of Christian submission. First, the divine dimension: submit yourselves to God. Each time you submit to Him, you resist the devil. Submission to God strengthens you. While the world may see it as weakness, it is actually a source of strength. Second, the family dimension. Wives are called to submit to their husbands, and children to their parents. This order brings harmony and reflects Christ's relationship with the church. Third, the church dimension. Submit to spiritual leaders and elders. When you submit to church leadership, you open the door for blessings, guidance, and divine opportunities. Fourth, the civil dimension. Believers must submit to government authorities, as all power is ordained by God.

Why do we submit? Out of love for Christ. Jesus submitted to the Father and died for us. Our submission is a response of love to Him. Jesus asked Peter, "Do you love Me?" Love is expressed through action. Jesus said, "If you love Me, keep My commandments." True love motivates sacrifice. Because Christ laid down His life for us, we are called to lay down our lives for others. Let us walk in submission like Christ did. Through it, we become vessels fit for God's use and walk in the path of true victory.

Lesson: Submission to God and to the authorities He has placed over us is not weakness but strength. It is the path to victory and the key to becoming a vessel God can use.

Action: Identify one area where you have resisted submission—to God, to church leadership, to family order, or to civil authority. Choose to submit willingly today out of love for Christ.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I choose to submit to You as Jesus did. Not my will, but Yours be done. Help me to submit to the authorities You have placed over me, knowing that this is the path to true victory.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Ephesians 2:8 KJV - "For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God."
devotionals.devotional:
Grace is God's power and ability working in the lives of men to bring His purposes to pass. It is saving, exceeding, and bountiful. Grace is not just a concept—it is divine action that produces tangible results in our lives. Progress, victory, and success in life are not based on intelligence, skill, or effort alone—but on the grace that God releases. Without the grace of God, no amount of resources, planning, or effort will be enough to fulfill our callings—in ministry, business, or life. Every God-given vision and true success story is carried by the power of grace.

First Corinthians 15:9-10 shows us how grace transformed Apostle Paul. He said, "By the grace of God I am what I am." The same grace that empowered Paul is available to you. Grace is not earned—it is a gift, freely given through Jesus Christ. Ephesians 2:4-9 reminds us that God is rich in mercy—and in many other blessings, including grace. Verses 8-9 emphasize that grace is a gift, not the result of our hard work or qualifications. By the grace of God at work in your life, others will be blessed. People shall be touched, helped, and lifted through the grace you have received.

Let us embrace this season as a time to walk in divine grace—resting in God's ability, not our own. Grace is not just for salvation; it is for every area of life. Whether you need wisdom, strength, finances, or breakthrough, grace is available. The key is to stop striving in your own strength and start depending on His grace. When you do, you will see things change.

Lesson: Grace is God's divine power at work in you to accomplish what you cannot do on your own. It is a gift, not a reward. Embrace it and walk in it.

Action: Identify one area where you have been striving in your own strength. Surrender it to God today and ask for His grace to empower you. Rest in His ability, not your own.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I receive Your grace today. I cannot do this on my own. Let Your grace work in me and through me to fulfill Your purpose for my life. By Your grace, I am what I am.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Romans 11:29 KJV - "For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance."
devotionals.devotional:
Our new birth—being born again—is the result of God's grace. Grace is not just favor; it is a divine force given to empower us for an assignment. There is grace for every need, and it is this same grace that brought you to this church. The call of grace is God working beyond human strength and ability. It is a divine operation both within and outside of a person. It energizes and motivates you so strongly that no external encouragement is needed. This call is reflected in our lives and service. It challenges us to live a Christlike life and to embody Christian character. It sets us apart from the crowd.
