What is the call of grace? First, it is a call to experiential knowledge of God. This knowledge empowers us to make a lasting impact on others. We act based on what we have encountered. The call of grace is a call to responsibility—it means not taking God's calling lightly. Ask yourself: How much influence am I having on others through my life? Second, it is a call to grow spiritually. We are not meant to remain spiritual babies. Growth in grace leads to growth in the knowledge of Jesus Christ. That knowledge comes through experience. How has the Word you know been working in your life? What has been your personal encounter with Christ?

Things to understand about the call of grace: The call of grace separates you. God separates and sets apart those He calls—even from people close to them. If your calling hasn't separated you from sin or from ungodly relationships, then you may not yet fully understand what the call of grace means. The call of grace is to reveal Jesus in us. The world wants to see Jesus—and they are to see Him in us. God wants to reveal Christ through you. The Christ we preach must be the Christ revealed in our lives. That is what makes our message effective.

Lesson: The call of grace is not just to be heard—it must be answered with deep conviction. It separates you for God's purpose, reveals Christ through you, and includes suffering for His sake.

Action: How convinced are you about the call of God upon your life? Take time today to pray and ask God to confirm His calling and to reveal Jesus more fully in you.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I answer the call of grace upon my life. Separate me for Your purpose. Reveal Your Son in me so that the world may see Jesus through my life. Let Your grace empower me to fulfill Your calling.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Corinthians 9:8 KJV - "And God is able to make all grace abound toward you; that ye, always having all sufficiency in all things, may abound to every good work."
devotionals.devotional:
To be abundant means to be more than enough—overflowing, inexhaustible, and ever-sufficient. When we speak of God's grace as abundant, we mean that there is more than enough grace for everything God calls us to do. There is no situation too difficult, no task too demanding, and no challenge too great where His grace will not sustain us. God's grace is not limited. It is enduring, ever-available, and purposeful. It is for salvation—and beyond. His interest is that we live by this grace, and it never fails. God's grace is the divine provision that empowers, transforms, and sustains.

What is the evidence that God's grace is abundant? First, grace saves us. Ephesians 2:8 declares, "For by grace are ye saved through faith." Paul testifies to the overflowing grace that saved him. Our transformed lives are visible testimonies of God's saving grace. Second, grace transforms our identity. Paul, once a persecutor, became a powerful apostle by grace. Ask yourself: Is the grace of God evident in your life? Does your life testify that God can save and transform? Third, grace calls and equips us to serve. Grace enables us to serve in God's kingdom, regardless of our past. Fourth, grace empowers growth and purpose. God's grace moves us from one level of growth to another. It empowers us to live for Him and carry out our unique assignments.

Important reminders about abundant grace: Abundant grace is for every believer. Every child of God has access to this overflowing grace. We must walk by faith, not by sight. Grace operates in the realm of faith. To walk in abundant grace, trust God's word above what you see. Do not grieve the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit is the seal of God's ownership in your life. It is not church title or activity that secures God's grace, but obedience and sensitivity to His Spirit. When we disobey or ignore His promptings, we grieve Him—and this hinders our experience of grace.

Lesson: God's grace is not just for getting saved—it is for living victoriously every day. It is abundant, sufficient, and available. Walk in it and let it transform you.

Action: Identify one area where you have been relying on your own strength. Confess it to God and ask for His abundant grace to be released in that area today.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I receive Your abundant grace. Let it abound toward me today so that I may have all sufficiency in all things and abound to every good work. I trust Your grace, not my strength.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 84:11 KJV - "For the LORD God is a sun and shield: the LORD will give grace and glory: no good thing will He withhold from them that walk uprightly."
devotionals.devotional:
The Spirit of Grace is essential in our lives and service, because Christ Jesus came full of grace. We serve a God of grace, and through Him, we enjoy both provision and abundant blessings. We must understand that it takes grace to fulfill our mission and ministry. Grace works from within—through our spirit—not from the outside. Every believer, every church, and every child of God who desires to succeed must walk in grace to be made complete. The Spirit of God releases grace to help us complete the work assigned to us. We cannot thrive without the manifestation of His Spirit working through us.

What are the things we must do? First, acknowledge the presence of the Lord in your life. Recognize His place in all things. Second, remember that the grace needed for every stage of your Christian journey comes from the Lord. Third, do not forget to honor the presence of the Lord. Fourth, as you continue to obey God, you will witness miracles. The voice of the Holy Spirit is heard in His teachings—the Word. The Spirit of God is real. What are the things we must not do? Do not grieve the Holy Spirit. When we grieve Him, He withholds His grace. Genesis 6:3 shows us that God's Spirit will not always strive with man.

Grace is a key that can be found and accessed. In these times, it is important to emphasize the things of the Lord so that our lives will carry true meaning. To succeed as a Christian man or woman, you must act in alignment with God's will—and for that, you need the release of grace. Let us stay awake in this season. You cannot insult the Spirit of Grace and go free. We must honor and follow Him in order to be blessed. The Spirit of Grace has been given to us all so that we do not fail. Let us follow His leadership and not fall short in the things of the Lord.

Lesson: The Spirit of Grace is the Spirit of God at work in you, releasing the grace you need for every stage of your journey. Honour Him, obey Him, and do not grieve Him.

Action: Take time today to honor the Holy Spirit. Acknowledge His presence in your life. Ask Him to release the specific grace you need for the assignment in front of you.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Holy Spirit, I honor You as the Spirit of Grace. Release Your grace upon me for every assignment. I will not grieve You. Lead me, and I will follow. Let my life carry true meaning for Your glory.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Romans 13:8 KJV - "Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law."
devotionals.devotional:
Debt is something outstanding and burdensome—its consequences can extend beyond a person's lifetime, affecting children and even future generations. But there are spiritual debts we must pay as believers. These debts require sacrifice, sometimes even giving up our comfort, to ensure they are paid. First, we owe the debt of living for Christ. Jesus paid our ultimate debt on the cross so that we might live for Him. Living for Christ is a debt every believer owes. Second Corinthians 5:14-15 reminds us that Christ died for all so that those who live should no longer live for themselves but for Him.

Second, we owe the debt of loving one another. We are commanded to love our neighbors and show genuine concern for their souls. True love should compel us to bring others to Christ. If your love does not grow to the point where you invite people to know Him, you have fallen short. Romans 13:8-10 says, "Owe no man any thing, but to love one another." Third, we owe a debt toward the lost. Those who do not yet know Christ are "the lost." We must pay our debt to them by preaching the gospel. This is a sacred obligation every Christian carries. Second Corinthians 5:18-19 says that God has given us the ministry of reconciliation.

Why must we preach the gospel to the lost? First, because of the reality of God's love. God's desire is that all people be saved. John 3:16 declares God's love for the world. Second, because of God's anger toward the unrepentant. Those who reject Christ remain under God's wrath because they have ignored His provision for salvation. Third, because of the reality of hell. Hell is real. Those who refuse Christ will face eternal separation from God. Winning souls for Christ requires sacrifice, but no cost is too great when it comes to rescuing people from eternal loss.

Lesson: You owe three spiritual debts: living for Christ, loving one another, and reaching the lost. Pay these debts faithfully, and you will live in God's favor.

Action: Identify one person you know who is not yet saved. Commit to praying for them daily this week and look for an opportunity to share the gospel with them.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I acknowledge my debts to You. I will live for Christ, love my neighbour, and reach the lost. Give me boldness and opportunity to pay these debts faithfully.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Hebrews 11:6 KJV - "But without faith it is impossible to please Him: for he that cometh to God must believe that He is, and that He is a rewarder of them that diligently seek Him."
devotionals.devotional:
Many people live their lives guided by feelings, by what they see, or by what they can reason out. But the life that pleases God is the life of unshakable faith—faith that is strong, consistent, and unbroken. This is the walk of faith God desires for every believer. The Bible makes it clear: "Without faith, it is impossible to please God." When we draw back from a life of faith, we displease Him. But if you are born again, God has already given you a measure of faith. The challenge is to develop and strengthen it until it becomes unshakable.

There are certain victories and levels of breakthrough in life that you cannot attain until your faith matures. Scripture tells us that "faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the Word of God." The more we expose ourselves to the Word, the stronger our faith becomes. On the other hand, neglecting the Word keeps our faith weak and ineffective. Let us examine the states of faith. Little faith produces little results. If God has called you to nations, little faith cannot fulfill that assignment. You must grow your faith to match the vision God has given you. Weak faith can be weakened by wrong influences and careless hearing. Be mindful of what you listen to. Only the Word of God can feed and strengthen faith. Failing faith needs support from the Word and consistent practice. Dead faith is faith without works or expression.

If your faith is unshakable, it will show. It will be seen in the works you do, the victories you win, and the breakthroughs you experience. Therefore, feed your faith daily with the Word of God, guard what you hear, and put your faith into action. Then your life will truly reflect the unshakable faith that is the key to every breakthrough.

Lesson: Faith must be developed from little to unshakable. Feed it with the Word, guard it from wrong influences, and put it into action. Unshakable faith produces unshakable results.

Action: Assess the state of your faith today. Is it little, weak, failing, or dead? Commit to feeding your faith daily through God's Word and taking one step of faith this week.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, grow my faith until it is unshakable. I feed my faith on Your Word. I refuse to be moved by circumstances. I believe You are a rewarder of those who diligently seek You.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Corinthians 4:2 KJV - "Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful."
devotionals.devotional:
Our calling as Christians is primarily individual rather than communal. Each of us will give account of our faith life personally. The full proof of our Christianity is seen in the report of our faith before God. To obtain a good report from God, there are two key areas to consider: what to avoid and what must be. What must we avoid? We must avoid eye-service. Eye-service means doing things only to be seen or praised by people. It has destroyed the integrity of many believers. Anyone who engages in eye-service is a hypocrite and cannot be trusted. Such people are not conscious of the presence of God but of men. They focus on themselves and serve for self-interest, not for God. Our call is to selfless service, not self-service.

What must be is faithfulness. Faithfulness is doing everything as unto the Lord. It is Jesus plus or minus nothing—Jesus alone. It is serving with singleness of heart. It is diligence in carrying out the work of the Lord in our ministry. "Whatsoever you do, do it heartily, as to the Lord." Faithfulness is God-focused, not men-focused. It is living in awareness that God sees us at all times. It means being diligent, sincere, and truthful. "A faithful witness will not lie: but a false witness will utter lies."

Moses is an example of a faithful servant of God. God Himself testified that Moses was faithful in all His house. This is the kind of report every believer should strive to obtain. To obtain a good report from God, avoid eye-service and self-centered service. Embrace faithfulness—serve with sincerity, diligence, and singleness of heart, as unto the Lord. This is the pathway to having God's commendation over our lives and ministries.

Lesson: A good report from God comes to those who avoid eye-service and embrace faithfulness. Serve as unto the Lord, not to be seen by men.

Action: Examine your motives in serving God today. Are you serving to be seen or to please God? Repent of any eye-service and recommit to faithful, heart-felt service.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, deliver me from eye-service. Let me serve You faithfully, knowing that You see all I do. Help me to work heartily as unto You, not to be seen by men.

devotionals.memoryVerse: John 15:14 KJV - "Ye are My friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you."
devotionals.devotional:
Those who will be saved during the tribulation will pay with their blood because they hold the testimony of Jesus. Today, we still have freedom and privileges to live and work as Christians, but in the tribulation it will be extremely difficult. Those left behind will face severe persecution and hardship. If they survive, it will be because they have kept the testimony of Jesus. Keeping the testimony of Jesus is both a command from Him and the desire of God. If your focus is the rapture, then you must keep the testimony of Jesus. Right now, it is easier to obey the commandments of Jesus because we are in the time of grace, but after the rapture that time of grace will be over.

Keeping the commandment of the Lord is wisdom. Everything we do should align with the Word of God—this is wisdom; not doing so is foolishness. God will judge not only our actions but also our motives. Therefore, even our thoughts must be subject to God's commandments. His commandments should be our lifestyle. During the tribulation there will be no one to tell people about Jesus. Yet those who are saved in that time will still keep His commandments. The testimony of Jesus is not merely recounting what He has done for you personally. It is living in the reality of what Jesus came for, lived for, and died for. Those who are saved will have this consciousness; you also must live with this consciousness.

We need to review our Christianity today and focus on the most important things: what Christ came for, lived for, and died for—even in the face of severe opposition. This is true steadfastness and faithfulness. In these days opposition will increase, and we must be prepared. Anyone who has been with Christ will bear witness and have His testimony. Many today lack the testimony of Christ because they have not truly been with Him. God told Paul in Acts 23:11 that just as he had testified about Him before, he would continue to do so. Likewise, we must testify about Christ wherever we go—whether in politics, business, wealth, or poverty. We must live as Christians everywhere and have the testimony of Jesus.

Lesson: The testimony of Jesus is not just what He has done for you but living in the reality of who He is and what He came for. Keep His commandments and live His testimony.

Action: Review your Christian life today. Are you merely recounting past testimonies, or are you living the testimony of Jesus now? Ask God to make His testimony evident in your daily life.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, let the testimony of Jesus be evident in my life. Help me to keep Your commandments and live in the reality of what You came for, lived for, and died for.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Philippians 4:19 KJV - "But my God shall supply all your need according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus."
devotionals.devotional:
God has promised to supply the needs of His people, and there shall be no lack. Divine provision covers every area of life—whether it is security, finances, health, peace, or opportunities—God is more than able to provide. God's resources are inexhaustible; no generation can ever run Him dry. He meets our needs, not according to our efforts or abilities, but according to His riches in glory by Christ Jesus. God's ways of providing are often unique and peculiar to each person. For example, when Jesus needed to feed the five thousand, He did not buy food—He multiplied the little that was available. In the same way, God can multiply what seems insufficient in your life.

Your part is to believe the Word of God, stay connected to Him, and be confident that He will provide. God always goes ahead of His people. He has already gone ahead of us, making crooked paths straight and releasing treasures of provision. Isaiah 45:2-3 declares that God will go before us and make the crooked places straight. The nature of God is rooted in love and care. He provides for both our physical and spiritual needs. That is why He is called Jehovah Jireh—the Lord Will Provide. At Mount Moriah, God foresaw Abraham's need and provided ahead of time. That is God's nature: He provides before the need arises.

In Luke 22:35, when Jesus sent out His disciples to preach, He told them to go without purse or bag. When they returned, He asked them, "Did you lack anything?" and they answered, "Nothing." This shows that when we are committed to God's work—especially in preaching the gospel—He ensures we lack nothing. We should not limit ourselves or depend on men. Instead, we must build strong faith in the God who provides. God calls us to focus on Him, not on human sources. In Matthew 6:33, Jesus teaches us to seek first the Kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto us.

Lesson: God is Jehovah Jireh, your faithful provider. He goes ahead of you, knows your needs, and supplies them according to His riches, not your efforts.

Action: Identify a need you have been worrying about. Release it to God today in prayer. Thank Him in advance for His provision, and trust that He has already gone ahead of you.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Jehovah Jireh, my Provider, I thank You that You go ahead of me. You know my needs before I ask. I trust You to supply all my need according to Your riches in glory by Christ Jesus.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Hebrews 13:8 KJV - "Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever."
devotionals.devotional:
Every good and perfect gift comes from God. God Himself defines what is good. Every good thing you have ever experienced did not happen by chance—it came from Him. He is the Father of lights. The sun still rises every morning—that is how consistent God is. He does not grow old or fade away. In the same way, the God who provided in the past will do it again. There is no variation or shadow of turning with Him. He is ever consistent! That is why the Bible says, "Jesus Christ, the same yesterday, today, and forever." God shows no favoritism. What He does for one, He can also do for another.

God knows our needs and has the capacity to provide them—even when we do not know them ourselves. Matthew 6:32 tells us that our heavenly Father knows we have need of all these things. God's provision covers every area—physical, mental, and spiritual. His provision is as consistent as light. All we need is faith. Second Peter 1:4 tells us that God has given us exceedingly great and precious promises. God's abundance is inexhaustible. His supply never runs dry. God is the source, and Jesus is the channel of His provision. To truly know God, we must know Christ. Outside Christ, we cannot experience the fullness of God's provision. This knowledge is experiential—it is a relationship with God that others can see in our lives.

God provides for us so that we can provide for others and support His kingdom work. If we want to access more of God's blessings, we must have a heart to bless others. Genesis 12:2 says God blessed Abraham so that he would be a blessing. Malachi 3:10-11 promises that God will open the windows of heaven and rebuke the devourer for those who bring their tithes into the storehouse. Our blessings are for the work of God. Finally, add virtue to your faith. Virtue means having the right attitude in life. Remember, the promises of God are the inheritance of the saints—not for unbelievers.

Lesson: God is consistent and faithful. He provided yesterday, He provides today, and He will provide tomorrow. His provision is for you and also for others through you.

Action: Identify one way God has provided for you in the past. Thank Him for His faithfulness. Then ask Him how you can be a channel of provision to someone else this week.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Father of lights, thank You for Your consistent provision. You are the same yesterday, today, and forever. Use me as a channel of Your provision to bless others and advance Your kingdom.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Exodus 15:26 KJV - "For I am the LORD that healeth thee."
devotionals.devotional:
One of the wonderful provisions of God for His children is healing—healing that covers every area of life: physical, spiritual, emotional, and psychological. He is Jehovah Rapha, the Lord who heals. When the Israelites faced bitter water on their journey to the Promised Land, God healed the water and made it sweet. In the same way, while we journey through life, we may encounter bitter experiences and painful situations—but our God is still able to heal and make things sweet again. God is not moved by our worries or tears but by our prayer of faith. Moses prayed, and God gave him direction. He did not just cry; he sought God for a solution. Likewise, God sometimes opens our eyes to see the solution to our challenges.

Prayer is not measured by how much we cry, but by how much we listen to God for His direction. Let us be a people who not only pray but also hear from the Lord. When Moses obeyed God's instruction, the bitter water became sweet. In the same way, God can give us divine instructions that will make our lives sweet again. Jehovah Rapha is an all-round healer—there is no limit to what He can restore. Verse 25 shows that God tested the Israelites' faith, and sometimes He tests ours too. May we be found faithful and genuine before Him.

In verse 26, God declares, "I am the Lord who heals you." Make this personal—say, "He is my healer." The tree Moses cast into the water is a symbol of Christ. Just as that tree turned bitterness into sweetness, the Cross of Christ turns every bitter situation into joy. Whatever you are facing today, bring the Cross into it—Christ will make it sweet. Because of what Jesus did on the Cross, no situation is too hard or too old for Him to change.

Lesson: Jehovah Rapha is your healer—physical, emotional, and spiritual. Bring your bitter situations to the cross, and He will make them sweet.

Action: Identify one area of bitterness or pain in your life today. Bring it to Jesus in prayer. Thank Him that He is your healer and trust Him to make it sweet.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Jehovah Rapha, You are my Healer. I bring every bitter situation to the cross of Christ. Heal me, make me whole, and turn my bitterness into sweetness. I trust You as my all-round healer.

devotionals.topic: Faith in God for Divine Provision
devotionals.memoryVerse: Luke 6:38 KJV - "Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom."
devotionals.devotional:
Our walk with God is a walk of faith—it is you and your God. Christianity is personal; our relationship with God is on an individual basis. David declared, "The Lord is my Shepherd; I shall not want." He said my Shepherd—not anyone else's. This means every believer must have a personal faith that works for them. Our Christian life is shaped by our individual faith in God. Whoever has faith has it for himself, and that faith glorifies and honors God. Faith must express itself in obedience to God. The Bible says, "Faith without works is dead." If your faith is not producing results, it is dead. Faith demands obedience. God wants us to obey Him.

Giving is an expression of faith. Giving strengthens the believer and is an act of praise and worship. We worship God through our giving. There is no way the Kingdom of God can grow without giving. Giving helps us meet needs in the church and reminds us that we are accountable to God, our Provider. When we give, we acknowledge that God is our source. If we must receive divine provision, we must also learn to give. What should we give? First, ourselves to God—make Him your Lord and Savior. If you cannot give yourself to God, you cannot truly give your money or resources to Him. "They first gave themselves to the Lord." Once you surrender yourself to God, there is nothing else you cannot give Him. Second, our resources. Everything God has blessed us with should be used to glorify Him.

The benefits of giving are many. It strengthens our faith in the God of provision. It builds confidence that He will bless us with more. It shows our commitment—true giving touches our pockets. Every giving is a seed. "He that waters shall himself be watered." It attracts divine blessings and brings eternal rewards—we have a store in heaven. Faith in God is not complete without obedience and giving. When we give ourselves and our resources to God, He releases His divine provision in abundance. Remember: "The just shall live by faith."

Lesson: Giving is an act of faith and worship. When you give yourself and your resources to God, you position yourself to receive His divine provision.

Action: Identify a giving opportunity this week—whether to your local church, a ministry, or someone in need. Give with a joyful heart as an act of faith and worship.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I give myself to You first. I trust You as my Provider. I will give cheerfully and faithfully, knowing that You will supply all my need according to Your riches in glory.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Matthew 28:19 KJV - "Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."
devotionals.devotional:
Mission is the driving force behind everything we do. We have a calling, and we also have understanding of that calling. The National Evangelical Mission is part of the "company" mentioned in Psalm 68:11—a company that proclaims and publishes God's Word. You are part of this divine company. This mission will continue until its finishing point: the return of Jesus Christ. Mission originates from God, but it has been entrusted to us. We take responsibility for the mission and we embrace the Great Commission. We do not see it as something given merely to the church structure, but something God has personally committed into our hands. If no one accepts responsibility for this work, it will remain undone. Even if others neglect it, you must rise to the responsibility.

In the National Evangelical Mission, we place missions at the center. Think of it this way: if you worked in a secular company and you truly embraced your role, you would never act in a way that would cause the company to collapse. The same principle applies to the company of God. God has a mission—to reach the world through Christ—and He works through us to accomplish it. In Ezekiel 1:1-3, God's vision became effective when Ezekiel understood it. Our vision must align with God's vision. Our message is the message of the vision of God. Christ established the Church to be the instrument that advances mission—to raise disciples and prepare people for God's work.

Jesus warned in Matthew 24:4-5 that we must guard ourselves against deception. One major sign of this deception is developing a maintenance mentality—a mindset focused only on keeping members rather than engaging them in mission. We emphasize missions so we do not become a church that stops raising people for God's work. We also hold missions high so that our love for God remains fervent and alive. Mission is the heartbeat of God until Christ returns. In Acts 13:1-3, we see God preparing and preserving His people for purpose. God is preserving you for a purpose.

Lesson: Mission is the heartbeat of God. You are part of the divine company called to proclaim His Word. Do not fall into a maintenance mentality—stay on mission until Jesus returns.

Action: Identify one way you can actively participate in missions this month—whether through prayer, giving, or going. Commit to it and ask God to ignite missionary passion in your heart.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I embrace the mission You have given to the Church. I am part of the company that proclaims Your Word. Keep my love for You fervent and my focus on missions until Jesus returns.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 100:4 KJV - "Enter into His gates with thanksgiving, and into His courts with praise: be thankful unto Him, and bless His name."
devotionals.devotional:
There is something called protocol. In every system—government, organizations, and even in the church—there are people known as protocol officers. Protocol is a system of rules, guidelines, and procedures that dictate how actions should be carried out. Before anyone can see a governor, they must follow certain protocols. God also has protocols. In Judges 1:1-2, when the Israelites inquired of God concerning the battle, He showed them the right procedure to follow. He said, "Judah shall go up first." God Himself established the order. Judah was one of the sons of Jacob, born to Leah. Among all her children, God had special interest in Judah, because it was through his lineage that Christ would come—Jesus, the Lion of the Tribe of Judah.

The principle here is simple: in everything we do, let praise go first. Praise is the spiritual protocol that opens doors and grants us access. Every time you want God to move, let Judah go first—that is, let praise and thanksgiving come before anything else. The word thanksgiving is made up of two words: thanks and giving. Both are essential. Thanks (praise) is not entertainment. It is not the part we rush through. It is protocol. Whenever you kneel down to pray, start with thanksgiving. There are many things God has done, and continues to do, that deserve thanks. The divine order is thanksgiving, then prayer. Even when you find yourself in trouble, begin with thanksgiving.

Giving is also part of thanksgiving. When you give, the Scripture says "it shall be given back to you." Giving does not take you to heaven, but it blesses you on earth. It positions you for God's favor. Whatever you give to God should cost you something. Do not give carelessly or without preparation. Plan and prepare your thanksgiving offering. Thanksgiving follows divine protocol. Let praise go first. Let giving follow. And in everything you do, always remember: God responds when Judah goes first.

Lesson: Thanksgiving is not optional—it is divine protocol. Let praise go first in your prayers, and let giving follow. God responds when Judah goes first.

Action: Before you pray your next prayer, spend time in genuine thanksgiving. List five things you are grateful for and thank God for them. Then bring your requests.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I enter Your gates with thanksgiving and Your courts with praise. I give You thanks for who You are and what You have done. Let my praise go first, and then my requests.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Philippians 4:6-7 KJV - "Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God."
devotionals.devotional:
God wants us as believers to be thankful to Him. We should be doing this from time to time as an act of worship. It is an expression of faith in the God we serve. This is expected to be our lifestyle. When we thank God, it is an expression that we love Him enough to give Him thanks. There are different attitudes of people toward thanksgiving. Some never give God thanks. All they think about is what God would do for them. They do not think about being rich toward God. Many live like the man in Luke 12:16-21. They do not have any place for God; they only think about themselves. They think that what they have gotten is because of their might or strength or ability. This should not be our attitude.

Some are hypocritical in their approach. When we talk about thanksgiving, we talk of genuine thanksgiving. Others come genuinely. We do not complain or approach thanksgiving with complaint. When you complain, you will be overwhelmed. Psalm 77:3 shows us that complaining leads to being overwhelmed. Thanksgiving should be your habit. It should be your lifestyle. It should be an act of faith. If you do not live by faith, you are committing sin. Romans 14:23 tells us that whatever is not of faith is sin. It is also an act of worship. As long as you live, you should worship God. Colossians 3:17 says, "Whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by Him." Psalm 100:4 instructs us to enter His gates with thanksgiving.

When we thank God, it gives us strength. God gives us strength and peace that passes all understanding when we thank Him. Philippians 4:6-7 promises that the peace of God, which passes all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus. Do not approach God with complaints. Do not be hypocritical. Come genuinely with thanksgiving as your lifestyle, your act of faith, and your act of worship. You will receive strength and peace beyond understanding.

Lesson: Thanksgiving is not a one-time event but a lifestyle. It is an act of faith and worship that brings strength and peace.

Action: Starting today, make thanksgiving your daily habit. Before you complain about anything, find something to thank God for. Let gratitude become your first response.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I choose to be a thankful believer. Forgive me for my complaints and hypocrisy. I make thanksgiving my lifestyle, my act of faith, and my act of worship. Thank You for Your goodness.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Proverbs 11:25 KJV - "The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself."
devotionals.devotional:
Here is a secret of wisdom: if you believe Jehovah is God of the universe and the Bible is true, then you must embrace this truth—generosity pays. If you are liberal in your giving to the Lord and to the poor, He will pay you back liberally. God can outgive you more easily than you can imagine. This proverb is closely connected to the one before it, which reads, "There is that scattereth, and yet increaseth; and there is that withholdeth more than is meet, but it tendeth to poverty" (Proverbs 11:24). Throwing away your money—to the right causes in the name of God—will bring increase. Restraining your giving will reduce you to poverty.

God has been very generous to mankind, and He rewards men that show a similar generosity to others. You can get ahead financially by learning to give generously, for the Lord will abundantly bless you. This wisdom is too high for any business school or economics class in the world, for they reject the existence of God and His supernatural impact on finances. God has blessed you. So you should give liberally to the poor. God carefully observes your giving and will treat you accordingly. Paul wrote, "He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully" (2 Corinthians 9:6).

R. G. LeTourneau, the Christian businessman who gave 90% of his income to the Lord, prospered by this arrangement. It is impossible to outgive God. A strong evidence of a righteous man is his generous spirit in giving to others. If you take care of those needing financial help, the Lord will take care of you. Every time there is an opportunity to give to God, to the poor, or to compensate someone working for you, give more than average. Many reason that they cannot afford to give—they say they will give generously once they get ahead—but this is perverse reasoning. You will not get ahead until after you become a generous giver.

Lesson: Generosity is not a loss but an investment. God sees your giving and promises to reward you abundantly. You cannot outgive God.

Action: Identify an opportunity to give today—to your church, to the poor, or to someone in need. Give generously and cheerfully, trusting God to repay you.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I choose to be a generous giver. Help me to give liberally and cheerfully, trusting that You will supply all my needs according to Your riches in glory.

devotionals.topic: What It Means to Be Victorious
devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Corinthians 12:9 KJV - "My grace is sufficient for thee: for My strength is made perfect in weakness."
devotionals.devotional:
To thrive in life, we must seek God's perspective, surrender to His will, and trust Him to provide what we truly need. In 2 Corinthians 12:9-10, Paul learned the secret of how to be triumphant: maintain God's perspective on the ups and downs of life, and depend on His power. The apostle was firmly convinced that having the person of the Holy Spirit living in him meant that God's power was available to him. And it is available for us too today and always. The first step is to believe God's power is within us through the presence of His Spirit. We must accept that God's priority is to transform us into His image, and not necessarily to provide comfortable circumstances.

Diligently seeking to maintain Jesus' perspective on hardships is also important. Jesus said in John 16:33, "In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world." Having embraced these truths, we can learn to depend on divine power. The key lies in submitting our will to the Lord's. Then, instead of reacting to life, we will respond on the basis of His will. Yielding control to the Holy Spirit will help us accept the Father's pattern for how His children are to live. When we can say, "Lord, whatever You choose to send will be all right with me," then we will experience the inner peace Christ promised us.

The victorious life is not about the absence of problems but about the presence of God's power in the midst of them. When you stop fighting your circumstances and start surrendering to God's will, you will discover a peace that passes all understanding. Divine perspective, surrender, and firm faith—these are the ingredients for the victorious life. You may still face challenges, but you will face them differently. You will face them with confidence, knowing that the same power that raised Christ from the dead lives in you.

Lesson: Victory is not found in comfortable circumstances but in depending on God's power and maintaining His perspective. Surrender is the key to triumph.

Action: Identify one area where you have been reacting to life rather than responding in faith. Surrender that area to God today and ask for His perspective and power.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I surrender my will to You. Whatever You choose to send will be all right with me. Let Your power be made perfect in my weakness. I choose to respond, not react, to life.

devotionals.topic: God's Delay Is Not His Denial
devotionals.memoryVerse: Matthew 7:7 KJV - "Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you."
devotionals.devotional:
Have you ever prayed and felt like God is saying "no" to your prayer? How do you feel thereafter? When your request is placed side by side with God's promises, do you feel God is not being honest with His promises, or do you resign to "His will," thinking He is not inclined to answer your request? God is true to His word. Every prayer of a child of God that passes the test of James 4:3 is answered, but sometimes the timeline of the answer may not be as we want. For example, consider the story of the transfiguration of Christ. Have you ever considered that it was the answer to Moses' prayer after more than 1,500 years?

In Exodus 33:17-23, Moses prayed and asked God to allow him to see His face, but God turned down that request. In Deuteronomy 3:23-27, God also denied his request to enter Canaan because He was angry with him over his disobedience. But as a loving Father and in keeping to His promises, God answered Moses' requests in His own time. During the transfiguration, Moses saw God's face and glory in Christ and also entered Canaan in his physical body. Think about it! God is not limited by time, space, and events as we know them. He is open to answering your requests in His time. His delay is not His denial.

Do not stop making your requests, even when you think He will say no to it. The enemy wants you to give up just before your breakthrough. Remember Abraham waited twenty-five years for Isaac. Joseph waited thirteen years for his dream to be fulfilled. The woman with the issue of blood waited twelve years. But in every case, God showed up at the perfect time. Your situation is not forgotten. Your prayer has not been ignored. God is working behind the scenes, orchestrating everything for your good and His glory. Keep praying. Keep believing. Keep trusting.

Lesson: God's timing is not our timing, but He is always faithful. Delay does not mean denial. Keep trusting, keep praying, and keep believing.

Action: Identify one prayer request you have given up on. Revive it today. Write it down and commit to praying about it again, trusting God's perfect timing.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Thank You Lord that You hear me when I pray. Irrespective of the delay in the answer to my prayers, help me to continue trusting that You will answer me.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Hebrews 11:6 KJV - "But without faith it is impossible to please Him: for he that cometh to God must believe that He is, and that He is a rewarder of them that diligently seek Him."
devotionals.devotional:
When you feel shaken, remember these unchanging truths about God. Our faith is not built on feelings or wishful thinking—it rests on something far more solid. Let us look at seven foundational aspects of Christianity. First, God is. Faith must be built on the simple confession that the Lord is real. He exists and is indeed God. Second, God is love. He is intimately concerned with your life and wants to engage in a relationship with you. Third, God is just. His justice is absolutely perfect—even when He lovingly disciplines us.

Fourth, God is all-knowing. He knows your heart, your pain, and your questions. You cannot shock or surprise Him. Fifth, God is everywhere. You never have to wonder where He is. Wherever you are, He is right by your side. Sixth, God is all-powerful. There is nothing greater than God. Regardless of how enormous your challenges and heartaches seem to be, you can overcome them in His power. Seventh, God is faithful. No matter how far you stray, He never gives up on you. Whatever you have done, He will always welcome you home.

When doubts arise or circumstances shake you, return to these truths. They are solid and unchanging. Your feelings will fluctuate. Your circumstances will change. But God remains the same yesterday, today, and forever. Build your life on this foundation, and you will not be moved. When the storms of life come—and they will come—you will stand firm because your house is built on the rock. Do not let your emotions dictate your theology. Let the unchanging character of God be the anchor for your soul.

Lesson: When circumstances shake you, return to the unchanging truths about God. He is, He loves, He is just, He knows, He is everywhere, He is all-powerful, and He is faithful.

Action: Write down these seven truths about God. When doubt or fear arises this week, read them aloud and confess them over your situation.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, when I feel shaken, help me remember who You are. You are real, loving, just, all-knowing, everywhere, all-powerful, and faithful. I build my life on these unchanging truths.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Mark 14:6 KJV - "Let her alone; why trouble ye her? she hath wrought a good work on Me."
devotionals.devotional:
While Jesus was in Bethany, reclining at the table in the home of Simon the Leper, a woman came with an alabaster jar of very expensive perfume, made of pure nard. She broke the jar and poured the perfume on His head. What a beautiful and wild display of love! While Jesus was relaxing, this woman came to Him and poured out everything she had. Many people saw her display and were bothered and confused. How could she behave in such a way? What was she thinking? She was publicly rebuked and lectured. Then Jesus responded. He knew exactly what she was doing.

She sacrificed her expensive perfume made of pure nard. She was not wasting the perfume. She was prophetically pouring it on Him to prepare for His burial because between His death and burial there would be no time to do that. She was pouring out her love to Him. Jesus endorsed her and edified her. He responded with love. As we reflect on this, we receive the same invitation to pour out our love on Jesus. What sacrifices can we make today out of our love for Him? We may look foolish and be misunderstood. However, Jesus always understands our sacrifices of love to Him. It is not about what others think of us, but what He thinks.

How can you pour out love on Him today? Perhaps through an act of worship, a financial sacrifice, or a service rendered in secret. Perhaps by forgiving someone who has hurt you or by sharing your faith with a lost soul. The woman gave what was most precious to her. What is your alabaster jar? What is your pure nard? Whatever it is, pour it out on Jesus. He sees it. He values it. He will defend you against every critic. Your sacrifice of love is never wasted.

Lesson: True love for Jesus is often misunderstood by others, but He sees and values every sacrifice we make for Him. Pour out your love on Him without fear.

Action: Identify one sacrifice you can make today to show your love for Jesus—whether time, money, or an act of service. Do it with joy, caring more about His opinion than others'.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, thank You for Your sacrificial love. Help me love like You. Help me care more about Your heart than the opinions of others. Give me boldness and courage to pour out my love on You.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Corinthians 10:31 KJV - "Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God."
devotionals.devotional:
When God opens doors for His people, those open doors always come with responsibilities. Why does God open doors for His people? First, for His glory. God opens doors primarily for His own glory, not for our selfish purposes. Isaiah 43:7 reminds us that we were created for His glory. Every opportunity, promotion, connection, or breakthrough is meant to bring honor to Him. It is for His kingdom purpose to be fulfilled through you. God has a reason for planting you in that business, in that family, in that office, and in every place you find yourself. He wants His agenda to be accomplished through your life.

Second, as an expression of His abounding love. Open doors are a demonstration of God's love toward us. They show that He cares, provides, and makes a way for His children. Third, so we can become a blessing to others. In Genesis 12:1-2, God told Abraham that He would bless him and make him a blessing. God does not bless us to store up blessings for ourselves; He blesses us so that we can bless others. The question is: How much of a blessing are you to others through the doors God has opened for you? Fourth, as evidence of His abiding presence. Fifth, as proof of God's power.

What is required of us? Be ready to glorify God. Do not be selfish with open doors. Preach the Gospel. Open doors are opportunities to share the Good News. Continue in prayer. Pray that the doors God has opened will remain open and that more doors will be opened. Use open doors to advance the Kingdom of God. Psalm 35:27 reminds us that the Lord delights in the prosperity of His servants, but that prosperity must be used to advance His Kingdom and promote His righteousness. Every open door is a stewardship. Use it wisely.

Lesson: Open doors from God are not for our selfish purposes but for His glory, for us to be a blessing, and for the advancement of His Kingdom.

Action: Identify one open door in your life currently. Ask God: How can I use this for Your glory and to bless others? Take one step to act on His answer.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, thank You for the doors You have opened for me. Help me to use them for Your glory, to be a blessing to others, and to advance Your Kingdom. I will not be selfish with Your blessings.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Luke 11:9 KJV - "And I say unto you, Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you."
devotionals.devotional:
How will we continue to enjoy the doors that God has opened for us? The blessings of God are conditional. There are requirements that must be met for those blessings to continue in our lives. God can open doors, and He can also shut doors for our safety and preservation. Therefore, there are expectations from us—there are keys we must apply. As it is written in Matthew 16:19, God has given us keys in the Kingdom. To continue enjoying open doors, we must do the following: have an open heart, an open mouth, and an open hand.

First, an open heart. We must open our hearts to God. We cannot enjoy open doors when our hearts are closed to Him. Hebrews 3:8,15 warns us not to harden our hearts. An open heart invites divine direction, revelation, and continued access to God's blessings. Second, an open mouth. We must have an open mouth—to praise, to preach, and to pray. Praise is a spiritual matter. You praise whether it is convenient or not. Praise is a spiritual weapon used in spiritual warfare. In the Christian race, praise is not optional; it is essential. We must also preach. Furthermore, our mouths must be open in prayer at all times and everywhere. An open mouth keeps heaven's doors open.

Third, an open hand. This speaks about giving. If you do not open your hand in giving and supporting the work of God, you cannot expect open doors to remain. Luke 6:38 teaches that giving activates receiving. An open hand attracts divine supply and sustained favor. When God opens a door, it is our responsibility to maintain the posture that keeps that door open. Open heart. Open mouth. Open hand. May we remain faithful in these keys so that the doors God has opened for us will remain open.

Lesson: To keep God's doors open, maintain an open heart toward God, an open mouth in praise and prayer, and an open hand in giving.

Action: Evaluate yourself today: Is your heart open to God? Is your mouth open in praise and prayer? Is your hand open in giving? Adjust where needed.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, keep my heart open to You, my mouth open in praise and prayer, and my hand open in giving. Let the doors You have opened for me remain open for Your glory.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Isaiah 40:31 KJV - "But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint."
devotionals.devotional:
This is a season of divine strength. Deuteronomy 33:24-25 says, "As your days, so shall your strength be." In the world, you are considered stronger when you are young. But before God, you become stronger as you grow older. Divine strength is not dependent on age; it is dependent on God. We need divine strength in the face of challenges. Joshua 14:10-12 shows us Caleb at eighty-five years old declaring that his strength was still the same as when he was forty-five years old. That was not ordinary strength; it was the strength of the Lord at work in his life. Psalm 28:8 tells us, "The Lord is the strength of His people."

We need the strength of the Lord in everything we do and in everything we are called to do. Isaiah 40:28-29 reminds us that every strength we need comes from God. This strength may not only come in physical ability; it can also come through wisdom and knowledge to do what we ought to do. We must believe God to make our lives and ministry result-oriented. Without divine strength, effort alone will not produce lasting results. Why does God give us strength? To fulfill divine purpose. God is the ultimate Creator, and He has made us secondary creators. He has given us all things, but we must create and build what we need to use.

The strength of God makes the supernatural possible in your life. It empowers you to do what is beyond your natural capacity. Psalm 103:5 says our strength is like that of the eagle that renews. God specializes in renewing strength when it seems exhausted. Philippians 4:13 declares, "I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me." Whatever is required in your life, God will give you the strength to accomplish it. As we wait on Him, we receive the strength needed to make things happen. God has the power to strengthen the weak and sustain those who trust in Him.

Lesson: Divine strength is not dependent on age but on God. He renews our strength daily and empowers us to fulfill His purpose.

Action: Identify one area where you feel weak or exhausted. Pray specifically for God's divine strength in that area. Trust Him to renew your strength today.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, You are the strength of my life. Renew my strength today. As my days, so shall my strength be. I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Colossians 3:13 KJV - "Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye."
devotionals.devotional:
Forgiveness means letting go of anger, resentment, or the desire to punish someone who has wronged you. It is the decision to release the offense and not keep it in your heart. It does not mean the wrong never happened. It simply means you refuse to hold the offense against the person anymore. In simple terms, forgiveness is releasing someone from the debt of the wrong they did to you. Forbearance means patiently enduring someone's behavior, weakness, or faults without reacting with anger. It is when a person has been doing the same thing for a long time—what he did three years ago, he did last year, he did yesterday, and he is still doing it today. Yet instead of reacting with anger, bitterness, or revenge, you choose to remain patient and control yourself.

The difference between forgiveness and forbearance is important. Forbearance has to do with patiently tolerating people's behavior and weaknesses over time. Forgiveness has to do with releasing the hurt and offense caused by what someone has done. Forbearance controls how you react to people, while forgiveness cleans your heart after you have been hurt. Both are necessary for peaceful relationships and spiritual maturity. Without forgiveness, your heart becomes a prison of bitterness. Without forbearance, every minor irritation becomes a major explosion.

As Christians, we are called to both forgive and forbear. Forgive as Christ forgave you—freely, completely, and without condition. Forbear with one another in love, recognizing that you also have weaknesses that others must tolerate. The world will tell you to hold grudges and demand your rights. But the Spirit tells you to forgive and forbear. Which voice will you obey? Choose the path of peace. Choose the path of love. Choose to forgive. Choose to forbear.

Lesson: Forgiveness releases the debt of wrongs done to you. Forbearance patiently endures repeated weaknesses. Both are essential for peace and spiritual maturity.

Action: Identify one person you need to forgive and one person whose weaknesses you need to forbear. Take a step today toward releasing offense and extending patience.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, help me to forgive as You have forgiven me. Give me the grace to forbear with those who repeatedly fail me. Let my heart be free from bitterness and my reactions be full of patience.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 144:1 KJV - "Blessed be the LORD my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight."
devotionals.devotional:
We are saved to do God's assignment. The assignment of God cannot be done by ordinary strength but by the strength of the Lord. By the strength of man, no one can go anywhere in this world. The strength of God helps us in our Christian life. As Christians, we are to recognize the strength of God in our lives. Victory comes through the strength of the Lord. Victory is recognized when the strength of God is acknowledged. There is no strength anywhere in the world except from God. God does not just strengthen us, but He trains us so that the strength of the Lord will run in us.

We can do nothing without the strength of the Lord. The strength of the Lord must be practiced in our lives. The Word of God is what makes us strengthened and trained. God sends trials in order to train His children. There is an assignment for every child of God. God prepares us and trains us in order to be strengthened. God will not use people who are not proven. God's intention and desire is to strengthen us. His interest is that His strength will be released for us. You have an assignment and a war for you to fight. God trains us for the days of war and fighting.

The trials you are facing are not punishments; they are training grounds. Every difficulty is developing your spiritual muscles. Every challenge is teaching you to depend on God's strength rather than your own. Do not despise the training. Do not run from the battle. Instead, embrace it as God's classroom. He is teaching your hands to war and your fingers to fight. He is preparing you for victories you cannot yet imagine. Trust the process. Trust the Trainer. His strength is being perfected in your weakness.

Lesson: God does not just give you strength; He trains you through trials so that His strength becomes operative in your life. Every challenge is preparation for greater victory.

Action: Thank God for a current trial or challenge. Ask Him what He is training you for through it. Trust that He is strengthening you for future battles.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, You are my strength. Train my hands for war and my fingers for battle. I receive every trial as training. Prepare me for the victories You have planned for me.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 84:7 KJV - "They go from strength to strength, every one of them in Zion appeareth before God."
devotionals.devotional:
The strength referred to here is not human strength. In the journey of faith, human strength alone cannot carry us through. As believers, we do not necessarily pray for an easy life; rather, we ask God for the strength to carry us through the challenges of life. God has already promised to give us that strength. In 2 Samuel 3:1, we see a contrast between the house of David and the house of Saul. The house of David was growing stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul was becoming weaker and weaker. This shows that divine strength can increase or decrease depending on our relationship with God.

Similarly, in 2 Corinthians 12:9, God made it clear that His grace is sufficient and that His strength is made perfect in weakness. In Acts 9:22, the Bible tells us that Paul increased in strength as he carried out his ministry. In the same way, God will also increase our strength so that we can succeed in life and in His service. When a person has divine strength, frustration cannot easily overcome them. Psalm 84:7 tells us that those who are in Zion go from strength to strength. As believers, God expects us to grow stronger spiritually every day.

How does God increase our strength? First, through the power of the Holy Ghost. In Isaiah 11:2, the Bible speaks about the Spirit of might. The strength of God has the capacity to increase in our lives. Second, through having a good relationship with God. Knowing God experientially opens the door for His strength. Third, through commitment to service. As we commit ourselves to serving God, He releases various kinds of strength. Fourth, through a strong and committed prayer life. Fifth, through dedication to hearing, reading, and obeying the Word of God. Always remember that no one can go far in life without the strength that comes from God.

Lesson: Divine strength can increase or decrease. To grow from strength to strength, cultivate your relationship with God through prayer, His Word, service, and the Holy Spirit.

Action: Identify which of the five ways to increase strength you have been neglecting. Commit to one specific practice this week to see your strength increase.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, increase my strength. I go from strength to strength by Your Spirit. Through prayer, Your Word, service, and a right relationship with You, let Your power grow in my life.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 145:4 KJV - "One generation shall praise thy works to another, and shall declare thy mighty acts."
devotionals.devotional:
Intergenerational faith transfer is God's intention for believers. One generation is expected to pass a legacy of true faith in God to another generation. This implies an unbroken chain of spiritual influence requiring each generation to serve as a bridge. Our call as church workers is a call for generational transformation. God does not intend that our ministry should stop with us. If our ministry stops with us, it means that we have failed in our Christian stewardship. Failure in our Christian stewardship is a major failure that will affect generations, even those yet unborn. God is looking for people who are ready to serve as bridges between generations—generational impact makers.

What is generational impact all about? It is about a righteous legacy. National Evangelical Mission as we have today is the outstanding legacy of our founding parents. Over fifty years ago, committed and dedicated believers took it upon themselves to start this mission that has continued to impact lives across the world. This is generational impact. The questions we must ask ourselves are: What is or will be my righteous legacy? What do I wish to pass on to those who are coming behind me? What is the impact that I hope to make to my generation and generations after me?

Steps to making generational impact include: being honest in taking personal inventory of our walk with God, readiness to invest our lives in others, modelling Christian life to our people, seeing the need for intergenerational faith transfer, being intentional about it, guarding the truth for continuity, being consistent both in private and public life, mentoring younger generations, and creating opportunities for service for the younger generation. God's intention is to see us make generational impact. He wants to see our ministries flow through us to our children, children's children, members, and followers.

Lesson: You are called to be a bridge, not a dead end. Your faith and ministry must outlive you and impact generations yet unborn.

Action: Identify one younger person you can mentor this year. Commit to investing in them spiritually, helping them grow and eventually impact their own generation.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, make me a generational impact maker. Let my faith and ministry outlive me. Help me to be a bridge, not a dead end, passing a righteous legacy to those coming behind me.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Mark 10:45 KJV - "For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give His life a ransom for many."
devotionals.devotional:
Jesus' impact is still felt even today. What are the qualities of a person committed to generational impact? First, commitment. The church worker must make a promise—a promise to God, a promise to the pastor, and a promise to the church. We must make up our minds to reproduce in every department we serve. Apart from making heaven, there are people who will use your life as a point of reference. Some lives will be changed because of you. We must determine to leave this conference with a strong commitment to reproduce. Paul said, "I was not disobedient unto the heavenly calling." That same declaration must be ours.

Second, dedication. Paul showed his commitment by saying he was not disobedient to the heavenly calling. What concerned him greatly was the care of all the churches. You should be concerned about the growth of the church. No matter your position, you must be dedicated. This burden will lead you to pray, especially when you face things beyond your control. Third, service. You cannot truly fit in without the heart of a servant. Examine your heart for pride, especially when you feel you have achieved something. The higher you go, the more you must ask God for a servant's heart. God resists the proud—if God resists you, how far can you go?

Fourth, integrity. Integrity means, "Do what I do, not just what I say." Let people see you as you truly are. A disciple is a follower who stays close because he admires the master and desires to learn from him. Your integrity is what makes you worth following. Without integrity, your words are empty. Without integrity, your influence is temporary. These four qualities—commitment, dedication, service, and integrity—are what God, the church leadership, and the church are looking for in your life. Cultivate them, and you will leave a lasting impact.

Lesson: Generational impact requires commitment, dedication, a servant's heart, and integrity. These qualities make you worth following and your legacy worth keeping.

Action: Which of the four qualities do you need to grow in? Choose one and take a practical step this week to develop it further.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, develop in me commitment, dedication, a servant's heart, and integrity. Let my life be worth following and my impact last for generations.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Philippians 1:6 KJV - "Being confident of this very thing, that He which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ."
devotionals.devotional:
Christianity is a progressive religion, not a stagnant one. It is God's help to develop our capacity. If no one thinks about advancement, he or she will not advance. We should take our calling seriously as children of God. There is a calling you have, and it must be cherished. Everyone should know his or her calling in order to make it relevant and effective. No one fulfills his or her calling in the comfort zone. You do not fulfill God's calling in your comfort zone. The calling of God is very important and should not be ignored. God's intention for our lives is that we move forward through progression.

You do not fulfill destiny in a strange land. As a child of God, you are meant to progress. God expects us to follow the directions He has set for our progress. God's plan is that we make progress in life. Every family desires progress. It is God's will that we progress and not remain stagnant. The Spirit of the Lord empowers us to make progress. When we are making progress, it draws God closer to us. When you are making progress, God takes note of it. When we desire to make progress, God steps into our lives. When God steps into our lives, progress becomes inevitable.

If you want to make progress, you must go where God wants you to go. As a Christian, you are not meant to remain in your comfort zone. The work Jesus started in us is not yet finished. The Scriptures explain that we are God's field. The reason we are still on earth is because there is more to do for Him. Do not settle for where you are. Do not be satisfied with past achievements. God has more for you. There is another level. There is greater progress. Keep moving forward. Keep pressing upward. Divine progression is your heritage.

Lesson: Christianity is progressive, not stagnant. God intends for you to move forward, grow, and advance. Do not settle for where you are.

Action: Identify one area where you have become stagnant or comfortable. Take one step today to break out of that comfort zone and move forward.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I receive divine progression. I will not remain stagnant. Help me to move forward, to grow, and to advance in every area of my life for Your glory.

devotionals.memoryVerse: James 4:8 KJV - "Draw nigh to God, and He will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded."
devotionals.devotional:
The kingdom of God is an ever-increasing kingdom, and we must prepare ourselves to meet God in every new season. When God comes down, visions are revealed, and lives are transformed—things never remain the same. God communicates what He wants and how He wants it because He is not an idol. Sanctification and purification are essential to prepare us for God's coming. If we desire to encounter God this season, we must adhere to His words and commandments. Hearts, attitudes, and character that remain unclean cannot receive Christ. To truly meet God, we must be clean and acceptable before Him.

It is God's will that we prepare ourselves for His coming. Without setting boundaries, we cannot experience His presence. God is holy by nature and does not tolerate iniquity. First Peter 1:15-16 says, "Be ye holy; for I am holy." Until we prepare and set our hearts right, we cannot fully receive what God has planned for us. Blessings from God come only when we are prepared to receive them. When we align ourselves with His will, we are assured of His blessings. Preparation is not optional; it is essential.

How do you prepare? Through repentance—turning away from sin and turning back to God. Through purification—allowing the Word to cleanse your thoughts and motives. Through consecration—setting yourself apart exclusively for God's use. Through prayer and fasting—humbling yourself before the Almighty. Do not rush into God's presence carelessly. Do not approach Him with dirty hands and a divided heart. Prepare yourself. Sanctify yourself. Purify yourself. Then come boldly before the throne of grace. Then encounter the living God.

Lesson: Encountering God requires preparation. Sanctification and purification are essential to experience His presence and receive His blessings.

Action: Set aside time this week for intentional preparation—confess sins, purify your heart, and consecrate yourself afresh to God before seeking His face.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, prepare me to meet You. Cleanse my heart, purify my hands, and sanctify my life. I want to encounter You fully. I will not come unprepared before Your presence.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 92:1 KJV - "It is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD, and to sing praises unto Thy name, O Most High."
devotionals.devotional:
As we approach the presence of God, we must do so with thanksgiving before presenting our requests. Alongside thanksgiving, consecration is vital. Psalm 140:13 emphasizes the importance, need, and our responsibility to thank God. Thanksgiving must be a consistent part of our lives. We must recognize God's faithfulness and goodness. Why should we give thanks? First, thanksgiving is spiritual. It is good to give thanks to the Lord and to sing praises to His name. Acknowledging Him in all things is a divine obligation. Second, it is a sign of life. Psalm 6:5 reminds us that those who fail to thank God are spiritually dead. Only the living can truly appreciate God's blessings and faithfulness. Third, because of God's goodness. He has been good to us, our families, and our businesses. For this, we owe Him heartfelt gratitude.

Consecration involves setting apart time, resources, and oneself to seek God exclusively. Exodus 28:41 teaches the importance of consecration in service to God. Exodus 19:16 and Joshua 3:5 emphasize that true consecration is necessary for encountering God and His blessings. Through consecration, we align ourselves with God's will and create a space for His presence in our lives. Thanksgiving acknowledges what God has done; consecration prepares us for what God wants to do. One looks back; the other looks forward. Both are essential.

Do not approach God with only your wish list. Come first with thanksgiving. Count your blessings. Name them one by one. Then present your requests. And do not come casually. Come consecrated—set apart, focused, and fully devoted. God inhabits the praises of His people, and He responds to the prayers of the consecrated. Make thanksgiving and consecration your lifestyle, not just an occasional event. You will see His power and presence in new ways.

Lesson: Approach God with thanksgiving for what He has done and consecration for what He wants to do. Both are essential for encountering His presence.

Action: Before you pray your next request, spend time in genuine thanksgiving. Then consecrate yourself afresh to God's will for that request.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, I come to You with thanksgiving and consecration. Thank You for Your goodness. I set myself apart for Your will. Create in me a space for Your presence.

devotionals.topic: The Enemy Must Fall for Our Sake
devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Corinthians 15:57 KJV - "But thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ."
devotionals.devotional:
Satan is a defeated foe, and every challenge we face in ministry, business, or family is a sign of the good work we are doing. God is in charge of your life and endeavors, and the enemy must fall for your sake because you are working in God's agenda. Why must the enemy fall for our sake? First, because this is God's business. Evangelism and outreach are God's assignments. When we commit ourselves to God's work, He ensures that no opposition can succeed against us. Second, because we are not alone. God is always with us, even when it feels like all hope is gone. Whether in ministry or business, as long as the work aligns with God's purpose, we are never abandoned. Third, because of the grace of Christ. God's unmerited favor empowers us to overcome challenges.

What must we be prepared to do? First, participate in Christ's victory. Our victory and success are essential for the growth of the body of Christ. As children of God, we are more than conquerors, and through Christ, we share in His triumph. Second, acknowledge the reality of the enemy. The devil is real and actively opposes God's people. To stand firm, we must practice righteousness and live in alignment with God's word. Third, remain steadfast in faith. Be unshakable in your commitment to God's work, knowing that your labor is not in vain.

Every challenge you face is an opportunity to experience God's power at work in you. The enemy falls because of God's agenda, not yours. You are victorious in Christ. Do not be intimidated by the size of the opposition. Do not be discouraged by the intensity of the battle. The enemy must fall. It is not a possibility; it is a promise. Stay courageous. Live righteously. Remain confident that God is always with you. The victory is already yours.

Lesson: The enemy is already defeated. Because you are working on God's agenda, opposition must fall. Stay courageous, live righteously, and remain confident in Christ's victory.

Action: Identify one area where the enemy is opposing you. Declare aloud that he must fall because you are working on God's agenda. Thank God for the victory.
devotionals.prayerConfession: Lord, thank You for the victory. The enemy must fall for my sake because I am working on Your agenda. I am more than a conqueror through Christ who loves me.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Luke 6:46 KJV - "And why call ye Me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?"
devotionals.devotional:
The Lordship of Jesus Christ highlights the significance of His authority and the understanding it brings to our lives. Without a deep comprehension of the Lordship of Jesus, a church cannot fulfill its ministry effectively. In this new season, our focus is to declare and proclaim the Lordship of Jesus Christ. Our emphasis is on lifting Jesus as Lord over all. As true Christians, Jesus Christ must take precedence in everything we do. We are not true followers until Jesus reigns as Lord over our lives. He is Lord and will always be.

The Lordship of Jesus signifies His ownership and authority over our lives. To live under His Lordship means to obey God wholeheartedly and continuously submit ourselves to His will. Jesus asked, "Why call ye Me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?" Lordship is not just a title we give Jesus; it is a reality we live. The Lordship of Jesus shapes every aspect of our lives—our ministries, families, and businesses—and causes us to treasure the things of Christ above all. This year, as we embrace a new season, our goals and plans will align with God's purposes because they are under the Lord's authority. Jesus is Lord over our lives and everything that concerns us.

How do we make Jesus Christ Lord over our lives? First, surrender completely to God. Second, recognize the Lordship of Jesus as the foundation of your success. His authority guarantees the fulfillment of our goals and makes us stand out from the crowd. Third, trust Him for answered prayers. Being under His Lordship ensures that our prayers are heard and that His will is done in our lives. Fourth, stay focused on Him. Do not let anything distract you from your fellowship with Christ. Let the Lordship of Jesus Christ take center stage in your life. You will experience His guidance, His blessings, and His unmatched sovereignty.

Lesson: Jesus is not just Savior but Lord. His Lordship requires our obedience, surrender, and focus. When He is truly Lord, everything else falls into place.

Action: Examine your life: Is Jesus truly Lord, or just Savior? Identify one area where you have not surrendered to His authority. Surrender it to Him today.
