Father, I thank You for Your Word. Help me to study it diligently and rightly divide the truth.

Confess this: I study to show myself approved unto God. I rightly divide the word of truth. The Word does not depart from my mouth. I meditate on it day and night. My way is prosperous, and I have good success. I am a student of the Word.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Thessalonians 5:17 KJV - "Pray without ceasing."
devotionals.devotional:
The call to pray is a timeless call for all believers, especially Christian workers in all generations. One who desires to be spiritually mature must not overlook the place of prayer. Prayer is not only designed for you to receive things from God; it is designed for your spiritual maturity. The greatest need in the work of God today is not just popularity or money; the greatest need is prayer.

Every Christian worker needs a good prayer life. When prayers are adequately employed, you will always have better results. Prayer is one of the greatest resources of the church here on earth. Scripture says, "Pray without ceasing" 1 Thessalonians 5:17 KJV, and "Men ought always to pray, and not to faint" Luke 18:1 KJV.

Through prayers, you encounter the supernatural, which changes and empowers you into spiritual maturity in life and Christian services. Men and women of God who have ever achieved something in Christendom were people who prayed. The child of God moves forward in life when he learns and disciplines himself to kneel before God in prayers. Rise and pray!

Lesson: Prayer is essential for spiritual maturity and effective ministry; you must pray without ceasing.

Action: Set a specific time today to pray. Use a prayer list and be committed to a quiet time with God.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the privilege of prayer. Help me to pray without ceasing and grow in my prayer life.

Confess this: I pray without ceasing. I am committed to a good prayer life. Prayer is my greatest resource. I encounter the supernatural through prayer. I am empowered into spiritual maturity. I rise and pray.

devotionals.memoryVerse: John 4:24 KJV - "God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth."
devotionals.devotional:
The ever-present God is your object of worship. Any one who has interest in spiritual maturity must discipline himself to worship the living God. A spiritually mature Christian worker will always have strong regards for the presence of God. He does not treat the presence of God with contempt in any way or anywhere. He holds the presence of God in awe and gives God the deep respect that He deserves.

In worship, the spiritually mature Christian glorifies, honours, and extols the ever-living and ever-present God. Scripture says, "God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth" John 4:24 KJV. Worship is essential for spiritual maturity and growth. When you worship, you give the Lord the centre stage of your life and yield your whole being to His supremacy and Lordship.

Praise is one of the ways the spiritually mature Christian worker says thank you to God for who He is, what He has done, what He is doing, and what He will do. Scripture says, "Praise ye the Lord: for it is good to sing praises unto our God; for it is pleasant; and praise is comely" Psalm 147:1 KJV. Find reasons to praise God in all situations. It will elevate your heart from daily distractions to lasting confidence in the living God.

Lesson: Worship and praise are essential for spiritual maturity; you must worship God in spirit and truth.

Action: Take time today to worship God intentionally. Sing praises to Him and ascribe worthiness to His name.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that I can worship You in spirit and truth. Help me to glorify You with my whole being.

Confess this: I worship God in spirit and truth. I hold His presence in awe. I glorify, honour, and extol the living God. I praise Him in good and difficult times. Praise is comely for me. I find reasons to praise God daily.

devotionals.topic: The Christian Worker And Christian Doctrine
devotionals.memoryVerse: John 7:17 KJV - "If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself."
devotionals.devotional:
Christian doctrine has been defined as the fundamental truths of the Bible faith. It is the teaching or instructions of the Lord that Christian believers must follow and obey as you journey from time to eternity. Although many have tried to avoid the study of Christian doctrine, saying it is dry and boring, neglecting it will make you vulnerable to the devil and false doctrines of false teachers.

It takes knowledge of Christian doctrine to do the will of God. Jesus made this clear when He said, "My doctrine is not mine, but His that sent me. If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself" John 7:16-17 KJV. All who want to know the will of God and do it rightly must know the Christian doctrine.

The acid test of all the challenges you are having in these last days is true knowledge of Christian doctrine. Many have had shipwreck of their faith for lack of understanding and knowledge of Christian doctrine. If you must do God's will and not derail, you must have a clear knowledge of Christian doctrine. Christian doctrine is your identity and road map for Christian mission.

Lesson: You must know Christian doctrine to do God's will and avoid being deceived by false teachers.

Action: Pick one core doctrine today (e.g., salvation, the Holy Spirit, the church) and study it in the Word.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the truth of Christian doctrine. Help me to know and apply Your doctrine correctly.

Confess this: I know Christian doctrine. I am not deceived by false teachers. I do the will of God because I know His truth. My doctrine is from God, not from men. I am grounded in the faith.

devotionals.topic: The Christian Worker And The Harvest
devotionals.memoryVerse: John 4:35 KJV - "Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest."
devotionals.devotional:
The heart of Christ is always on planting the seed of the gospel and harvesting the souls of mankind for God. The Lord says, "Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest" John 4:35 KJV.

One of the reasons why you often fail to do the work and will of God is that you never love to look up to the harvest field. You are often looking away from it. You must remember that for the purpose of soul harvest you are called. You can begin to be actively involved in soul harvest by being compassionate toward sinners, sharing the hope of eternal life, healing the broken hearted, setting the captives free, and encouraging the weak in faith.

Jesus saw the multitudes and was moved with compassion because they were fainted and scattered abroad as sheep having no shepherd. He said, "The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest" Matthew 9:37-38 KJV. You are a labourer in His harvest. Lift up your eyes and look on the fields.

Lesson: The fields are white unto harvest; you must lift up your eyes and labour for souls.

Action: Lift up your eyes today. See the souls around you who are ready to be harvested, and pray for labourers.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that the harvest is plenteous. Help me to lift up my eyes and see the fields that are white unto harvest.

Confess this: I lift up my eyes and look on the fields. The harvest is white already. I am a labourer in God's harvest. I am compassionate toward sinners. I share the hope of eternal life. I am sent to the harvest.

devotionals.topic: The Christian Worker And Church Planting
devotionals.memoryVerse: Matthew 16:18 KJV - "And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it."
devotionals.devotional:
Church planting is the essence for which you carry out the great commission. The church of Jesus Christ is never destined to disappear from the scene. Jesus says, "The gates of hell shall not prevail against it" Matthew 16:18 KJV. The true church must continue to exist and play her role to the world. The church's unique role to the world and need of mankind cannot be substituted.

The Christian worker must be concerned and committed to church planting, because each true church is a living cell of the body of Christ. It has within it the power to expand and reproduce itself through committed Christian workers. Planting of churches must continue until Christ returns. You must keep on planting churches because the church is God's agent in the world through which He expresses Himself to the world.

No person, village, town, or nation is ever born Christian. Your principal responsibility as a Christian worker is to be evangelistic, reaching out to men, women, boys, girls, and children in various places with the gospel of Christ. As soon as they truly believe in Christ as Lord and Saviour, such converted persons are baptized and made members of the visible Christian community Acts 2:46-47 KJV. Plant churches!

Lesson: Church planting is central to the Great Commission; the church is God's redeeming agent on earth.

Action: Pray for your local church and ask God to show you how you can be involved in planting or strengthening a church.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for Your church. Help me to be committed to planting and establishing churches.

Confess this: I am a church planter. The gates of hell cannot prevail against the church. I am committed to planting churches. The church is God's agent in the world. I am part of the church that cannot be stopped.

devotionals.topic: The Christian Worker And Training Others
devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Timothy 2:2 KJV - "And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also."
devotionals.devotional:
The Lord Jesus Christ sets a great example for you in training other Christian workers. When He started His ministry, He called twelve ordinary men whom He trained for the work of the ministry. He taught them, cared for them, encouraged them, and showed them how to live a life of faith. After His death and resurrection, He commanded them to go and make disciples of all nations Matthew 28:19 KJV.

As a trained Christian worker, you must follow this example of our Lord Jesus Christ. It is not enough for you to do the work of the ministry alone; you must train others to do it too. This is what is called multiplication. Paul told Timothy, "And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also" 2 Timothy 2:2 KJV.

There are so many believers in your churches today who are willing to serve God, but they have not been trained. They are like raw materials waiting to be processed. The Christian worker must identify such people and invest his or her life in them. You must take time to disciple, mentor, and train other Christian workers. This is the only way you can reach the world with the gospel of Christ.

Lesson: You must train other Christian workers to multiply the work of the ministry.

Action: Identify someone today who is willing to serve but needs training. Begin to invest in them.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the example of Jesus in training workers. Help me to train and mentor others.

Confess this: I train other Christian workers. I identify raw materials and invest my life in them. I multiply the work of the ministry. I am a mentor and a coach. I follow the example of Jesus.

devotionals.topic: The Christian Worker And Peace Of Mind
devotionals.memoryVerse: Philippians 4:6 KJV - "Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God."
devotionals.devotional:
Today is World Mental Health Day. The world is full of anxiety, stress, and mental turmoil. But as a Christian worker, you are called to live in the peace of God. Scripture says, "Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus" Philippians 4:6-7 KJV.

This peace is not the absence of trouble; it is an inner peace, a serenity and tranquility that is a legacy from the Lord Jesus Christ. Jesus said, "In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world" John 16:33 KJV. You are designed to enjoy Christ's peace in a troubled world. The degree of worry and peace in your heart—which is greater?

You are to cast all your cares upon Him because He cares for you 1 Peter 5:7 KJV. When you are anxious, you are not trusting God. When you pray with thanksgiving, the peace of God guards your heart and mind. This is your inheritance as a child of God.

Lesson: The Christian worker enjoys the peace of God that passes all understanding by casting all cares upon Him.

Action: Identify one worry you have been carrying. Cast it upon the Lord in prayer and thank Him for the answer.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for Your peace that passes all understanding. Help me to cast all my cares upon You.

Confess this: I am careful for nothing. I pray with thanksgiving, and the peace of God guards my heart and mind. I have peace in a troubled world. I am not anxious. I cast all my cares upon the Lord, for He cares for me.

devotionals.topic: The Christian Worker And The Joy Of The Lord
devotionals.memoryVerse: John 15:11 KJV - "These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full."
devotionals.devotional:
Joy never comes as a result of what is happening outside, nor does it depend on circumstances around you. Joy is the natural outcome of the love of God in you. The heart filled with the love of God is always filled with joy in the Holy Ghost. The Lord says, "These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full" John 15:11 KJV.

Christians are designed to live a joyful life daily in all situations before your family members, Christian brethren, and friends. Scripture says, "The joy of the Lord is your strength" Nehemiah 8:10 KJV. Your joy is not dependent on your circumstances; it is dependent on your relationship with Christ.

As a Christian worker, you are to measure your spiritual progress by your joy. Can people access you as a joyful Christian worker? Are you living a joyful Christian life? If the joy of the Lord is your strength, then you are strong even in the midst of trials.

Lesson: The joy of the Lord is your strength; it is not dependent on circumstances but on your relationship with Christ.

Action: Choose to rejoice today, regardless of your circumstances. Let the joy of the Lord be your strength.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the joy of the Lord. Help me to live a joyful life in all situations.

Confess this: The joy of the Lord is my strength. My joy does not depend on circumstances. My joy is full in Christ. I am a joyful Christian worker. I rejoice in all situations.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Thessalonians 5:18 KJV - "In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you."
devotionals.devotional:
Today is Thanksgiving Day in Canada. As a Christian worker, you are called to live a life of gratitude. Scripture says, "In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you" 1 Thessalonians 5:18 KJV. This is not just a suggestion; it is the will of God for your life.

Gratitude is a choice. It is not based on your circumstances; it is based on your trust in God. Scripture says, "Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name" Psalm 100:4 KJV. You are to thank God for who He is, what He has done, what He is doing, and what He will do.

A grateful heart is a powerful weapon against discouragement and depression. When you focus on the goodness of God, your perspective changes. You are to be thankful in all things—both good and difficult. This is the discipline of the mature Christian worker.

Lesson: Gratitude is the will of God; you must give thanks in all circumstances.

Action: List five things you are grateful for today and thank God specifically for each one.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for Your goodness. Help me to live a life of gratitude in all circumstances.

Confess this: In everything, I give thanks. This is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning me. I enter His gates with thanksgiving. I am thankful for who He is and what He has done. I am a grateful Christian worker.

devotionals.topic: The Christian Worker And God's Stewardship Of Resources
devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Peter 4:10 KJV - "As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God."
devotionals.devotional:
As a Christian worker, you are a steward of God's resources. This includes your finances, your time, your talents, and the manifold grace of God. Scripture says, "As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God" 1 Peter 4:10 KJV.

You are to manage God's resources wisely. Scripture says, "Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the Lord of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it" Malachi 3:10 KJV. You are to honour God with your finances and trust Him for His provision.

God's resources are not just for you; they are for the work of the kingdom. You are to use what God has given you to bless others. This is the heart of stewardship. When you manage God's resources well, you become a channel of blessing to your generation.

Lesson: You are a steward of God's resources; you must manage them wisely to bless others.

Action: Review your finances and resources today. Ask God to show you how to use them for His kingdom.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for entrusting me with Your resources. Help me to be a faithful steward of all that You have given me.

Confess this: I am a steward of God's manifold grace. I manage His resources wisely. I honour God with my finances. I bless others with what He has given me. I am a channel of blessing.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Hebrews 11:6 KJV - "But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him."
devotionals.devotional:
Without faith, it is impossible to please God. As a Christian worker, your ministry is built on faith. Scripture says, "But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him" Hebrews 11:6 KJV.

Faith is not just believing in God; it is trusting His Word and acting on it. Scripture says, "Faith which worketh by love" Galatians 5:6 KJV. Your faith is energized by the love of God that is shed abroad in your heart. When you walk in love, your faith works effectively.

You are to step out in faith, take risks, and trust God for the impossible. Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen Hebrews 11:1 KJV. You must believe that God is who He says He is and that He will do what He has promised.

Lesson: Faith is essential for the Christian worker; without faith, you cannot please God.

Action: Identify one area where you need to step out in faith today. Trust God and act on His Word.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the gift of faith. Help me to believe You and act on Your Word.

Confess this: I have faith in God. I believe He is and that He rewards those who diligently seek Him. My faith works by love. I step out in faith. I trust God for the impossible. I am a believer, not a doubter.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Thessalonians 4:3 KJV - "For this is the will of God, even your sanctification, that ye should abstain from fornication."
devotionals.devotional:
Purity is essential for the Christian worker. Scripture says, "For this is the will of God, even your sanctification, that ye should abstain from fornication" 1 Thessalonians 4:3 KJV. You are called to live a pure and holy life, both in your body and in your thoughts.

Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit. You are not to defile it with impurity, evil thoughts, evil desires, or deeds. You are required to honour and please God with your body and life. Scripture says, "Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God" Matthew 5:8 KJV.

Purity is not just about avoiding sin; it is about being set apart for God's use. You are to live a life that reflects the holiness of God. When you are pure, you are able to see God and walk in His presence.

Lesson: Purity is the will of God; you are called to live a holy and set-apart life.

Action: Examine your heart and mind today. Confess any impurity and ask God to purify you.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that I can be pure. Help me to live a holy and set-apart life for Your glory.

Confess this: I am sanctified. I abstain from impurity. My body is a temple of the Holy Spirit. I am pure in heart and I see God. I honour and please God with my body and life.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Proverbs 11:3 KJV - "The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them."
devotionals.devotional:
Integrity is one of the highest virtues of the Christian worker. Scripture says, "The integrity of the upright shall guide them" Proverbs 11:3 KJV. Integrity means that you are consistent in your words and actions. What you say is what you do. You are honest and transparent.

As a Christian worker, you are to be transparent in your dealing with people. Scripture says, "Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men" 2 Corinthians 8:21 KJV. Your integrity should be visible to both God and men. You are to be trustworthy, dependable, and reliable.

Without integrity, your ministry will not last. People will not trust you, and God will not bless you. You are to be a person of your word, one who does not waver or compromise on the truth.

Lesson: Integrity guides the upright; you must be honest, transparent, and dependable.

Action: Evaluate your integrity today. Are there any areas where you have not been honest or consistent? Make it right.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that I can walk in integrity. Help me to be honest and transparent in all my dealings.

Confess this: The integrity of the upright guides me. I am honest in the sight of God and men. I am trustworthy and dependable. My word is my bond. I do not compromise on the truth.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Mark 10:45 KJV - "For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many."
devotionals.devotional:
You are called to serve, not to be served. Scripture says, "For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many" Mark 10:45 KJV. This is the example of Christ. He came to serve, and you are to follow in His steps.

Service is the hallmark of the Christian worker. Scripture says, "For, brethren, ye have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another" Galatians 5:13 KJV. You are to serve others with humility and love. Your service should not be for recognition or reward; it should be a demonstration of the love of Christ.

Service is the key to greatness in the Kingdom. Jesus said, "Whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister" Matthew 20:26 KJV. You are to be a servant to all, just as Christ served you.

Lesson: You are called to serve others with humility and love, following the example of Christ.

Action: Look for one opportunity to serve someone today without expecting anything in return.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the example of Christ. Help me to serve others with humility and love.

Confess this: I am called to serve, not to be served. I follow the example of Christ. I serve others with love. I am great in the Kingdom because I am a servant. I minister to others as Christ ministered to me.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Colossians 3:12 KJV - "Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering."
devotionals.devotional:
Compassion is at the heart of the Christian worker. Scripture says, "Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering" Colossians 3:12 KJV. You are to be filled with tender mercies and compassion toward others.

Jesus saw the multitudes and was moved with compassion because they were fainted and scattered abroad as sheep having no shepherd Matthew 9:36 KJV. Compassion is not just feeling sorry for someone; it is doing something to help them. Compassion moves you to action.

As a Christian worker, you are to be compassionate toward the lost, the hurting, the brokenhearted, and the weak. You are to look for opportunities to show mercy and kindness. This is the love of God in demonstration.

Lesson: Compassion moves you to action; you must put on mercies, kindness, and tenderness toward others.

Action: Today, show compassion to someone who is hurting. Speak a kind word or offer practical help.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for Your compassion toward me. Help me to be compassionate toward others.

Confess this: I put on bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, and longsuffering. I am moved with compassion. I help the hurting. I am a tenderhearted Christian worker.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Hebrews 12:1 KJV - "Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us."
devotionals.devotional:
Perseverance is essential for the Christian worker. Scripture says, "Let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us" Hebrews 12:1 KJV. You are in a race, and you must run with patience and endurance.

The Christian life is not a sprint; it is a marathon. You will face challenges, obstacles, and temptations. But you must not give up. Scripture says, "And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not" Galatians 6:9 KJV. Your labour is not in vain in the Lord.

Perseverance is what keeps you going when the going gets tough. It is the determination to finish well. You are to keep your eyes on Jesus, the Author and Finisher of your faith Hebrews 12:2 KJV. Do not give up. The prize is at the end of the race.

Lesson: Perseverance keeps you running the race; you must not give up, for your reward is coming.

Action: Identify one area where you are tempted to give up. Determine today to keep running with patience.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the strength to persevere. Help me to run the race with patience and endurance.

Confess this: I run with patience the race set before me. I lay aside every weight and the sin that besets me. I am not weary in well doing. In due season, I shall reap. I finish well. I keep my eyes on Jesus.

devotionals.topic: A Reminder: Preparing To Honour Those Who Labour Among You
devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Thessalonians 5:12-13 KJV - "And we beseech you, brethren, to know them which labour among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you; And to esteem them very highly in love for their work's sake. And be at peace among yourselves."
devotionals.devotional:
This coming Sunday, the 25th of October, National Evangelical Mission will set aside a day to appreciate its pastors. But appreciation does not begin on the day itself; it begins in the heart, long before the day arrives. This devotional is a reminder to every member: prepare your heart now to honour those whom God has placed over you.

Scripture says, "And we beseech you, brethren, to know them which labour among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you; And to esteem them very highly in love for their work's sake. And be at peace among yourselves" (1 Thessalonians 5:12-13 KJV). Notice the three things this verse asks of you: know them, esteem them, and be at peace with one another. To know them means to recognise their labour, their burden, and their calling. To esteem them means to honour them highly, not because they are perfect, but because of the work they do for the Lord.

The Word says, "Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you" (Hebrews 13:17 KJV). Your pastor watches over your soul. He will give an account for you before God. That is a weighty responsibility, and it deserves your honour.

As you prepare for Sunday, do not come empty-hearted. Search your heart. Is there any resentment, criticism, or gossip against your pastor? Repent of it. Plan to be in church on Sunday with a grateful heart, ready to celebrate those who labour among you. Prepare a word of encouragement, a prayer of blessing, or a gift of love.

Lesson: Honour your pastor by knowing him, esteeming him, obeying his leadership, praying for him, and preparing your heart to celebrate him on Pastors Appreciation Sunday.

Action: Today, spend time praying for your pastor. Then, prepare one specific way you will honour him on Sunday, 25th October.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the shepherd You have placed over me. I choose today to prepare my heart to honour him as You have commanded. Forgive me for any criticism, gossip, or resentment I have held against him.

Confess this: I know those who labour among me. I esteem them very highly in love for their work's sake. I obey my pastor and submit to his leadership. I pray for him daily. I speak well of him to others. I am preparing my heart to honour him on Pastors Appreciation Sunday.

devotionals.topic: Introduction: The Realities Of Our Union With Christ
devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Corinthians 5:17 KJV - "Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new."
devotionals.devotional:
This is a 45-day journey. For the next 45 devotionals, we will walk through what the New Testament calls the In Him realities — the believer's position and possessions in Christ. We will look at the expressions the Holy Spirit uses across the Epistles: in Him, in Christ, in Christ Jesus, in whom, in the beloved, through Him, through whom, by Him, by whom, with Him, of Him, from Him, unto Him, for Him, in His Son. Each expression reveals something that already belongs to you because you are in Him.

But before we go further, hear this clearly: these expressions are not filler words. They are not random phrases to skim past. Every time the Holy Spirit writes in Him, or in Christ, or in whom, or by Him, or with Him, He is pointing to a treasure. He is showing you a facet of Christ, and He is showing you that you are included in Him.

Notice also that these expressions carry characteristics. Some are in the present tense — already true now, like "ye are complete in him" (Colossians 2:10 KJV). Some are in the past tense — already done, like "who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ" (Ephesians 1:3 KJV). Some are positional — a standing before God, like "accepted in the beloved" (Ephesians 1:6 KJV). Some are corporate — shared by every believer, like "hath raised us up together" (Ephesians 2:6 KJV). Some are relational — companionship, like "we shall also live with him" (2 Timothy 2:11 KJV). Some are possessive — what is yours, like "in whom also we have obtained an inheritance" (Ephesians 1:11 KJV). We will see these characteristics as we go. For now, know this: every expression is a window. Look through it and you will see Christ.

The Bible says, "Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ" (Ephesians 1:3 KJV). Every blessing is already yours — not because you earned it, but because you are in Him. Notice the tense. These are not future promises you are waiting for. They are present possessions you already hold. You have been blessed. You have been redeemed. You are seated with Christ. You are a new creation. You have eternal life.

So here is what we will do together for the next 45 days. We will read the Word. We will understand it. We will meditate on it. We will believe it. We will confess it. We will act on it. And we will continue in it. Each devotional will be short. Each will give you a Scripture, a thought to meditate on, a confession to speak, and one action to take.

And we will keep it balanced. Being in Christ is not a licence to sin. The one who abides in Him walks as He walked. Scripture says, "He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked" (1 John 2:6 KJV). So as we discover the riches of our position in Him, we will also remember our responsibility to live worthy of that position.

Lesson: Every believer already possesses all spiritual blessings in Christ; but abiding in Him means walking as He walked.

Action: Begin a journal today. Write at the top of the page: "I Am In Christ." Then, write down one truth from Ephesians 1 that you want to believe and live out over these 45 days.

Bible Portions — Pause Here. Look Again. What Treasure About Christ Do You See?

  • in Christ: Ephesians 1:3
    Here is Christ as the Treasury of every spiritual blessing. Every blessing God has is stored in Him — and you are in Him. What blessing have you been begging for that Christ has already placed in your account?
  • in him: Ephesians 1:4
    Here is Christ as the Place of your election. Before the world began, God chose you — not in yourself, but in Christ. Do you see yourself as chosen, or do you still live as an accident?
  • in the beloved: Ephesians 1:6
    Here is Christ as the Beloved in whom you are accepted. You are not accepted because of what you do; you are accepted because you are found in the One the Father loves. Do you know you are accepted, or are you still striving for approval?
  • in whom: Ephesians 1:7
    Here is Christ as the Fountain of redemption. The blood that purchased you is in Him, and you are in Him. Have you received redemption as a present possession, or do you still live as a slave?
  • in whom: Ephesians 1:11
    Here is Christ as the Source of your inheritance. Your inheritance is not a future hope; it is a present reality in Him. What are you treating as future that God has already given you in Christ?
  • in whom: Ephesians 1:13
    Here is Christ as the Seal of your security. You were sealed with the Holy Spirit when you believed — in Him. Are you living in the confidence of that seal, or in doubt?
  • in Christ: Ephesians 1:10
    Here is Christ as the Centre of all things. God's plan is to gather all things in Him — and you are part of that gathering. Is Christ the centre of your life, or is something else?
  • in Christ: Ephesians 1:12
    Here is Christ as the Ground of your hope. You first trusted in Christ — not in yourself, not in your works, not in your feelings. Where is your trust actually resting?

Look again. Every expression above is not a phrase to skim past. It is a doorway. When you see in Him, in Christ, in whom, in the beloved, stop. Look. Ask: what incredible thing about Christ is being revealed here? Then say the promise aloud and write what you see in your journal.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that I am in Christ. I am not trying to become something I am not; I am learning to live as who I already am in Him. Open the eyes of my understanding to see the riches of my inheritance in Christ. And help me to walk as He walked.

Confess this: I am in Christ. I am with Him. I am through Him. Every spiritual blessing is mine in Him. I am redeemed, righteous, and seated with Him in heavenly places. I am a new creation. I have eternal life. And I choose to walk as He walked.

devotionals.topic: Learning To Apply What You Read
devotionals.memoryVerse: James 1:22 KJV - "But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves."
devotionals.devotional:
Reading the Bible is not the same as living it. A person can read the In Him expressions every day for years and still be unchanged. The difference is not in how much we read, but in how we apply what we read. God said to Joshua, "This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success" (Joshua 1:8 KJV). Meditate. Then observe to do. Then comes success.

So as we continue this 45-day journey, remember the pattern: read the Word, understand it, meditate on it, believe it, confess it, act on it, and continue in it. That is how the In Him realities move from the page to your life.

Notice that confession is part of the pattern. It is not enough to read and understand. It is not enough to meditate and believe. For the Word to become effective in you, you must also confess it. But when you confess, mean what you say. Do not repeat words without thought. Speak them from your heart, in agreement with God. Scripture says, "For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation" (Romans 10:10 KJV).

A journal will help you. When you find an expression like in Him, in Christ, through Him, or of Him, write it down. Mark it in your Bible. Not because the marking itself changes you, but because it gives you a place to return to. The Bible Portions block at the end of each devotional is there for that purpose.

But there is a deeper reason to stop at each expression. These are not filler words. They are not random phrases. And they carry characteristics. Some are present tense — already true now. Some are past tense — already done, finished, accomplished. Some are positional — a standing before God, not a feeling. Some are corporate — shared by every believer. Some are relational — companionship. Some are possessive — what is yours. When you see in Him, in Christ, in whom, by Him, with Him, of Him, through Him, stop. Look. Something incredible about Christ is being revealed in that very expression. The Holy Spirit is showing you a facet of who Christ is, and showing you that you are included in Him. Every expression is a doorway into a revelation of Christ.

Lesson: The Word changes us when we read it, understand it, believe it, confess it, and act on it — not when we merely read or mark it. And every In Him expression is a doorway into a deeper revelation of Christ.

Action: Choose one expression from the Bible Portions below. Write it in your journal. Note its tense and its characteristic. Then, apply the process: read it, think about it, believe it, say it aloud, and do one thing that agrees with it. And when you see the expression, stop and ask: what incredible thing about Christ is being revealed here?

Bible Portions — Don't Rush Past This. There Is Treasure In These Words.

  • in him: Acts 17:28
    Here is Christ as the Atmosphere of your life. You do not merely live near Him — you live, move, and have your being in Him. This is locative and present tense. Are you living as if Christ is far away, when He is actually the air you breathe?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 5:17
    Here is Christ as the Source of a new creation. If you are in Christ, you are not a patched-up old person — you are a new creature. This is present tense. Are you still living as the old person, or as the new creation Christ has made you?
  • in him: 2 Corinthians 5:21
    Here is Christ as your Righteousness. He was made sin so that you might be made the righteousness of God in Him. This is present tense. Are you still trying to become righteous, when Christ has already made you righteous in Him?
  • in him: Philippians 3:9
    Here is Christ as the Righteousness that comes by faith. Paul wanted to be found in Him, not having his own righteousness. This is positional. Whose righteousness are you actually standing in — yours or His?
  • of him: 1 Corinthians 1:30
    Here is Christ as the Wisdom, Righteousness, Sanctification, and Redemption of God. And it is of Him that you are in Christ Jesus. This is causative. Do you see Christ as your everything, or are you still searching for wisdom, righteousness, and redemption elsewhere?

Look again. These expressions are not to be skimmed. They are to be stopped at, looked into, and meditated on. When you see in him, in Christ, of him, stop. Look. Ask: what incredible thing about Christ is being revealed here? Then say the promise aloud and write what you see in your journal.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for Your Word. I do not want to be a hearer only, but a doer. Teach me to read, to understand, to meditate, to believe, to confess, and to act on what I read. And teach me to stop and look whenever I see an In Him expression, so that I may see the incredible things about Christ that You are revealing.

Confess this: I am a doer of the Word. I read it, I understand it, I meditate on it, I believe it, I confess it, and I act on it. When I confess, I mean what I say. I speak from my heart in agreement with God. The Word takes root in my heart and shapes my life. I abide in Christ, and I walk as He walked.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Colossians 3:3 KJV - "For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God."
devotionals.devotional:
There is a truth so profound that it sounds almost too simple to believe: you live inside of Christ. He is not a distant figure you reach toward; He is the atmosphere you breathe. The Apostle Paul declared to the philosophers of Athens, "For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring" (Acts 17:28 KJV).

Paul was not speaking of a general relationship with God that all men have. He was declaring a truth that would later be fully revealed in the New Covenant: in Christ, the believer's very existence is wrapped up in Him. You do not live alongside Christ; you live in Him. You do not move toward Him; you move within Him. Your being is not separate from His; it is hidden in His.

The Amplified Bible renders Acts 17:28 this way: "For in Him we live and move and have our being." Notice the three verbs: live, move, have our being. In Him you live — He is your source of life. In Him you move — He is your pathway of action. In Him you have your being — He is your very identity.

But this truth is not a licence to live as you please. The one who lives and moves in Him is called to walk as He walked. Scripture says, "He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked" (1 John 2:6 KJV). To abide in Him is to walk in obedience to His Word. And if a believer turns away and continues in sin, refusing to repent, Scripture warns that such a one can still be judged (Hebrews 10:26-27 KJV).

Lesson: You live, move, and have your being in Christ; but abiding in Him means walking as He walked.

Action: Throughout today, whenever you feel alone or uncertain, whisper to yourself: "I am in Him." Then, take one deliberate step of obedience in an area where God has spoken to you.

Bible Portions — Look At This. Let It Change How You See Today.

  • in him: Acts 17:28
    Christ is the atmosphere of your life. You do not have to reach for Him; you are already in Him. How would today look if you lived as if He were the air you breathe?
  • with Christ: Colossians 3:3
    Your life is hidden with Christ in God. It is not on display for the world to approve or reject. It is secure in Him. Where are you seeking approval that only God can give?
  • with him: Colossians 3:4
    You will appear with Him in glory. The future is certain because the present is secure. Are you living in the light of that certainty?
  • with Christ: Colossians 3:1
    You are risen with Christ. Your position is above, not beneath. What are you still seeking below that you should be seeking above?
  • in Christ: Romans 12:5
    You are one body in Christ. You are not a solitary believer. You are joined to others. Who are you walking with in the body?

Carry this with you today. When you feel alone, remember: you are in Him. When you feel uncertain, remember: your life is hidden with Christ in God.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that I live and move and have my being in Christ. I am never alone. I am never outside Your reach. I choose today to abide in Him and to walk as He walked.

Confess this: In Him I live. In Him I move. In Him I have my being. I abide in Him, and He abides in me. I walk even as He walked. I am safe. I am secure. I am in Him.

devotionals.topic: Redeemed By The Blood Of The Lamb
devotionals.memoryVerse: Ephesians 1:7 KJV - "In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace."
devotionals.devotional:
Redemption is not something you are waiting for. It is not a future hope. It is a present possession. The Bible declares, "In whom we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins" (Colossians 1:14 KJV). Notice the tense: we have. Not we will have. Not we hope to have. We have it now, in Him.

The word redemption carries the idea of being bought back. You were once in the slave market of sin, held under the dominion of darkness. But Jesus paid the price. He purchased you with His own blood. He did not merely forgive you from a distance; He bought you out of bondage and brought you into His own family.

This redemption is not partial. It is not temporary. It is complete, and it is secured by the blood of the everlasting covenant. The writer of Hebrews declares that Christ "obtained eternal redemption for us" (Hebrews 9:12 KJV). You are not just forgiven; you are ransomed. You belong to Him.

Yet being redeemed does not mean you can live as you please. A slave who has been purchased by a new master is expected to serve that master. Scripture asks, "What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own? For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's" (1 Corinthians 6:19-20 KJV).

Lesson: In Christ, you already have complete and eternal redemption through His blood; but you were bought with a price, so you must glorify God with your life.

Action: Today, when the enemy reminds you of your past, declare: "I am redeemed. The blood of Jesus has purchased me. I am not a slave; I am a son. And I will glorify God with my life."

Bible Portions — There Is Blood-Bought Treasure Here. Look.

  • in whom: Ephesians 1:7
    Christ is the Fountain of redemption. The blood that purchased you is in Him, and you are in Him. Have you received redemption as a present possession, or do you still live as a slave?
  • in whom: Colossians 1:14
    Christ is the Price that was paid. Your forgiveness is not a theory; it is a purchase. What sin are you still trying to pay for that Christ has already paid?
  • by him: Colossians 1:20
    Christ is the Peacemaker. By Him, God reconciled all things to Himself. What area of your life still needs to be reconciled to Him?
  • with him: Colossians 2:12
    Christ is the One in whom you were buried and raised. Your old life is buried with Him. What old thing are you still trying to keep alive?
  • with him: Colossians 2:13
    Christ is the One who quickened you. You were dead, and He made you alive. What dead thing are you still trying to resurrect in your own strength?

Walk in it. You are redeemed. Not partially. Not temporarily. Fully and forever. Live like it.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I have redemption through His blood. I am not trying to earn my forgiveness; I have already received it. I walk in the freedom of the redeemed, and I glorify You with my life.

Confess this: In Him I have redemption through His blood. I am forgiven. I am ransomed. I am purchased. I am not a slave to sin. I am a son of God. I was bought with a price, and I glorify God in my body and in my spirit. I walk in freedom and victory.

devotionals.topic: Pastors Appreciation Sunday: Say Good Things About Pastors
devotionals.memoryVerse: Jeremiah 3:15 KJV - "And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding."
devotionals.devotional:
We pause the In Him series again today for Pastors Appreciation Sunday. Believers across National Evangelical Mission are pausing to say good things about those whom God has given to shepherd them. This is a sacred day. It is a day to lift up the men and women who have answered the call to feed the flock of God. It is a day to say: thank you.

God said, "And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding" (Jeremiah 3:15 KJV). Your pastor is a gift from God to you. He is not merely an employee of the church; he is a shepherd given by the heart of God. He was appointed to feed you, to guide you, to protect you, and to lead you in the ways of the Lord.

Peter wrote, "Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof, not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind; Neither as being lords over God's heritage, but being ensamples to the flock. And when the chief Shepherd shall appear, ye shall receive a crown of glory that fadeth not away" (1 Peter 5:2-4 KJV). Your pastor shepherds you willingly. He does not lord it over you. He is an example to you. And a crown of glory awaits him.

Today, say good things about your pastor. Thank God for him. Speak well of him. Encourage him. Let him know that his labour is not in vain in the Lord. Pray for him and his family. Bless him in every way you can. This is not flattery; this is the honour that God commands. Those who labour among you deserve to be loved, respected, and celebrated. Today, do exactly that.

Lesson: Your pastor is a gift from God to you; you must honour him, speak well of him, and bless him on this Pastors Appreciation Sunday and every day.

Action: Today, speak one specific word of appreciation to your pastor. Thank him for a particular way he has blessed your life, and pray a blessing over him and his family.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the gift of my pastor. I choose today to say good things about him and to bless him with all my heart.

Confess this: My pastor is a gift from God to me. I speak well of him. I bless him. I honour him. I encourage him. His labour is not in vain in the Lord. I pray for him and his family. I celebrate him today and every day. He will receive a crown of glory that fadeth not away.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Corinthians 1:30 KJV - "But of him are ye in Christ Jesus, who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption."
devotionals.devotional:
Most believers spend their lives trying to become righteous. They strive, they pray, they repent, they do good works — all in an attempt to be acceptable to God. But the gospel declares something radically different. You are not trying to become righteous; you already are righteous in Christ. He is your righteousness.

The Apostle Paul wrote, "For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him" (2 Corinthians 5:21 KJV). This is not a promise of future righteousness. This is a declaration of present reality. At the moment of salvation, you were made the righteousness of God in Christ. You did not earn it; you received it.

Christ Himself is your righteousness. When God looks at you, He does not see your failures; He sees His Son. You stand before Him as righteous as Jesus is righteous. This truth is not a licence to sin; it is a foundation for holy living.

But understand this: the righteousness that is yours in Christ is not a cover for ongoing sin. Scripture says, "Little children, let no man deceive you: he that doeth righteousness is righteous, even as he is righteous" (1 John 3:7 KJV). The one who is truly righteous in Him will practise righteousness. And Scripture also warns that the Lord disciplines those He loves, and chastens every son He receives (Hebrews 12:5-11 KJV).

Lesson: You are already the righteousness of God in Christ; but those who are truly righteous in Him will practise righteousness and not continue in sin.

Action: Today, when you feel unworthy or condemned, declare: "I am the righteousness of God in Christ." Then, examine your life and turn away from anything that does not reflect that identity.

Bible Portions — Here Is A Treasure Worth Stopping For.

  • in him: 2 Corinthians 5:21
    Christ is your Righteousness. He was made sin so that you might be made the righteousness of God in Him. Are you still trying to become righteous, when Christ has already made you righteous in Him?
  • of him: 1 Corinthians 1:30
    Christ is your Wisdom, Righteousness, Sanctification, and Redemption. And it is of Him that you are in Christ Jesus. Do you see Christ as your everything, or are you still searching elsewhere?
  • in Christ Jesus: 1 Corinthians 1:30
    Christ is the Place where all of this is found. You are not righteous in yourself; you are righteous in Him. Where are you looking for your righteousness today?
  • in him: Philippians 3:9
    Christ is the Righteousness that comes by faith. Paul wanted to be found in Him, not having his own righteousness. Whose righteousness are you actually standing in?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 5:17
    Christ is the Source of a new creation. If you are in Him, you are new. What old identity are you still wearing that Christ has already taken away?

Rest in this. You are not trying to become righteous. You are righteous in Him. Now live like it.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am the righteousness of God. I do not strive to earn Your approval; I rest in Your acceptance. I am righteous because of Jesus, and I choose to live righteously.

Confess this: I am the righteousness of God in Christ. I am accepted. I am approved. I am beloved. I do not strive to be righteous; I am righteous. And because I am righteous, I practise righteousness.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Corinthians 5:17 KJV - "Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new."
devotionals.devotional:
When you were born again, something radical happened. You did not simply turn over a new leaf. You did not merely add God to your life. You became an entirely new creation. The old person you were is gone. A brand new person has come. This is not a metaphor; it is a spiritual reality.

Scripture declares, "Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new" (2 Corinthians 5:17 KJV). The old nature — the sin nature you inherited from Adam — has been done away with. In its place, God has given you His own nature. You are a partaker of the divine nature (2 Peter 1:4 KJV).

Paul wrote to the Galatians, "For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision, but a new creature" (Galatians 6:15 KJV). What matters is not your religious background, your past failures, or your natural heritage. What matters is that you are a new creation in Christ.

But this new creation is not an excuse to live as you please. Scripture warns, "Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap. For he that soweth to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting" (Galatians 6:7-8 KJV). A new creation must still choose to walk after the Spirit and not after the flesh.

Lesson: In Christ, you are a completely new creation; but you must choose to walk after the Spirit and not after the flesh.

Action: Today, when the enemy reminds you of your past, declare: "I am a new creation in Christ." Then, sow to the Spirit by doing one thing that pleases God.

Bible Portions — There Is Newness Here. Look At It.

  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 5:17
    Christ is the Source of a new creation. If you are in Christ, you are not a patched-up old person — you are a new creature. Are you still living as the old person, or as the new creation Christ has made you?
  • in Christ Jesus: Galatians 6:15
    Christ is the Place where newness is found. Neither circumcision nor uncircumcision matters — only a new creature. What old label are you still wearing that Christ has already removed?
  • in Christ Jesus: Galatians 3:26
    Christ is the One through whom you are a child of God. You are not just a new creature; you are a new creature in a family. Whose family do you belong to?
  • in Christ Jesus: Galatians 3:28
    Christ is the One in whom all divisions are removed. There is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female. What division are you still holding on to that Christ has already removed?
  • in Christ Jesus: Galatians 5:6
    Christ is the One in whom faith works by love. What matters is not outward ritual, but faith working through love. Is your faith working through love today?

Live as the new creation. You are not who you were. You are who you are in Him. Walk in it.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am a new creation. The old person is gone. The new person has come. I choose to walk after the Spirit.

Confess this: I am a new creation in Christ. Old things have passed away. All things have become new. I am a partaker of the divine nature. I sow to the Spirit. I walk after the Spirit and not after the flesh. I am a child of God.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Ephesians 2:6 KJV - "And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus."
devotionals.devotional:
Where are you right now in the spirit realm? Many believers would answer, "I am on earth, struggling through life, trying to overcome my circumstances." But the Word of God gives a very different answer. In Christ, you are seated in heavenly places. You are not fighting for victory; you are fighting from victory.

Scripture declares, "And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus" (Ephesians 2:6 KJV). This is not a future promise; it is a present reality. You were raised with Christ. You are seated with Christ. His position is your position. His victory is your victory. His authority is your authority.

The Amplified Bible beautifully renders Ephesians 2:6 KJV: "And He raised us up together with Him and made us sit down together [giving us joint seating with Him] in the heavenly sphere [by virtue of our being] in Christ Jesus." You have joint seating with Jesus. You are not beneath your circumstances; you are above them.

But this seat of authority is not for those who live in disobedience. Scripture says, "If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God. Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth" (Colossians 3:1-2 KJV). To be seated with Him is to seek the things that are above. It is to put to death the deeds of the flesh (Colossians 3:5 KJV).

Lesson: In Christ, you are seated in heavenly places; but that position calls you to seek the things above and to put to death the deeds of the flesh.

Action: Today, when you face a challenge, remind yourself: "I am seated with Christ in heavenly places." Then, put away one thing in your life that does not belong to that position.

Bible Portions — Look Up. You Are Seated Higher Than You Think.

  • in Christ Jesus: Ephesians 2:6
    Christ is the Place of your seating. You are not beneath your circumstances; you are seated with Him above them. What circumstance are you still fighting from below?
  • with Christ: Ephesians 2:5
    Christ is the One who quickened you. You were dead, and He made you alive with Him. What dead thing are you still trying to resurrect in your own strength?
  • with Christ: Colossians 3:1
    Christ is the One you are risen with. Your position is above, not beneath. What are you still seeking below that you should be seeking above?
  • with Christ: Colossians 3:3
    Christ is the One your life is hidden with. Your life is secure in Him. What are you trying to protect that is already safe in Christ?
  • with him: Romans 8:32
    Christ is the One who is freely given. He who did not spare His own Son will freely give you all things with Him. What are you still doubting that God will give?

Sit in this. You are seated with Christ. Not beneath. Not beside. Seated with Him in heavenly places.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am seated in heavenly places. I have joint seating with Jesus. His position is my position. His victory is my victory. And I choose to seek the things above.

Confess this: I am seated with Christ in heavenly places. I am not beneath my circumstances; I am above them. I am not fighting for victory; I am fighting from victory. I seek the things above. I put to death the deeds of the flesh. I am more than a conqueror through Him who loves me.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 John 5:11 KJV - "And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son."
devotionals.devotional:
Eternal life is not something you will receive when you die. It is not a future hope. It is a present possession. The Bible declares, "And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son" (1 John 5:11 KJV). Notice the tense: hath given. Not will give. Not might give. He has given it. You have it now.

The Amplified Bible renders 1 John 5:11-12 this way: "And this is that testimony: God gave us eternal life, and this life is in His Son. He who possesses the Son has that life; he who does not possess the Son of God does not have that life." The question is not whether you will have eternal life someday. The question is whether you have the Son. If you have Jesus, you have eternal life.

Eternal life is not just endless existence; it is the very life of God. It is the God-kind of life imparted to your spirit at the new birth. Jesus said, "I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly" (John 10:10 KJV). This life is not something you produce; it is something you possess. It is not something you earn; it is something you receive. And it is found only in Him.

But the life that is in you must be lived out. Scripture says, "If ye continue in my word, then are ye my disciples indeed" (John 8:31 KJV). And again, "Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these... they which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God" (Galatians 5:19-21 KJV). If a believer turns away and continues in sin, Scripture warns that such a one will not inherit the kingdom.

Lesson: In Christ, you already possess eternal life; but you must continue in His Word and walk in the Spirit, for those who persist in the flesh will not inherit the kingdom.

Action: Today, thank God that you have eternal life in Christ. Then, examine your walk. Are you continuing in His Word? Take one step to abide more deeply in Him.

Bible Portions — Look Here. Life Is Not A Future Hope. It Is A Present Possession.

  • in his Son: 1 John 5:11
    Christ is the Location of eternal life. The life is not in a place; it is in a Person. Do you see eternal life as something you will receive, or as something you already possess in Him?
  • in him: 1 John 5:20
    Christ is the True God and Eternal Life. You are in Him who is true. What does it mean to you that your life is hidden in the One who is true?
  • in Christ Jesus: 2 Timothy 1:9
    Christ is the One in whom grace was given before the world began. Your salvation was not an afterthought. It was planned. What does that tell you about God's commitment to you?
  • in Christ Jesus: 2 Timothy 1:13
    Christ is the One in whom faith and love are found. You are not producing them on your own. They are in Him. Where are you trying to produce faith and love in your own strength?
  • in Christ: 1 Thessalonians 4:16
    Christ is the One in whom the dead shall rise first. Even death cannot separate you from Him. What fear are you carrying that Christ has already overcome?

Live in it. You have eternal life. Not someday. Now. Live as one who has it.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I have eternal life. It is not a future hope; it is a present possession. You have given it to me, and it is found in Your Son. And I choose to continue in Your Word.

Confess this: I have eternal life. This life is in Jesus, and I have Jesus. I have the God-kind of life in my spirit. I continue in His Word. I walk in the Spirit and not in the flesh. I have the assurance of heaven. I have eternal life in Him.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Romans 8:37 KJV - "Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us."
devotionals.devotional:
You are not a survivor. You are not someone barely holding on. You are not someone hoping to make it through. You are more than a conqueror. The word the Holy Spirit chose is a compound word that means you are super-conquerors. You do not just win; you win with overwhelming abundance.

Scripture says, "Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us" (Romans 8:37 KJV). Notice the phrase: through Him. Your victory is not in your own strength. It is not in your own ability. It is not in your own wisdom. It is through Him who loved you. Your victory flows out of your union with Christ.

The Amplified Bible renders Romans 8:37 this way: "Yet amid all these things we are more than conquerors and gain a surpassing victory through Him Who loved us." Paul goes on to list every conceivable threat — tribulation, persecution, famine, nakedness, peril, sword — and declares that none of them can separate you from the love of God in Christ Jesus. You are not just enduring; you are overcoming.

But this victory is not for those who turn back. Scripture says, "Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him" (Hebrews 10:38 KJV). The one who endures to the end shall be saved (Matthew 24:13 KJV). Your victory is secure in Christ, but you must continue in Him, grounded and settled, and not be moved away from the hope of the gospel (Colossians 1:23 KJV).

Lesson: Through Christ, you are more than a conqueror; but you must endure to the end and continue in the faith.

Action: Today, when you face a trial, declare: "I am more than a conqueror through Him who loved me." Then, take one step of enduring faith — do not draw back, but press forward in obedience.

Bible Portions — Stop Here. Victory Is Not Something You Are Fighting For.

  • through him: Romans 8:37
    Christ is the Channel of your victory. You are more than a conqueror through Him. What battle are you fighting as if the outcome depended on you alone?
  • in Christ Jesus: Romans 8:1
    Christ is the Place where there is no condemnation. You are not condemned. What condemnation are you still carrying that Christ has already removed?
  • in Christ Jesus: Romans 8:2
    Christ is the One who set you free. The law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has made you free. What are you still living as a slave to?
  • with him: Romans 8:17
    Christ is the One you suffer with and are glorified with. Your suffering is not meaningless. What suffering are you enduring that will one day be swallowed up in glory?
  • with him: Romans 6:8
    Christ is the One you died with and will live with. Your old life is buried with Him. What old life are you still trying to keep alive?

Walk in it. You are more than a conqueror. Not because of your strength, but because of His. Live in that victory.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that through Christ I am more than a conqueror. My victory is not in my own strength; it is in Him who loved me and gave Himself for me. And I choose to endure to the end.

Confess this: I am more than a conqueror through Him who loved me. No trial can separate me from His love. I am not a victim; I am a victor. I endure to the end. I continue in the faith, grounded and settled. My victory is in Christ.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Romans 5:1 KJV - "Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ."
devotionals.devotional:
Peace with God is not something you strive for; it is something you already have. It is not a feeling that comes and goes; it is a legal standing that was secured at Calvary. The moment you believed on Jesus, you were justified by faith, and you entered into peace with God.

Scripture declares, "Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ" (Romans 5:1 KJV). Notice the tense: we have. Not we will have. Not we hope to have. We have it now. The war between you and God is over. You are no longer His enemy; you are His child.

The Amplified Bible expands Romans 5:1-2: "Therefore, since we are justified (acquitted, declared righteous, and given a right standing with God) through faith, let us grasp the fact that we have the peace of reconciliation to hold and to enjoy peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. Through Him also we have our access (entrance, introduction) by faith into this grace in which we firmly and safely stand."

But this peace is not a licence to return to the very things from which you were saved. Scripture warns, "For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries" (Hebrews 10:26-27 KJV). The peace of God is for those who walk in the light, not for those who turn back to darkness.

Lesson: Through Christ, you already have peace with God; but you must walk in the light and not turn back to the darkness from which you were saved.

Action: Today, when anxiety rises, remind yourself: "I have peace with God through Jesus Christ." Then, walk in the light by confessing any sin and turning from it.

Bible Portions — There Is Peace Here. Look At It.

  • in Christ: Romans 12:5
    Christ is the One in whom you are joined to others. You are one body in Him. Who are you walking with in the body?
  • with him: Romans 6:4
    Christ is the One you were buried with and raised with. Your old life is buried. What old thing are you still trying to keep alive?
  • with him: Romans 6:6
    Christ is the One your old self was crucified with. The body of sin is done away with. What sin are you still living as if it has power over you?
  • with him: Romans 8:17
    Christ is the One you are a joint-heir with. Everything that belongs to Him belongs to you. What inheritance are you still doubting?
  • with him: Romans 8:32
    Christ is the One through whom all things are freely given. He who did not spare His own Son will freely give you all things. What are you still doubting that God will give?

Rest in this. You have peace with God. Not because of your performance, but because of His finished work. Live in that peace.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that through Christ I have peace with God. I am justified by faith. I am no longer Your enemy; I am Your child. And I choose to walk in the light.

Confess this: I have peace with God through my Lord Jesus Christ. I am justified by faith. I am no longer under condemnation. I walk in the light and not in darkness. My peace is not based on my feelings; it is based on His finished work.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Luke 19:10 KJV - "For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost."
devotionals.devotional:
We pause the In Him series today to focus on Mission Month. For the next two days, we will turn our attention to the mission of God — the great work of reaching the lost with the gospel of Jesus Christ. But mission is not merely a church programme. It is the heartbeat of God. It is the reason Jesus came into the world.

Jesus said, "For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost" (Luke 19:10 KJV). The mission of God began in the heart of the Father, was carried out by the Son, and is continued by the Holy Spirit through the church. The mission is not complete. There are still millions who have never heard the name of Jesus. There are still multitudes who are lost without hope. And God is calling His people to rise up and reach them.

Paul wrote, "For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth" (1 Timothy 2:3-4 KJV). God's desire is that all men be saved. His heart beats for the lost. His love reaches out to the nations. And He has chosen to accomplish His mission through His people — through you.

Mission is not just for missionaries. It is for every believer. You are a missionary wherever you are — in your home, your workplace, your community, and your city. You are called to be a witness for Jesus. This month, let the heartbeat of God become your heartbeat. Let the mission of God become your mission.

Lesson: Mission is the heartbeat of God; every believer is called to share the gospel and reach the lost.

Action: Today, ask God to give you His heart for the lost. Begin to pray for one person who does not yet know Jesus.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the mission of Your heart. I choose today to embrace the mission of God and to share the gospel with others.

Confess this: I am a missionary. I carry the heartbeat of God. I seek and save the lost. I share the gospel with those around me. I pray for the nations. I am committed to the mission of God.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Mark 16:15 KJV - "And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature."
devotionals.devotional:
We continue our pause from the In Him series today, as we conclude our focus on Mission Month. The mission of God is not a suggestion. It is a command. Before Jesus ascended into heaven, He gave His disciples a commission that has never been rescinded. It is called the Great Commission. It is the marching order for every believer until He returns.

Jesus said, "Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature" (Mark 16:15 KJV). The command is universal in scope. It is not just for the apostles. It is not just for pastors. It is not just for missionaries. It is for every believer. You are called to go. You are called to preach. You are called to make disciples.

After His resurrection, Jesus gave even more detail: "All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world" (Matthew 28:18-20 KJV).

The Great Commission is not just about preaching; it is about making disciples. It is about baptising new believers and teaching them to obey everything Jesus commanded. Mission is not complete until new believers are grounded in the faith and raised up to become disciples who make other disciples. This month, commit yourself afresh to the Great Commission.

Lesson: The Great Commission is the marching order for every believer; you are called to go, preach, and make disciples of all nations.

Action: Today, identify one person you can begin to disciple. If you have not shared the gospel with anyone this month, plan to do so before the week is over.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the Great Commission. I choose today to obey it and to make disciples of all nations.

Confess this: I go into all the world. I preach the gospel to every creature. I make disciples. I baptise them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. I teach them to obey everything Jesus commanded. I am committed to the Great Commission.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Colossians 2:10 KJV - "And ye are complete in him, which is the head of all principality and power."
devotionals.devotional:
We resume our In Him series today. Many believers live with a constant sense of lack. They feel incomplete. They feel they are missing something. They chase after experiences, blessings, and spiritual gifts, hoping to finally feel whole. But the Word of God declares that you are already complete in Christ.

Scripture says, "And ye are complete in him, which is the head of all principality and power" (Colossians 2:10 KJV). The word complete means filled up, lacking nothing, having everything you need. In Christ, you are not partially saved, partially healed, or partially blessed. You are complete. You lack nothing.

The Amplified Bible renders Colossians 2:9-10 this way: "For in Him the whole fullness of Deity (the Godhead) continues to dwell in bodily form [giving complete expression of the divine nature]. And you are in Him, made full and having come to fullness of life [in Christ you too are filled with the Godhead — Father, Son and Holy Spirit — and reach full spiritual stature]." Every believer is filled with the fullness of God.

But to be complete in Him is not to sit still. The one who is complete in Christ must continue to walk in Him, rooted and built up, established in the faith (Colossians 2:6-7 KJV). Scripture also warns, "Therefore we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard, lest at any time we should let them slip" (Hebrews 2:1 KJV).

Lesson: In Christ, you are complete and filled with the fullness of God; but you must continue to walk in Him and not let what you have heard slip away.

Action: Today, when you feel lacking or incomplete, declare: "I am complete in Christ. I am filled with the fullness of God." Then, take one step to continue walking in Him — read the Word, pray, and stay grounded.

Bible Portions — Stop And Look. What Treasure About Christ Do You See?

  • in him: Colossians 2:10
