    Christ is the Fullness of God in bodily form, and you are complete in Him. What part of your life are you still treating as incomplete?
  • in him: Colossians 2:6
    Christ is the One you received, and the One you walk in. You did not receive a doctrine; you received a Person. Are you walking in Him, or in your own effort?
  • in him: Colossians 2:7
    Christ is the Soil in which you are rooted. You are built up in Him. What are you rooted in right now — the Word, or the world?
  • in whom: Colossians 2:3
    Christ is the Treasury of all wisdom and knowledge. Every answer you need is hidden in Him. What question are you still trying to answer outside of Christ?
  • in whom: Colossians 2:11
    Christ is the One who circumcised your heart. The old nature has been cut off. What old nature are you still living as if it has power over you?

Live in this. You are complete in Christ. Not partially. Not almost. Complete. Live like it.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am complete. I am filled with Your fullness. I lack nothing. And I choose to continue walking in Him.

Confess this: I am complete in Christ. I am filled with the fullness of God — Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. I lack nothing. I continue to walk in Him, rooted and built up, established in the faith. I do not let the Word slip.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Ephesians 1:6 KJV - "To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved."
devotionals.devotional:
One of the deepest needs of the human heart is the need to be accepted. We long to belong. We long to be approved. We long to be welcomed. And in Christ, that need is fully and eternally met. You are accepted in the Beloved. Not tolerated. Not merely allowed. Accepted — fully, completely, forever.

Scripture says, "To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved" (Ephesians 1:6 KJV). The word accepted means to be highly favoured, to be received with delight, to be embraced. God does not merely permit you to come into His presence; He welcomes you with joy. He sees you in Christ, and because He loves His Son, He loves you.

The Amplified Bible renders Ephesians 1:4-6 this way: "Even as [in His love] He chose us [actually picked us out for Himself as His own] in Christ before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless in His sight, even above reproach, before Him in love. For He foreordained us to be adopted as His own children through Jesus Christ... [So that we might be] to the praise and the commendation of His glorious grace, which He so freely bestowed on us in the Beloved."

But being accepted does not mean being exempt from correction. Scripture says, "For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth" (Hebrews 12:6 KJV). And again, "Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off" (Romans 11:22 KJV). If a believer turns away and persists in sin, God will discipline him — and if he remains hardened, he can be cut off.

Lesson: In Christ, you are fully and eternally accepted by God; but you must continue in His goodness, for He disciplines those He loves.

Action: Today, when you feel rejected or unworthy, declare: "I am accepted in the Beloved." Then, examine your life and continue in His goodness, turning from anything that displeases Him.

Bible Portions — Here Is A Treasure Worth Stopping For.

  • in the beloved: Ephesians 1:6
    Christ is the Beloved in whom you are accepted. You are not accepted because of what you do; you are accepted because you are found in the One the Father loves. Do you know you are accepted, or are you still striving for approval?
  • in him: Ephesians 1:4
    Christ is the Place of your election. You were chosen in Him before the world began. Do you see yourself as chosen, or do you still live as an accident?
  • in whom: Ephesians 1:7
    Christ is the Fountain of redemption. The blood that purchased you is in Him. What guilt are you still carrying that has already been washed away?
  • in Christ: Ephesians 1:3
    Christ is the Treasury of every spiritual blessing. Every blessing is stored in Him. What blessing are you still begging for that has already been given?
  • in whom: Ephesians 1:11
    Christ is the Source of your inheritance. Your inheritance is not a future hope; it is a present reality. What are you treating as future that God has already given?

Rest in this. You are accepted in the Beloved. Not because you performed. Because you are in Him. Live in that acceptance.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am accepted in the Beloved. I do not strive for Your approval; I already have it. I am welcomed into Your presence with joy. And I choose to continue in Your goodness.

Confess this: I am accepted in the Beloved. I am highly favoured. I am received with delight. God sees me in Christ, and He loves me. I continue in His goodness. I walk in His ways. I am approved. I am welcomed. I am accepted.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Hebrews 4:16 KJV - "Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need."
devotionals.devotional:
Under the old covenant, only the high priest could enter the Holy of Holies, and only once a year, and only with great fear and trembling. The presence of God was veiled, restricted, and dangerous to approach. But under the new covenant, everything has changed. In Christ, you have boldness and access to God. You can come before His throne freely, confidently, and without fear.

Scripture says, "In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him" (Ephesians 3:12 KJV). Notice the phrase: in whom. Your access to God is not based on your own merit; it is based on your position in Christ. You do not come to God as a stranger; you come as a son or daughter.

The Amplified Bible renders Ephesians 3:12 this way: "In Whom, because of our faith in Him, we dare to have the boldness (courage and confidence) of free access — an unreserved approach to God with freedom and without fear." You have unreserved access. You have freedom. You have boldness. The veil has been torn from top to bottom. The way into the presence of God is wide open.

But this access is not for those who come with unrepentant hearts. Scripture says, "If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me" (Psalm 66:18 KJV). And again, "Who shall ascend into the hill of the Lord? or who shall stand in his holy place? He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart" (Psalm 24:3-4 KJV). The one who comes to the throne must come with clean hands and a pure heart.

Lesson: In Christ, you have boldness and free access to God; but you must come with clean hands and a pure heart, turning from iniquity.

Action: Today, approach God's throne boldly. But first, examine your heart. Confess any sin and turn from it, so that your access is not hindered.

Bible Portions — Look At This. The Door Is Open.

  • in whom: Ephesians 3:12
    Christ is the Door of access. In Him you have boldness and confidence. What are you still approaching God with fear about, when the door is wide open?
  • in whom: Ephesians 2:21
    Christ is the Cornerstone in whom the whole building is joined. You are part of that building. What part of the body are you still trying to stand apart from?
  • in whom: Ephesians 2:22
    Christ is the One in whom you are being built into a dwelling place of God. You are not just saved; you are being built. What is God building in you right now?
  • in Christ Jesus: Ephesians 2:13
    Christ is the One who brought you near by His blood. You were once far off; now you are near. What are you still treating as far off that Christ has brought near?
  • in Christ: Ephesians 3:6
    Christ is the One in whom you are a fellow heir. You are not an outsider; you are included. What are you still treating yourself as excluded from?

Come boldly. The door is open. The veil is torn. You have access. Use it.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I have boldness and access to You. I can come before Your throne with confidence and without fear. I am not a stranger; I am Your child. And I come with clean hands and a pure heart.

Confess this: I have boldness and access to God in Christ. I approach Your throne with confidence. I have unreserved access. I have freedom. I have boldness. I come with clean hands and a pure heart. I turn from iniquity, and You hear me.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Corinthians 1:30 KJV - "But of him are ye in Christ Jesus, who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption."
devotionals.devotional:
Many believers spend their lives searching for wisdom. They read books, attend conferences, seek counsel, and pursue knowledge. And these things have their place. Reading widely, studying diligently, and seeking wise counsel can sharpen the mind, build skill, and help you succeed in the physical realm. Solomon himself wrote, "The hand of the diligent shall bear rule: but the slothful shall be under tribute" (Proverbs 12:24 KJV). Diligence in study is not wasted.

Yet the Word of God declares that there is a wisdom higher than all of that. It is not something you must search for; it is a Person who lives inside you. Christ Himself is your wisdom.

Scripture says, "In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge" (Colossians 2:3 KJV). The Amplified Bible expands this: "In Him all the treasures of [divine] wisdom and [all the riches of spiritual] knowledge and enlightenment are stored up and lie hidden." Every treasure of wisdom — every insight, every revelation, every answer you will ever need — is hidden in Christ. And Christ lives in you.

Paul wrote, "But of him are ye in Christ Jesus, who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption" (1 Corinthians 1:30 KJV). Christ is not just the source of wisdom; He is your wisdom. You do not need to strive to become wise; you already possess the wisdom of God because you possess Christ. The Holy Spirit within you is your Teacher, your Guide, and your Counsellor.

But wisdom must be applied. Scripture says, "But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves" (James 1:22 KJV). The wise person is not the one who knows much, but the one who does what he knows. When you face a difficult decision, do not lean on your own understanding. Ask the Holy Spirit for wisdom, and then act on what He shows you.

Lesson: In Christ, you possess the very wisdom of God; but you must apply that wisdom by being a doer of the Word, not a hearer only.

Action: Today, when you face a decision, do not lean on your own understanding. Ask the Holy Spirit for wisdom, and then take one step of obedience based on what He shows you.

Bible Portions — There Is Treasure Here. Look.

  • in whom: Colossians 2:3
    Christ is the Treasury of wisdom and knowledge. Every answer you need is hidden in Him. What question are you still trying to answer outside of Christ?
  • of him: 1 Corinthians 1:30
    Christ is your Wisdom, Righteousness, Sanctification, and Redemption. And it is of Him that you are in Christ Jesus. Do you see Christ as your everything?
  • in Christ Jesus: 1 Corinthians 1:30
    Christ is the Place where all of this is found. You are not wise in yourself; you are wise in Him. Where are you looking for wisdom today?
  • in Christ: Colossians 2:5
    Christ is the One in whom your faith stands. Your faith is not in your own understanding; it is in Him. What are you still trying to figure out on your own?
  • in him: Colossians 2:6
    Christ is the One you walk in. Wisdom is not just knowing; it is walking. Are you walking in Him today, or in your own understanding?

Apply this. Christ is your wisdom. Not a book. Not a conference. A Person. Walk in Him.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I have wisdom. Christ Himself is my wisdom. The Holy Spirit lives in me and teaches me all things. And I choose to be a doer of the Word, not a hearer only.

Confess this: Christ is my wisdom. In Him are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. The Holy Spirit lives in me and guides me into all truth. I do not lean on my own understanding. I am a doer of the Word, not a hearer only. I apply the wisdom of God.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Romans 8:17 KJV - "And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together."
devotionals.devotional:
An heir is someone who has a legal right to an inheritance. An heir does not earn the inheritance; he receives it. He does not work for it; he is born into it. And in Christ, you have been born into the family of God. You are not just a servant; you are a son or daughter. And because you are a child, you are an heir.

Scripture says, "For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus" (Galatians 3:26 KJV). And again, "And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise" (Galatians 3:29 KJV). You are not just saved; you are adopted into God's family. You are not just forgiven; you are given a place at the table. You are an heir of God and a joint-heir with Jesus Christ.

The Amplified Bible renders Romans 8:17 this way: "And if we are [His] children, then we are [His] heirs also: heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ [sharing His inheritance with Him]." Everything that belongs to the Father belongs to you. Everything that belongs to Jesus belongs to you. You have a legal right to the inheritance of the saints in light.

But being an heir also means sharing in the suffering. Scripture says, "If so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together" (Romans 8:17 KJV). And again, "If we suffer, we shall also reign with him: if we deny him, he also will deny us" (2 Timothy 2:12 KJV). The heir who endures will inherit; the heir who turns back will not.

Lesson: In Christ, you are an heir of God and a joint-heir with Jesus; but you must endure and not deny Him, for the heir who turns back will not inherit.

Action: Today, think like an heir. Confess that you are a child of God and a joint-heir with Jesus. Then, take one step of enduring faith — do not deny Him, but press forward in obedience.

Bible Portions — Look At Your Inheritance. It Is Already Yours.

  • in Christ Jesus: Galatians 3:26
    Christ is the One through whom you are a child of God. You are not just saved; you are family. Whose family do you belong to?
  • in Christ Jesus: Galatians 3:28
    Christ is the One in whom all divisions are removed. You are one in Him. What division are you still holding on to that Christ has already removed?
  • with him: Romans 8:17
    Christ is the One you suffer with and are glorified with. Your suffering is not meaningless. What suffering are you enduring that will one day be swallowed up in glory?
  • with him: 2 Timothy 2:11
    Christ is the One you died with and will live with. Your old life is buried with Him. What old life are you still trying to keep alive?
  • with him: 2 Timothy 2:12
    Christ is the One you suffer with and will reign with. If you endure, you will reign. What are you being tempted to give up on right now?

Walk as an heir. You are not a servant. You are a son. You are a daughter. You are an heir. Live like it.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am Your child and an heir. I have a legal right to the inheritance of the saints. I am a joint-heir with Jesus. And I choose to endure and not deny Him.

Confess this: I am a child of God. I am an heir of God and a joint-heir with Jesus. Everything that belongs to the Father belongs to me. I endure with Him. I do not deny Him. I will reign with Him. I claim my inheritance by faith.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Corinthians 6:11 KJV - "And such were some of you: but ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God."
devotionals.devotional:
Sanctification is not something you achieve; it is something you receive. It is not a process you complete; it is a position you already hold. In Christ, you have been sanctified — set apart, made holy, consecrated to God. This is not a future hope; it is a present reality.

Paul wrote to the Corinthians, "Unto the church of God which is at Corinth, to them that are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints" (1 Corinthians 1:2 KJV). Notice the tense: are sanctified. Not will be sanctified. Not are trying to be sanctified. They were already sanctified in Christ. They were already called saints.

The Amplified Bible renders 1 Corinthians 6:11 this way: "And such some of you were [once]. But you were washed clean (purified by a complete atonement for sin and made free from the guilt of sin), and you were consecrated (set apart, hallowed), and you were justified [pronounced righteous, by trusting] in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the [Holy] Spirit of our God." You were washed. You were sanctified. You were justified. These are past-tense realities that you possess right now.

But sanctification is not only a position; it is also a practice. Scripture says, "For this is the will of God, even your sanctification, that ye should abstain from fornication" (1 Thessalonians 4:3 KJV). And again, "Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord" (Hebrews 12:14 KJV). The one who is sanctified must pursue holiness.

Lesson: In Christ, you have already been sanctified and set apart; but you must pursue holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord.

Action: Today, when you feel unworthy or unholy, declare: "I am sanctified in Christ Jesus." Then, pursue holiness by turning away from anything that defiles.

Bible Portions — Look Here. You Are Already Set Apart.

  • in Christ Jesus: 1 Corinthians 1:2
    Christ is the Place where you are sanctified. You are not trying to become holy; you are holy in Him. What are you still trying to earn that Christ has already given?
  • in Christ: Colossians 1:2
    Christ is the One in whom you are a saint. You are not just forgiven; you are set apart. Do you see yourself as a saint, or as a sinner who is trying harder?
  • in Christ: Colossians 1:28
    Christ is the One in whom you are presented perfect. You are not being presented as a work in progress; you are presented complete in Him. What are you still trying to perfect in your own strength?
  • in Christ Jesus: 2 Timothy 3:12
    Christ is the One in whom you live godly. Godliness is not your achievement; it is your life in Him. What are you trying to achieve that Christ has already accomplished?
  • in Christ Jesus: 2 Timothy 3:15
    Christ is the One in whom salvation is found. You are not saved by your works; you are saved by faith in Him. What are you still trying to add to the finished work of Christ?

Walk in holiness. You are sanctified in Christ. Now pursue the holiness that matches your position.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am sanctified. I have been washed, set apart, and made holy. And I choose to pursue holiness in my daily life.

Confess this: I am sanctified in Christ Jesus. I am washed clean. I am set apart. I am a saint of God. I pursue holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord. My sanctification is based on my position in Christ, and it is lived out in my practice.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Ephesians 1:7 KJV - "In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace."
devotionals.devotional:
Forgiveness is not something you must beg for. It is not something you must earn. It is not something that is granted reluctantly after you have punished yourself enough. In Christ, you have forgiveness of sins. It is a present possession, secured by the blood of Jesus and given freely by the grace of God.

Paul declared in the synagogue at Antioch, "Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins: And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses" (Acts 13:38-39 KJV). Through Jesus, forgiveness is preached. Through Jesus, you are justified. Through Jesus, you are cleansed from all things.

The Amplified Bible renders Ephesians 1:7 this way: "In Him we have redemption through His blood, the remission of our offenses, in accordance with the riches and the generosity of His gracious favour." Notice that your forgiveness is according to the riches of His grace, not according to the magnitude of your sin. No sin is too great for His grace. The blood of Jesus cleanses you from all sin.

But forgiveness is not a licence to continue in sin. Scripture says, "What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? God forbid. How shall we, that are dead to sin, live any longer therein?" (Romans 6:1-2 KJV). The one who has been forgiven must not return to the sin that was forgiven. And if a believer sins again, he must confess it and turn from it, for God is faithful and just to forgive (1 John 1:9 KJV).

Lesson: Through Christ, you already have complete forgiveness of sins; but you must not continue in sin, for forgiveness calls you to walk in newness of life.

Action: Today, if the enemy reminds you of a past sin, declare: "I am forgiven. The blood of Jesus has cleansed me." Then, walk in newness of life, refusing to return to the old patterns.

Bible Portions — There Is Freedom Here. Look.

  • in whom: Ephesians 1:7
    Christ is the Fountain of redemption. The blood that purchased you is in Him. What guilt are you still carrying that has already been washed away?
  • by him: Acts 13:38-39
    Christ is the One through whom forgiveness is preached. Your forgiveness is not a theory; it is a proclamation. Have you received it as a present reality?
  • in whom: Colossians 1:14
    Christ is the One in whom you have redemption and forgiveness. It is not something you are waiting for; it is something you have. What are you still waiting for that Christ has already given?
  • by him: Colossians 1:20
    Christ is the Peacemaker. By Him, God reconciled all things to Himself. What area of your life still needs to be reconciled to Him?
  • in him: 2 Corinthians 5:21
    Christ is your Righteousness. He was made sin so that you might be made the righteousness of God in Him. What are you still trying to pay for that Christ has already paid?

Walk in forgiveness. You are forgiven. Not partially. Not temporarily. Fully and forever. Live like it.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that through Christ I have forgiveness of sins. I am cleansed by His blood. I am justified by His grace. And I choose to walk in newness of life.

Confess this: I am forgiven. The blood of Jesus has cleansed me from all sin. I am justified. God remembers my sins no more. I do not continue in sin. I walk in newness of life. I am free in Christ.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Colossians 3:1 KJV - "If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God."
devotionals.devotional:
When Jesus rose from the dead, you rose with Him. This is one of the most profound truths in the New Testament. You are not just forgiven; you are raised. You are not just pardoned; you are given a new life. The resurrection of Jesus was not just a historical event; it was your resurrection too.

Scripture says, "Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life. For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection" (Romans 6:4-5 KJV). You were buried with Him, and you were raised with Him. His resurrection is your resurrection.

The Amplified Bible renders Colossians 3:1 this way: "If then you have been raised with Christ [to a new life, thus sharing His resurrection from the dead], aim at and seek the rich, eternal treasures that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God." You have been raised with Christ. You share in His resurrection.

But this new life is not a life of ease or compromise. Scripture says, "Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry: For which things' sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience" (Colossians 3:5-6 KJV). To be raised with Christ is to put to death the old ways. If you return to them, you invite the very wrath from which you were saved.

Lesson: With Christ, you have been raised to newness of life; but you must put to death the old ways, for returning to them invites the wrath of God.

Action: Today, set your affection on things above. Put to death one thing in your life that belongs to the old nature.

Bible Portions — Look Up. You Are Risen With Him.

  • with him: Romans 6:4
    Christ is the One you were buried with and raised with. Your old life is buried. What old thing are you still trying to keep alive?
  • with him: Romans 6:6
    Christ is the One your old self was crucified with. The body of sin is done away with. What sin are you still living as if it has power over you?
  • with him: Romans 6:8
    Christ is the One you died with and will live with. Your life is now hidden in His. What are you still trying to live out that belongs to your old life?
  • with Christ: Galatians 2:20
    Christ is the One you are crucified with. It is no longer you who live, but Christ lives in you. What part of you are you still trying to keep on the throne?
  • with Christ: Colossians 2:20
    Christ is the One you died with. You have died to the world's rudiments. What worldly rule are you still living under that Christ has already freed you from?

Walk in newness. You are risen with Christ. You are not who you were. Live as who you are.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that with Christ I have been raised to newness of life. My old nature is dead. My new life is hidden with Christ in You. And I choose to put to death the old ways.

Confess this: I have been raised with Christ. I walk in newness of life. My old nature is dead. I put to death the deeds of the flesh. I set my affection on things above. I live out of my resurrection life in Christ.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Corinthians 5:18 KJV - "And all things are of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation."
devotionals.devotional:
Reconciliation means that a broken relationship has been restored. It means that hostility has ended, distance has been closed, and peace has been established. In Christ, you have been reconciled to God. You are no longer estranged. You are no longer alienated. You are no longer an enemy. You are a friend, a child, and an heir.

Scripture says, "And all things are of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation" (2 Corinthians 5:18 KJV). Notice the tense: hath reconciled. It is already done. God did not wait for you to make things right. He took the initiative. He sent Jesus. He accomplished the reconciliation. You are reconciled.

Paul wrote to the Colossians, "And, having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things unto himself... And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled in the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and unreproveable in his sight: If ye continue in the faith grounded and settled, and be not moved away from the hope of the gospel" (Colossians 1:20-23 KJV).

Notice that last phrase — if ye continue in the faith. Reconciliation is real and complete, but it is for those who continue in the faith. Scripture warns, "For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning" (2 Peter 2:20 KJV).

Lesson: By Christ, you have been reconciled to God; but you must continue in the faith, grounded and settled, and not be moved away from the hope of the gospel.

Action: Today, thank God for your reconciliation. Then, take a step to remain grounded in the faith — read the Word, pray, and stay connected to the body of Christ.

Bible Portions — Look Here. You Have Been Brought Near.

  • by him: Colossians 1:20
    Christ is the Peacemaker. By Him, God reconciled all things to Himself. What area of your life still needs to be reconciled to Him?
  • by him: Colossians 3:17
    Christ is the One through whom you give thanks. All that you do, you do in His name, giving thanks by Him. Is your life marked by thanksgiving?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 5:19
    Christ is the One in whom God was reconciling the world to Himself. You are part of that reconciliation. Who are you carrying that message to?
  • in him: 2 Corinthians 1:20
    Christ is the Yes and Amen of every promise. Every promise of God finds its Yes in Him. What promise are you still doubting?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 3:14
    Christ is the One in whom the veil is taken away. You can see clearly now. What are you still living as if you cannot see?

Walk in reconciliation. You have been brought near. Now live as one who is near.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that by Christ I have been reconciled to You. I am no longer alienated. I am no longer an enemy. I am Your child. And I choose to continue in the faith.

Confess this: I am reconciled to God. I am no longer alienated. I am presented holy, blameless, and above reproach. I continue in the faith, grounded and settled. I am not moved away from the hope of the gospel. I have a ministry of reconciliation.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Ephesians 3:17 KJV - "That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love."
devotionals.devotional:
Stability is not a luxury; it is a necessity for the Christian life. You need to be rooted, established, and built up so that you cannot be moved by every wind of doctrine, every trial, or every attack of the enemy. And the good news is that in Christ, you are already rooted, already built up, and already established.

Scripture says, "As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him: Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving" (Colossians 2:6-7 KJV). You received Christ, and you walk in Him. You are rooted in Him. You are built up in Him. You are established in the faith.

The Amplified Bible renders Colossians 2:7 this way: "Have the roots [of your being] firmly and deeply planted [in Him, fixed and founded in Him], being continually built up in Him, becoming increasingly more confirmed and established in the faith, just as you were taught, and abounding and overflowing in it with thanksgiving." Your roots are in Christ. Your foundation is in Christ. Your stability is in Christ.

But being rooted does not mean being immovable in the wrong direction. Scripture warns, "Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ" (Colossians 2:8 KJV). The one who is rooted in Christ must be on guard against deception. Stability is only stable if it is in the truth.

Lesson: In Christ, you are rooted, built up, and established; but you must guard your heart against deception and remain rooted in the truth.

Action: Today, identify one area where you have felt unstable. Remind yourself that you are rooted and established in Christ. Then, guard yourself against any teaching that contradicts the Word of God.

Bible Portions — Stop Here. You Are Rooted Deeper Than You Know.

  • in him: Colossians 2:6
    Christ is the One you walk in. You received Him, and you walk in Him. Are you walking in Him today, or in your own effort?
  • in him: Colossians 2:7
    Christ is the Soil in which you are rooted. You are built up in Him. What are you rooted in right now — the Word, or the world?
  • in whom: Colossians 2:3
    Christ is the Treasury of all wisdom and knowledge. Every answer you need is hidden in Him. What question are you still trying to answer outside of Christ?
  • in Christ: Colossians 2:5
    Christ is the One in whom your faith stands. Your faith is not in your own understanding; it is in Him. What are you still trying to figure out on your own?
  • in him: 1 John 2:6
    Christ is the One you abide in, and the One you walk as. If you abide in Him, you walk as He walked. Is your walk matching your position?

Stand firm. You are rooted in Christ. Not shallowly. Deeply. Stand firm in Him.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am rooted, built up, and established. I am not tossed to and fro. And I choose to guard my heart against deception.

Confess this: I am rooted in Christ. I am built up in Him. I am established in the faith. I am not moved by every wind of doctrine. I am on guard against deception. I remain rooted in the truth. I am stable. I am firm.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Ephesians 1:11 KJV - "In whom also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will."
devotionals.devotional:
Before the world began, God made a decision about you. He did not choose you because of anything you would do. He did not choose you because of your background, your abilities, or your potential. He chose you because He wanted you. He chose you in Christ, and He chose you in love.

Scripture says, "According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will" (Ephesians 1:4-5 KJV). You were chosen in Him before the foundation of the world. You were predestined to be adopted as God's own child through Jesus Christ.

The Amplified Bible renders Ephesians 1:4 this way: "Even as [in His love] He chose us [actually picked us out for Himself as His own] in Christ before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy (consecrated and set apart for Him) and blameless in His sight, even above reproach, before Him in love." You are not an afterthought. You are not a mistake. You are chosen, picked out, and set apart for God Himself.

But being chosen does not mean being exempt from responsibility. Scripture says, "Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall" (2 Peter 1:10 KJV). Election must be confirmed by a life of obedience. The chosen one must walk worthy of the calling with which he is called (Ephesians 4:1 KJV).

Lesson: In Christ, you were chosen and predestined by God before the foundation of the world; but you must make your calling and election sure by a life of obedience.

Action: Today, thank God that He chose you in Christ before the world began. Then, examine your life and confirm your election through obedience.

Bible Portions — Look At This. You Were Chosen Before You Were Born.

  • in him: Ephesians 1:4
    Christ is the Place of your election. You were chosen in Him before the world began. Do you see yourself as chosen, or do you still live as an accident?
  • in whom: Ephesians 1:11
    Christ is the Source of your inheritance. Your inheritance is not a future hope; it is a present reality. What are you treating as future that God has already given?
  • in Christ: Ephesians 1:10
    Christ is the Centre of all things. God's plan is to gather all things in Him. Is Christ the centre of your life, or is something else?
  • in Christ: Ephesians 1:12
    Christ is the Ground of your hope. You first trusted in Christ. Where is your trust actually resting?
  • in whom: Ephesians 1:13
    Christ is the Seal of your security. You were sealed with the Holy Spirit when you believed. Are you living in the confidence of that seal, or in doubt?

Walk as the chosen. You were not chosen because of what you would do. You were chosen because of who He is. Live worthy of that calling.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that You chose me in Christ before the foundation of the world. I am not an afterthought. I am chosen and beloved. And I choose to make my calling and election sure.

Confess this: I am chosen in Christ. I am predestined to be adopted as God's own child. I am holy and blameless before Him in love. I make my calling and election sure. I walk worthy of the calling with which I am called. I am chosen and beloved.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Colossians 1:12 KJV - "Giving thanks unto the Father, which hath made us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light."
devotionals.devotional:
You have an inheritance. It is not something you are waiting to receive when you die. It is not something that is stored away for a distant future. In Christ, you have already obtained an inheritance. It is yours now, and it is yours forever. The Father has made you able to share in it.

Scripture says, "In whom also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will: That we should be to the praise of his glory, who first trusted in Christ" (Ephesians 1:11-12 KJV). You have obtained an inheritance. It is already yours in Him.

The Amplified Bible renders Colossians 1:12 this way: "Giving thanks to the Father, Who has qualified and made us fit to share the portion which is the inheritance of the saints (God's holy people) in the Light." You have been made able to partake. You have been qualified for the inheritance. You did not qualify yourself; God qualified you.

But an inheritance can be squandered. Scripture tells of the prodigal son who wasted his inheritance in riotous living (Luke 15:13 KJV). You can possess an inheritance and yet lose its benefits by living for the flesh. Scripture warns that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God (1 Corinthians 6:9 KJV). The inheritance is yours, but you must walk worthy of it.

Lesson: In Christ, you have already obtained an inheritance; but you must walk worthy of it, for an inheritance can be squandered by those who return to the flesh.

Action: Today, thank God for your inheritance. Then, walk worthy of it — refuse to squander it by living for the flesh.

Bible Portions — Look Here. Your Inheritance Is Already Yours.

  • in whom: Ephesians 1:11
    Christ is the Source of your inheritance. You have obtained it. What inheritance are you still waiting to receive that has already been given?
  • in whom: Ephesians 1:13
    Christ is the Seal of your security. You were sealed with the Holy Spirit. Are you living in the confidence of that seal?
  • in Christ: Ephesians 1:12
    Christ is the Ground of your hope. You first trusted in Christ. Where is your trust actually resting?
  • in Christ: Colossians 1:2
    Christ is the One in whom you are a saint. You are not just forgiven; you are set apart. Do you see yourself as a saint?
  • in Christ: Colossians 1:28
    Christ is the One in whom you are presented perfect. You are not being presented as a work in progress; you are presented complete in Him. What are you still trying to perfect in your own strength?

Walk worthy. You have an inheritance. It is already yours. Now live like an heir.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I have obtained an inheritance. You have qualified me to share in everything that belongs to Your children. And I choose to walk worthy of it.

Confess this: I have obtained an inheritance in Christ. I am qualified to share in the inheritance of the saints. Healing, provision, peace, joy, and eternal life belong to me. I walk worthy of my inheritance. I do not squander it. I claim my inheritance by faith.

devotionals.topic: Sealed Until The Day Of Redemption
devotionals.memoryVerse: Ephesians 1:13 KJV - "In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise."
devotionals.devotional:
When you believed the gospel, something happened to you that cannot be undone by outside forces. You were sealed with the Holy Spirit. A seal is a mark of ownership. It is a guarantee. It is a pledge. God placed His own Spirit inside you as a seal, declaring that you belong to Him and that He will complete what He started.

Scripture says, "In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory" (Ephesians 1:13-14 KJV). You were sealed with the Holy Spirit. He is the down payment, the guarantee, the pledge of your full inheritance.

The Amplified Bible renders Ephesians 1:13 this way: "In Him you also who have heard the Word of Truth, the glad tidings (Gospel) of your salvation, and have believed in and adhered to and relied on Him, were stamped with the seal of the long-promised Holy Spirit." You are stamped with God's seal. You are marked as His own.

But the seal is not a guarantee for those who do not continue. Scripture says, "And you... hath he reconciled... If ye continue in the faith grounded and settled, and be not moved away from the hope of the gospel" (Colossians 1:21-23 KJV). The one who is sealed must continue in Him. Scripture also warns, "Cast not away therefore your confidence, which hath great recompence of reward" (Hebrews 10:35 KJV).

Lesson: In Christ, you are sealed with the Holy Spirit; but you must continue in the faith, grounded and settled, and not be moved away from the hope of the gospel.

Action: Today, when doubt about your salvation arises, declare: "I am sealed with the Holy Spirit." Then, continue in the faith by staying grounded in the Word and in prayer.

Bible Portions — Stop Here. You Are Sealed.

  • in whom: Ephesians 1:13
    Christ is the Seal of your security. You were sealed with the Holy Spirit when you believed. Are you living in the confidence of that seal, or in doubt?
  • in whom: Ephesians 1:11
    Christ is the Source of your inheritance. Your inheritance is not a future hope; it is a present reality. What are you treating as future that God has already given?
  • in Christ: Ephesians 1:12
    Christ is the Ground of your hope. You first trusted in Christ. Where is your trust actually resting?
  • in the beloved: Ephesians 1:6
    Christ is the Beloved in whom you are accepted. You are not accepted because of what you do; you are accepted because you are found in the One the Father loves. Do you know you are accepted?
  • in him: Ephesians 1:4
    Christ is the Place of your election. You were chosen in Him before the world began. Do you see yourself as chosen?

Walk in confidence. You are sealed. Not tentatively. Not conditionally. Sealed. Live in that security.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am sealed with the Holy Spirit. I belong to You. And I choose to continue in the faith, grounded and settled.

Confess this: I am sealed with the Holy Spirit. I am marked as God's own possession. I continue in the faith. I am grounded and settled. I am not moved away from the hope of the gospel. No power can undo that seal. I am secure in Christ.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Colossians 2:13 KJV - "And you, being dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, hath he quickened together with him, having forgiven you all trespasses."
devotionals.devotional:
You were once dead. Not sick, not weak, not struggling — dead. Dead in trespasses and sins. You had no spiritual life, no connection to God, no ability to respond to Him. But God, in His rich mercy and great love, did something about it. He made you alive together with Christ.

Scripture says, "But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us, Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ, (by grace ye are saved)" (Ephesians 2:4-5 KJV). God did not wait for you to become worthy. He did not wait for you to clean yourself up. He quickened you — He made you alive — while you were still dead in your sins.

The Amplified Bible renders Colossians 2:13 this way: "And you who were dead in trespasses and in the uncircumcision of your flesh (your sensuality, your sinful carnal nature), [God] brought to life together with [Christ], having [freely] forgiven us all our transgressions." You were brought to life together with Christ. You were made alive. The same power that raised Jesus from the dead raised you from spiritual death.

But the life that was given to you must be lived out. Scripture says, "If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God" (Colossians 3:1 KJV). The one who has been made alive must live in newness of life. And if a believer turns back to the death from which he was saved, Scripture warns that the latter end is worse than the beginning (2 Peter 2:20 KJV).

Lesson: In Christ, you have been made alive together with Him; but you must live in newness of life, for turning back to death brings a worse end.

Action: Today, thank God that He made you alive together with Christ. Then, seek the things above and live in newness of life.

Bible Portions — Look At This. You Were Dead. Now You Are Alive.

  • with him: Colossians 2:13
    Christ is the One who quickened you. You were dead, and He made you alive. What dead thing are you still trying to resurrect in your own strength?
  • with him: Colossians 2:12
    Christ is the One you were buried with and raised with. Your old life is buried. What old thing are you still trying to keep alive?
  • in Christ Jesus: Ephesians 2:6
    Christ is the Place of your seating. You are seated with Him above your circumstances. What circumstance are you still fighting from below?
  • in Christ Jesus: Ephesians 2:10
    Christ is the One in whom you are God's workmanship. You are not an accident; you are a masterpiece. Do you see yourself as God's workmanship?
  • in Christ Jesus: Ephesians 2:13
    Christ is the One who brought you near by His blood. You were once far off; now you are near. What are you still treating as far off that Christ has brought near?

Walk in newness. You were dead. Now you are alive. Live like it.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that You made me alive together with Christ. I was dead in my sins, but You quickened me. And I choose to live in newness of life.

Confess this: I am made alive together with Christ. I am quickened by the power of God. I am no longer dead in my sins. I am alive to God. I seek the things above. I live in newness of life. I do not return to death.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Ephesians 2:19 KJV - "Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellow citizens with the saints, and of the household of God."
devotionals.devotional:
You are not an outsider. You are not a stranger. You are not a foreigner. In Christ, you are a fellow citizen with the saints and a member of God's own household. You belong to the family of God. You have a place at the table. You have a room in the Father's house.

Scripture says, "Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellow citizens with the saints, and of the household of God; And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone; In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord: In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit" (Ephesians 2:19-22 KJV).

The Amplified Bible renders Ephesians 2:21 this way: "In Him the whole structure is joined (bound, welded) together harmoniously, and it continues to rise (grow, increase) into a holy temple in the Lord." You are part of a greater structure. You are a living stone in God's building. You are being built together with other believers into a dwelling place for God.

But a living stone must remain in the building. Scripture says, "If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire" (1 Corinthians 3:14-15 KJV). Not all who begin in the household of God remain faithful. And Scripture warns that some will be cut off if they do not continue in His goodness (Romans 11:22 KJV).

Lesson: In Christ, you are no longer a stranger or foreigner; you are a fellow citizen with the saints and of God's household; but you must remain in the household and continue in His goodness.

Action: Today, thank God that you belong to His family. Then, strengthen your bond with the body of Christ by connecting with another believer.

Bible Portions — Look Here. You Belong.

  • in whom: Ephesians 2:21
    Christ is the Cornerstone in whom the whole building is joined. You are part of that building. What part of the body are you still trying to stand apart from?
  • in whom: Ephesians 2:22
    Christ is the One in whom you are being built into a dwelling place of God. You are not just saved; you are being built. What is God building in you right now?
  • in Christ: Ephesians 3:6
    Christ is the One in whom you are a fellow heir. You are not an outsider; you are included. What are you still treating yourself as excluded from?
  • in whom: Ephesians 3:12
    Christ is the Door of access. In Him you have boldness and confidence. What are you still approaching God with fear about, when the door is wide open?
  • in Christ Jesus: Ephesians 3:11
    Christ is the One in whom God's eternal purpose is accomplished. You are part of that purpose. What purpose are you still trying to find outside of Christ?

Walk as family. You belong. Not because you earned a place. Because you are in Him. Live as a member of the household.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am no longer a stranger or foreigner. I am a fellow citizen with the saints and of Your household. And I choose to remain in Your family.

Confess this: I am a fellow citizen with the saints. I am of the household of God. I am a living stone in God's building. I remain in the household. I continue in His goodness. I am being built together with other believers into a dwelling place for God.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Ephesians 3:6 KJV - "That the Gentiles should be fellow heirs, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the gospel."
devotionals.devotional:
In the Old Covenant, the Gentiles were outsiders. They were not part of Israel. They were not part of the covenant. They had no access to the promises of God. But in Christ, everything changed. In Christ, the Gentiles are fellow heirs, members of the same body, and partakers of the same promise.

Scripture says, "That the Gentiles should be fellow heirs, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the gospel" (Ephesians 3:6 KJV). This is the mystery that was hidden for ages but revealed in Christ: there is no longer Jew or Gentile. There is no longer insider or outsider. In Christ, all believers share the same inheritance, belong to the same body, and partake of the same promise.

The Amplified Bible renders Ephesians 3:6 this way: "That the Gentiles are now to be fellow heirs [with the Jews], members of the same body and joint partakers [sharing] in the same divine promise in Christ through [their acceptance of] the glad tidings (the Gospel)." You share equally with every other believer. Your heritage, your membership, your promise is the same as any other saint of God.

But belonging to the body requires walking in love. Scripture says, "I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you that ye walk worthy of the vocation wherewith ye are called, With all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love; Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace" (Ephesians 4:1-3 KJV). If you are part of the body, you must walk in love toward the body.

Lesson: In Christ, you are a fellow heir, a member of the same body, and a joint partaker of the promise; but you must walk in love and keep the unity of the Spirit.

Action: Today, reach out to a believer from a different background and walk in love toward them. Strengthen the unity of the body of Christ.

Bible Portions — Look Here. You Are Not An Outsider.

  • in Christ: Ephesians 3:6
    Christ is the One in whom you are a fellow heir. You are not an outsider; you are included. What are you still treating yourself as excluded from?
  • in Christ: Ephesians 3:11
    Christ is the One in whom God's eternal purpose is accomplished. You are part of that purpose. What purpose are you still trying to find outside of Christ?
  • in whom: Ephesians 3:12
    Christ is the Door of access. In Him you have boldness and confidence. What are you still approaching God with fear about?
  • in Christ Jesus: Philippians 1:1
    Christ is the One in whom you are a saint. You are not just forgiven; you are set apart. Do you see yourself as a saint?
  • in Christ Jesus: Philippians 1:26
    Christ is the One in whom your rejoicing abounds. Your joy is not circumstantial; it is in Him. What are you still trying to find joy in outside of Christ?

Walk in unity. You are part of the body. Not a spectator. A member. Live like it.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am a fellow heir, a member of the same body, and a joint partaker of Your promise. And I choose to walk in love and keep the unity of the Spirit.

Confess this: I am a fellow heir in Christ. I am a member of the same body. I am a joint partaker of the promise. I walk in love. I keep the unity of the Spirit. I am fully included in the family of God.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Ephesians 4:15 KJV - "But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ."
devotionals.devotional:
Growth is not optional for the Christian. You are called to grow up in Christ — in every area, in every dimension, in every aspect of your life. And this growth happens as you speak the truth in love and as you are joined together with the rest of the body of Christ.

Scripture says, "But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ: From whom the whole body fitly joined together and compacted by that which every joint supplieth, according to the effectual working in the measure of every part, maketh increase of the body unto the edifying of itself in love" (Ephesians 4:15-16 KJV). You grow up into Him. He is your Head. You are part of His body. And as every part functions properly, the body grows in love.

The Amplified Bible renders Ephesians 4:16 this way: "For because of Him the whole body (the church, in all its various parts), closely joined and firmly knit together by the joints and ligaments with which it is supplied, when each part [with power adapted to its need] is working properly [in all its functions], grows to full maturity, building itself up in love." You are part of a body. You have a function.

But growth requires maturity, and maturity requires putting away childish things. Scripture says, "When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things" (1 Corinthians 13:11 KJV). The believer who does not grow can be caught in deception and carried about with every wind of doctrine (Ephesians 4:14 KJV). Growth is not just a blessing; it is a protection.

Lesson: In Christ, you are called to grow up in Him; growth protects you from deception and enables you to build up the body in love.

Action: Today, identify one way you can contribute to the growth of the body of Christ. Speak the truth in love and use your gifts to build others up.

Bible Portions — Look Here. You Are Growing.

  • in Christ Jesus: Philippians 3:3
    Christ is the One in whom you rejoice. Your joy is not circumstantial; it is in Him. What are you still trying to find joy in outside of Christ?
  • in Christ Jesus: Philippians 3:14
    Christ is the One in whom the prize is found. You are pressing toward the mark. What are you still chasing that is not the prize?
  • in Christ Jesus: Philippians 4:7
    Christ is the One in whom peace guards your heart and mind. Your peace is not circumstantial; it is in Him. What are you still trying to control that you should be trusting to Him?
  • in Christ Jesus: Philippians 4:19
    Christ is the One in whom your needs are supplied. Your supply is not in the economy; it is in Him. What need are you still doubting that God will supply?
  • in Christ Jesus: Philippians 4:21
    Christ is the One in whom every saint is greeted. You are part of a family. Who in the body are you still holding at arm's length?

Grow up in Him. You are not meant to stay a spiritual child. You are meant to grow. Grow up into Him in all things.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am called to grow up in Him. I am part of His body. And I choose to grow into maturity and to build others up in love.

Confess this: I grow up into Christ in all things. He is my Head. I am part of His body. I put away childish things. I am not carried about by every wind of doctrine. I speak the truth in love. I build others up, and I am built up in love.

devotionals.topic: World Children's Day: Growing In Christ
devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Peter 2:2 KJV - "As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby."
devotionals.devotional:
We pause the In Him series today to mark World Children's Day. Around the world, attention is turned to the well-being, protection, and future of children. As believers, we have a special reason to celebrate this day. Children are a gift from God, and they hold a special place in His heart. But this day also reminds us of a spiritual truth: every believer begins as a spiritual child and must grow.

Jesus said, "Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God" (Mark 10:14 KJV). Jesus welcomed children. He blessed them. He valued them. And He told us that unless we become like little children, we cannot enter the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 18:3 KJV). There is a childlike faith, humility, and trust that every believer must have.

But the Bible also tells us not to stay as children forever. Peter wrote, "As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby" (1 Peter 2:2 KJV). You are to grow. You are to mature. You are to move from milk to solid food. And you are to help others — especially the children in your care — to grow in their faith too.

Today, take a moment to thank God for the children in your life. Pray for them. Bless them. And also examine your own spiritual growth. Are you still a spiritual child, or are you growing into maturity? Every child of God is called to grow. Let this World Children's Day remind you to grow in grace, and to help the children around you grow in Christ.

Lesson: World Children's Day reminds us to value and bless children, and to grow in our own spiritual lives as children of God.

Action: Today, pray a blessing over the children in your life. Then, ask God to help you grow into spiritual maturity.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the gift of children. I choose today to bless them, pray for them, and help them grow in Christ. I also choose to grow in my own spiritual life.

Confess this: I value children. I bless them and pray for them. I help them grow in Christ. I am also growing in my own faith. I desire the sincere milk of the Word. I move from milk to solid food. I grow into spiritual maturity. I am a child of God who is growing up in Him.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Peter 1:3 KJV - "Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead."
devotionals.devotional:
We resume our In Him series today. Hope is not wishful thinking. It is not a vague optimism that things might turn out well. In Christ, you have a living hope — a confident expectation that is anchored in the resurrection of Jesus Christ. It is alive, it is certain, and it cannot be shaken.

Scripture says, "Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you, Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time" (1 Peter 1:3-5 KJV). Your hope is living because it is rooted in a living Saviour.

The Amplified Bible renders 1 Peter 1:3 this way: "Praised (honored, blessed) be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ (the Messiah)! By His boundless mercy we have been born again to an ever-living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead." Your hope is not based on your circumstances. It is not based on your feelings. It is based on the finished work of Jesus and His resurrection from the dead.

But this hope is kept for those who are kept by the power of God through faith. Scripture says, "Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation" (1 Peter 1:5 KJV). Faith is the channel through which God's keeping power flows. Continue in the faith. Hold fast to your hope. For the one who endures to the end shall be saved (Matthew 24:13 KJV).

Lesson: In Christ, you have a living hope anchored in His resurrection; but you must continue in faith, for you are kept by the power of God through faith.

Action: Today, thank God for your living hope. Then, take one step to strengthen your faith — read the Word, pray, and hold fast to your confession.

Bible Portions — Stop Here. There Is Living Hope In These Words.

  • in Christ Jesus: 1 Thessalonians 5:18
    Christ is the One in whom God's will is found. You are in Him, so you can give thanks in everything. What are you struggling to give thanks for that you can bring to Him?
  • in Christ Jesus: 1 Peter 5:14
    Christ is the One in whom peace is found. Peace be with you because you are in Him. What are you still trying to find peace in outside of Christ?
  • in Christ: 1 Thessalonians 4:16
    Christ is the One in whom the dead shall rise first. Even death cannot separate you from Him. What fear are you carrying that Christ has already overcome?
  • in him: 1 John 2:5
    Christ is the One in whom the love of God is perfected. You are in Him, and His love is being perfected in you. What area of your life still needs to be perfected in love?
  • in him: 1 John 2:6
    Christ is the One you abide in, and the One you walk as. If you abide in Him, you walk as He walked. Is your walk matching your position?

Walk in hope. Your hope is alive. Not because of your circumstances. Because of His resurrection. Live in that hope.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I have a living hope. My hope is anchored in the resurrection of Jesus Christ. And I choose to continue in faith.

Confess this: I have a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ. I am kept by the power of God through faith. I hold fast to my hope. I continue in the faith. My hope is alive. My hope is certain. My hope is in Christ.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Peter 2:9 KJV - "But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light."
devotionals.devotional:
You are not an ordinary person. You are not just one of the crowd. In Christ, you have been given a remarkable identity. You are a chosen generation. You are a royal priesthood. You are a holy nation. You are a peculiar people. You are a priest and a king in the kingdom of God.

Scripture says, "But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light: Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy" (1 Peter 2:9-10 KJV). You have been called out of darkness into His marvellous light.

The Amplified Bible renders 1 Peter 2:9 this way: "But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a dedicated nation, [God's] own purchased, special people, that you may set forth the wonderful deeds and display the virtues and perfections of Him Who called you out of darkness into His marvellous light." You are God's own purchased, special people. You are a priest who offers spiritual sacrifices. You are a king who reigns in life through Christ.

But this identity comes with a responsibility. You are called to shew forth the praises of Him who called you out of darkness. Scripture says, "Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul" (1 Peter 2:11 KJV). A royal priest must live a holy life. Your conduct must reflect your calling.

Lesson: In Christ, you are a chosen generation and a royal priesthood; but you must abstain from fleshly lusts and live a life worthy of your calling.

Action: Today, thank God for your identity as a royal priest. Then, abstain from one fleshly desire that wars against your soul, and offer your life as a spiritual sacrifice.

Bible Portions — Look Here. You Are A Priest And A King.

  • in Christ Jesus: 2 Timothy 1:1
    Christ is the One in whom the promise of life is found. You are in Him, so the promise is yours. What promise are you still doubting?
  • in Christ Jesus: 2 Timothy 2:1
    Christ is the One in whom grace is found. You are to be strong in the grace that is in Him. What are you trying to be strong in outside of His grace?
  • in Christ Jesus: 2 Timothy 2:10
    Christ is the One in whom salvation is found. You are in Him, and His salvation is yours. Who are you carrying that salvation to?
  • in him: 1 John 2:8
    Christ is the One in whom the truth is realized. The darkness is passing away, and the true light is shining. What darkness are you still living in that Christ has already dispelled?
  • in him: 1 John 2:27
    Christ is the One in whom the anointing abides. You have an anointing from Him that teaches you all things. What are you still trying to learn outside of His anointing?

Live as a royal priest. You are not ordinary. You are chosen, royal, holy, and peculiar. Live like it.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am a chosen generation and a royal priesthood. I am Your own special people. And I choose to live a holy life worthy of my calling.

Confess this: I am a chosen generation. I am a royal priesthood. I am a holy nation. I am a peculiar people. I shew forth the praises of Him who called me out of darkness into His marvellous light. I abstain from fleshly lusts. I live a holy life.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Peter 2:6 KJV - "Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded."
devotionals.devotional:
A building is only as strong as its cornerstone. The cornerstone sets the angles, determines the direction, and holds the structure together. In Christ, you have a chief corner stone — a foundation that is elect and precious. He is the One upon whom everything else is built.

Scripture says, "To whom coming, as unto a living stone, disallowed indeed of men, but chosen of God, and precious, Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ" (1 Peter 2:4-5 KJV). You are a living stone, built upon the living Stone. You are part of a spiritual house, a holy priesthood.

The Amplified Bible renders 1 Peter 2:6 this way: "For it is contained in Scripture: Behold, I lay in Zion a Chief Cornerstone, chosen (elect) and precious, and he who believes in (relies on, trusts in, and adheres to) Him [and Him alone, making Him his entire reliance] shall not be put to shame or be disappointed." The one who believes in Him will not be confounded. You will not be put to shame. Your foundation is secure.

But a living stone must remain in the building. Scripture warns, "But he that lacketh these things is blind, and cannot see afar off, and hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins. Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall" (2 Peter 1:9-10 KJV). You are a living stone, but you must remain built upon the Cornerstone. Do not be moved away from the foundation.

Lesson: In Christ, you are a living stone built upon the Chief Corner Stone; but you must remain in the building and make your calling and election sure.

Action: Today, thank God that you are built upon the Chief Corner Stone. Then, examine your foundation and make sure you are firmly built upon Christ.

Bible Portions — Look Here. You Are Built On A Sure Foundation.

  • in him: 1 John 2:28
    Christ is the One you abide in, and the One you will have confidence before. If you abide in Him, you will not be ashamed at His coming. Are you living in that confidence?
  • in him: 1 John 3:3
    Christ is the One in whom your hope rests. Everyone who has this hope in Him purifies himself. What are you still holding on to that needs to be purified?
  • in him: 1 John 3:5
    Christ is the One in whom there is no sin. He appeared to take away sins. What sin are you still living as if it has power over you?
  • in him: 1 John 3:6
    Christ is the One you abide in. Whoever abides in Him does not continue in sin. Is your abiding producing the fruit of holiness?
  • in him: 1 John 3:24
    Christ is the One you abide in, and the One who abides in you. The proof is the Holy Spirit He has given you. Are you living in the awareness of His indwelling?

Stand firm. You are built on the Chief Corner Stone. Not on sand. On the Rock. Stand firm in Him.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am a living stone built upon the Chief Corner Stone. My foundation is secure. And I choose to remain in the building.

Confess this: I am a living stone, built upon the Chief Corner Stone. I am part of a spiritual house. I am a holy priesthood. I offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God by Jesus Christ. I make my calling and election sure. I will not be confounded.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Peter 2:21 KJV - "For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps."
devotionals.devotional:
Suffering is not a popular topic, but it is a biblical one. In Christ, you are called to suffer well. You are called to endure hardship with grace, to respond to mistreatment with patience, and to follow the example of Jesus, who suffered without sin and without revenge.

Scripture says, "For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully. For what glory is it, if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God. For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps" (1 Peter 2:19-21 KJV).

The Amplified Bible renders 1 Peter 2:21 this way: "For even to this were you called [it is inseparable from your vocation]. For Christ also suffered for you, leaving you [His personal] example, so that you should follow in His footsteps." Suffering is inseparable from your calling. But Christ left you an example. He did not retaliate. He did not threaten. He entrusted Himself to God.

But suffering well does not mean suffering passively or without hope. Scripture says, "Wherefore let them that suffer according to the will of God commit the keeping of their souls to him in well doing, as unto a faithful Creator" (1 Peter 4:19 KJV). Commit your soul to God. Continue in well doing. And remember that "the God of all grace, who hath called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you" (1 Peter 5:10 KJV).

Lesson: In Christ, you are called to suffer well, following His example; but you must commit your soul to God and continue in well doing.

Action: Today, if you face mistreatment or hardship, do not retaliate. Commit your soul to God and continue in well doing.

Bible Portions — Look Here. You Are Not Alone In Your Suffering.

  • in him: 1 John 4:13
    Christ is the One you abide in, and the One who abides in you. The proof is the Holy Spirit He has given you. Are you living in the awareness of His indwelling?
  • in him: 1 John 4:15
    Christ is the One you confess, and the One who abides in you. If you confess Jesus as the Son of God, God abides in you. What are you still hesitant to confess?
  • in him: 1 John 5:20
    Christ is the True God and Eternal Life. You are in Him who is true. What does it mean to you that your life is hidden in the One who is true?
  • in Christ Jesus: 1 Peter 5:14
    Christ is the One in whom peace is found. Peace be with you because you are in Him. What are you still trying to find peace in outside of Christ?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 2:14
    Christ is the One who always leads you in triumph. Your suffering is not defeat; it is triumph in Him. What trial are you still viewing as defeat that Christ is turning into triumph?

Suffer well. You are not alone. You are in Him. And He will perfect, stablish, strengthen, and settle you.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am called to suffer well. I choose today to follow the example of Jesus. I will not retaliate. I will commit my soul to You and continue in well doing.

Confess this: I am called to suffer well. I follow the example of Christ. I do not retaliate. I do not threaten. I commit my soul to God. I continue in well doing. The God of all grace will perfect, stablish, strengthen, and settle me.

devotionals.topic: International Day For The Elimination Of Violence Against Women: Walking in Love and Dignity
devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Peter 3:7 KJV - "Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered."
devotionals.devotional:
We pause the In Him series today to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. It is a day when the world turns its attention to the dignity and safety of women and girls. As believers, we should not treat this day as a secular observance to be ignored. Scripture speaks clearly about how women are to be treated, and it calls every believer to walk in love, honour, and protection.

The Apostle Peter wrote, "Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered" (1 Peter 3:7 KJV). Notice that the husband is to dwell with his wife according to knowledge. He is to know her, understand her, and treat her with honour. He is not to dominate her, abuse her, or disregard her. He is to honour her as a joint heir of the grace of life.

Paul wrote, "Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it... So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church" (Ephesians 5:25, 28-29 KJV). The standard for the husband is the love of Christ. Christ gave Himself for the church. He nourishes and cherishes her. He does not harm her. He uses His strength for her.

Violence against women is a violation of God's design and God's commands. Whether physical, emotional, verbal, or spiritual, abuse is sin. It has no place in the life of a believer. If you are a husband, love your wife as Christ loved the church. If you are a member of the church, stand up for the dignity and safety of women and girls around you. Speak up when you see injustice. Offer help when you see harm. And walk in love and honour in your own relationships.

Lesson: God calls every believer to honour women, protect them from harm, and walk in love and dignity; abuse is sin and has no place in the church.

Action: Today, examine your own relationships. Are you treating the women in your life with the honour, love, and dignity that God commands? If not, repent and make it right.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the dignity of every person. I choose today to walk in love and honour toward women and girls. I will not abuse, belittle, or harm them. I will protect them and speak up for them.

Confess this: I walk in love and dignity. I honour women as joint heirs of the grace of life. I love my wife as Christ loved the church. I nourish and cherish her. I speak up for the vulnerable. I stand against violence and abuse. My relationships reflect the love of Christ.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 John 1:7 KJV - "But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin."
devotionals.devotional:
We resume our In Him series today. You were once darkness. Not in darkness, but darkness itself. Your very nature was dark, devoid of light, devoid of truth, devoid of God. But something changed. In Christ, you are now light. Not just someone who has light, but light itself. You are a child of light, and you are called to walk as a child of light.

Scripture says, "For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord: walk as children of light: (For the fruit of the Spirit is in all goodness and righteousness and truth;) Proving what is acceptable unto the Lord" (Ephesians 5:8-10 KJV). You are light in the Lord. This is your identity. This is your nature. Walk as a child of light.

The Amplified Bible renders Ephesians 5:8 this way: "For once you were darkness, but now you are light in the Lord; walk as children of Light [lead the lives of those native-born to the Light]." You are native-born to the light. It is your natural environment. It is your identity. You do not have to try to be light; you are light in the Lord. You simply need to walk according to your new nature.
