But walking in the light is not optional. Scripture says, "And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them" (Ephesians 5:11 KJV). The one who is light must have no fellowship with darkness. To walk in the light is to live honestly, transparently, and uprightly before God and man. You are light. Walk as a child of light. Let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.

Lesson: In Christ, you are light in the Lord; but you must walk as a child of light, having no fellowship with the works of darkness.

Action: Today, walk as a child of light. Be honest, transparent, and upright. And turn away from any fellowship with darkness that you have allowed into your life.

Bible Portions — Look Here. You Are Light.

  • in the Lord: Ephesians 5:8
    Christ is the One in whom you are light. You were darkness, but now you are light in Him. What darkness are you still living in that Christ has already dispelled?
  • in the Lord: Ephesians 6:10
    Christ is the One in whom you are strong. Your strength is not in yourself; it is in Him. What are you trying to be strong in outside of the Lord?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 2:14
    Christ is the One who always leads you in triumph. Your life is a fragrance of Him everywhere. What place are you carrying His fragrance to today?
  • in the beloved: Ephesians 1:6
    Christ is the Beloved in whom you are accepted. You are not accepted because of what you do; you are accepted because you are found in the One the Father loves. Do you know you are accepted?
  • in him: Ephesians 1:4
    Christ is the Place of your election. You were chosen in Him before the world began. Do you see yourself as chosen?

Walk in the light. You are not darkness anymore. You are light. Live like it.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am light in the Lord. I am no longer darkness. I am a child of light. And I choose to walk as a child of light, in goodness, righteousness, and truth.

Confess this: I am light in the Lord. I was once darkness, but now I am light. I walk as a child of light. I have no fellowship with the works of darkness. I live in goodness, righteousness, and truth. My light shines before men, and they glorify my Father in heaven.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Philippians 4:13 KJV - "I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me."
devotionals.devotional:
You are not called to live the Christian life in your own strength. You are not called to fight spiritual battles with natural weapons. You are called to be strong in the Lord and in the power of His might. Your strength is not in yourself; it is in Him.

Scripture says, "Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might. Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places. Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand" (Ephesians 6:10-13 KJV).

The Amplified Bible renders Ephesians 6:10 this way: "In conclusion, be strong in the Lord [be empowered through your union with Him]; draw your strength from Him [that strength which His boundless might provides]." Your strength comes from your union with Him. You draw it from Him. You do not manufacture it; you receive it. You are strong in the Lord and in the power of His might.

But this strength must be exercised with vigilance. Scripture says, "Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour: Whom resist stedfast in the faith" (1 Peter 5:8-9 KJV). The one who is strong in the Lord must remain watchful, resist the devil, and stand firm in the faith.

Lesson: In Christ, you are strong and empowered; but you must be vigilant, resist the devil, and stand firm in the faith.

Action: Today, do not rely on your own strength. Draw your strength from the Lord. Put on the whole armour of God and stand in His power.

Bible Portions — Look Here. Your Strength Is In Him.

  • in the Lord: Ephesians 6:10
    Christ is the One in whom you are strong. Your strength is not in yourself; it is in Him. What are you trying to be strong in outside of the Lord?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 5:17
    Christ is the Source of a new creation. If you are in Christ, you are a new creature. Are you still living as the old person, or as the new creation Christ has made you?
  • in him: Philippians 3:9
    Christ is the Righteousness that comes by faith. Paul wanted to be found in Him, not having his own righteousness. Whose righteousness are you actually standing in?
  • in Christ Jesus: Philippians 4:19
    Christ is the One in whom your needs are supplied. Your supply is not in the economy; it is in Him. What need are you still doubting that God will supply?
  • in Christ: Colossians 1:2
    Christ is the One in whom you are a saint. You are not just forgiven; you are set apart. Do you see yourself as a saint?

Stand strong. You are strong in the Lord. Not in yourself. Draw your strength from Him.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am strong and empowered. My strength comes from my union with You. And I choose to remain vigilant and stand firm in the faith.

Confess this: I am strong in the Lord and in the power of His might. I draw my strength from Him. I put on the whole armour of God. I stand against the wiles of the devil. I am sober and vigilant. I resist the devil, steadfast in the faith. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.

devotionals.topic: All Things Created And Held Together
devotionals.memoryVerse: Colossians 1:17 KJV - "And he is before all things, and by him all things consist."
devotionals.devotional:
Everything you see, everything you touch, everything that exists was created in Christ and for Christ. He is not a created being; He is the Creator. And He is not just the Creator of the past; He is the Sustainer of the present. He holds all things together by the word of His power.

Scripture says, "For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist" (Colossians 1:16-17 KJV). All things were created by Him and for Him. All things are held together by Him.

The Amplified Bible renders Colossians 1:17 this way: "And He Himself existed before all things, and in Him all things consist (cohere, are held together)." Everything holds together in Christ. The universe holds together in Christ. The church holds together in Christ. And your life holds together in Christ. He is the centre of all things.

But this truth also means that He is the Head. Scripture says, "And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence" (Colossians 1:18 KJV). The One who holds all things together must have first place in your life. He is not just the Sustainer of the universe; He is the Lord of your life.

Lesson: In Christ, all things were created and are held together; but He must have the preeminence in your life.

Action: Today, rest in the knowledge that Christ is holding your life together. Then, give Him first place in one area where you have been keeping Him second.

Bible Portions — Look Here. He Holds Everything Together.

  • by him: Colossians 1:16
    Christ is the Creator. By Him all things were made, in heaven and on earth. What are you treating as if it exists apart from Him?
  • by him: Colossians 1:17
    Christ is the Sustainer. By Him all things consist. The same power that holds the universe together holds you. What are you trying to hold together in your own strength?
  • for him: Colossians 1:16
    Christ is the Purpose. All things were created for Him. What are you living for that is not Him?
  • by him: Colossians 1:20
    Christ is the Peacemaker. By Him, God reconciled all things to Himself. What area of your life still needs to be reconciled to Him?
  • by him: Colossians 3:17
    Christ is the One through whom you give thanks. All that you do, you do in His name, giving thanks by Him. Is your life marked by thanksgiving?

Rest in this. Christ holds everything together. Including you. Give Him first place.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ all things were created and hold together. He is before all things, and by Him all things consist. My life is held together by Him.

Confess this: In Christ all things were created. By Him all things consist. He is before all things. My life is held together by Him. I give Him the preeminence in my life. He is the Head of the body. He is Lord of my life.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Corinthians 2:14 KJV - "Now thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place."
devotionals.devotional:
You are not fighting for victory; you are fighting from victory. God always causes you to triumph in Christ. Not sometimes. Not occasionally. Always. Every battle, every trial, every circumstance — you are led in triumph because you are in Christ.

Scripture says, "Now thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place. For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish" (2 Corinthians 2:14-15 KJV). God always causes you to triumph. He does not cause you to barely survive. He does not cause you to scrape by. He causes you to triumph.

The Amplified Bible renders 2 Corinthians 2:14 this way: "But thanks be to God, Who in Christ always leads us in triumph [as trophies of Christ's victory] and through us spreads and makes evident the fragrance of the knowledge of God everywhere." You are a trophy of Christ's victory. You are led in triumph. And through you, the fragrance of His knowledge spreads everywhere.

But being led in triumph does not mean being exempt from the fight. Scripture says, "For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places" (Ephesians 6:12 KJV). You will face battles. But you face them as one who is already victorious in Christ. The triumph is yours; walk in it.

Lesson: In Christ, God always causes you to triumph; you are a trophy of His victory, but you must still stand in the fight.

Action: Today, when you face a challenge, declare: "God always causes me to triumph in Christ." Then, stand firm in the fight, knowing that the victory is already yours.

Bible Portions — Look Here. You Are Led In Triumph.

  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 2:14
    Christ is the One in whom you triumph. Not sometimes. Always. What battle are you fighting as if the outcome depended on you?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 1:21
    Christ is the One in whom you are established. God has confirmed you in Him. Are you living in that confidence?
  • in him: 2 Corinthians 1:20
    Christ is the Yes and Amen of every promise. Every promise of God finds its Yes in Him. What promise are you still doubting?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 3:14
    Christ is the One in whom the veil is taken away. You can see clearly now. What are you still living as if you cannot see?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 5:19
    Christ is the One in whom God was reconciling the world to Himself. You are part of that reconciliation. Who are you carrying that message to?

Walk in triumph. You are not fighting for victory. You are fighting from victory. Stand firm in the triumph of Christ.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ You always cause me to triumph. I am a trophy of Christ's victory. I am led in triumph wherever I go. And I choose to stand firm in the fight.

Confess this: God always causes me to triumph in Christ. I am a trophy of His victory. I am led in triumph. Through me, the fragrance of His knowledge spreads everywhere. I stand firm in the fight, knowing the victory is mine.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Corinthians 3:18 KJV - "But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord."
devotionals.devotional:
You are being transformed. Not by your own effort, not by your own discipline, but by the Spirit of the Lord. As you behold the glory of the Lord, you are changed into His image, from glory to glory. This is not a one-time event; it is an ongoing process. And it is happening in you right now.

Scripture says, "Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord" (2 Corinthians 3:17-18 KJV). Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. And as you behold His glory, you are changed into His image.

The Amplified Bible renders 2 Corinthians 3:18 this way: "And all of us, as with unveiled face, [because we] continued to behold [in the Word of God] as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are constantly being transfigured into His very own image in ever increasing splendour and from one degree of glory to another; [for this comes] from the Lord [Who is] the Spirit." You are constantly being transfigured. You are being changed into His image.

But transformation requires beholding. Scripture says, "Blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it" (Luke 11:28 KJV). The one who is transformed is the one who beholds the Lord in His Word and keeps it. Spend time in His presence. Behold His glory in the Word. And as you do, you will be changed.

Lesson: In Christ, you are being transformed into His image from glory to glory by the Spirit of the Lord as you behold His glory.

Action: Today, spend time beholding the glory of the Lord in His Word. Let the Holy Spirit transform you into His image.

Bible Portions — Look Here. You Are Being Changed.

  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 5:17
    Christ is the Source of a new creation. If you are in Christ, you are a new creature. Are you still living as the old person, or as the new creation Christ has made you?
  • in him: 2 Corinthians 5:21
    Christ is your Righteousness. He was made sin so that you might be made the righteousness of God in Him. Are you still trying to become righteous?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 5:19
    Christ is the One in whom God was reconciling the world to Himself. You are part of that reconciliation. Who are you carrying that message to?
  • in him: Philippians 3:9
    Christ is the Righteousness that comes by faith. Paul wanted to be found in Him, not having his own righteousness. Whose righteousness are you actually standing in?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 3:14
    Christ is the One in whom the veil is taken away. You can see clearly now. What are you still living as if you cannot see?

Behold His glory. You are being changed. From glory to glory. Keep beholding. Keep being transformed.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am being transformed into Your image from glory to glory by the Spirit of the Lord. I am changed as I behold Your glory.

Confess this: I am being transformed into the image of Christ. I am changed from glory to glory by the Spirit of the Lord. As I behold His glory in the Word, I am transformed. I keep the Word. I reflect His image more clearly every day.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Ephesians 3:17 KJV - "That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love."
devotionals.devotional:
You are not just forgiven; you are loved. You are not just accepted; you are rooted and grounded in love. Before you ever loved God, He loved you. Before you ever did anything for Him, He set His affection upon you. And that love is not a passing feeling; it is the soil in which your whole life is planted.

Scripture says, "That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love, May be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height; And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God" (Ephesians 3:17-Ephesians 3:19 KJV). Notice that Paul prays for you to be rooted and grounded in love — and then to know the love of Christ, which passes knowledge. This is a love too great to measure. It has breadth, length, depth, and height. It surrounds you on every side.

The Amplified Bible renders Ephesians 3:17 this way: "May Christ through your faith [actually] dwell (settle down, abide, make His permanent home) in your hearts! May you be rooted deep in love and founded securely on love." Christ does not merely visit your heart; He settles down in it. He makes it His permanent home. And from that home, His love becomes the root system of your life.

But being rooted in love means that love must flow out of you. Scripture says, "Beloved, if God so loved us, we ought also to love one another" (1 John 4:11 KJV). The one who is rooted in the love of Christ will love others. And if a believer hardens his heart against others and refuses to forgive, he closes himself off from the very love he claims to possess. Scripture warns, "But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses" (Matthew 6:15 KJV).

Lesson: In Christ, you are rooted and grounded in love; but that love must flow out of you, and you must forgive as you have been forgiven.

Action: Today, meditate on the breadth, length, depth, and height of Christ's love for you. Then, let that love flow out of you by forgiving someone and showing them kindness.

Bible Portions — Look Here. You Are Rooted In Love.

  • in Christ: Ephesians 3:6
    Christ is the One in whom you are a fellow heir. You are not an outsider; you are included. What are you still treating yourself as excluded from?
  • in him: Ephesians 1:4
    Christ is the Place of your election. You were chosen in Him before the world began. Do you see yourself as chosen?
  • in whom: Ephesians 1:7
    Christ is the Fountain of redemption. The blood that purchased you is in Him. What guilt are you still carrying that has already been washed away?
  • in the beloved: Ephesians 1:6
    Christ is the Beloved in whom you are accepted. You are not accepted because of what you do; you are accepted because you are found in the One the Father loves. Do you know you are accepted?
  • in whom: Ephesians 3:12
    Christ is the Door of access. In Him you have boldness and confidence. What are you still approaching God with fear about, when the door is wide open?

Rest in His love. You are rooted and grounded in love. Not shallowly. Deeply. Let it flow out of you.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that I am rooted and grounded in love. I choose today to meditate on the love of Christ and to let that love flow out of me to others.

Confess this: I am rooted and grounded in love. Christ dwells in my heart by faith. I know the love of Christ which passeth knowledge. I am filled with all the fulness of God. I forgive as I have been forgiven. I love others as Christ has loved me.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Colossians 2:11 KJV - "In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ."
devotionals.devotional:
Under the old covenant, circumcision was a physical act. It was a sign of belonging to God's covenant people. But in Christ, there is a greater circumcision — a spiritual one. It is not made with hands. It is not outward. It is inward. It is the putting off of the body of the sins of the flesh.

Scripture says, "In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ: Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him from the dead" (Colossians 2:11-12 KJV). You have been circumcised spiritually. The old nature has been cut off. The body of sin has been put away.

The Amplified Bible renders Colossians 2:11 this way: "In Him also you were circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands, but in a [spiritual] circumcision [performed by] Christ by stripping off the body of the flesh (the whole corrupt, carnal nature with its passions and lusts)." In Christ, the old nature was stripped off. It was removed. It was put away.

But this circumcision of the heart must be lived out. Scripture says, "Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry" (Colossians 3:5 KJV). The old nature has been cut off; now you must put it to death in your daily walk. You are free to live in the newness of life that Christ has given you.

Lesson: In Christ, you have been spiritually circumcised; the old nature has been cut off, and you must now put it to death in your daily walk.

Action: Today, when temptation comes, remind yourself: "My old nature has been cut off. I am not a slave to sin." Then, put to death one deed of the flesh.

Bible Portions — Look Here. The Old Nature Is Cut Off.

  • in whom: Colossians 2:11
    Christ is the One who circumcised your heart. The old nature has been cut off. What old nature are you still living as if it has power over you?
  • with him: Colossians 2:12
    Christ is the One you were buried with and raised with. Your old life is buried. What old thing are you still trying to keep alive?
  • with him: Colossians 2:13
    Christ is the One who quickened you. You were dead, and He made you alive. What dead thing are you still trying to resurrect?
  • in him: Colossians 2:10
    Christ is the Fullness of God, and you are complete in Him. What part of your life are you still treating as incomplete?
  • in whom: Colossians 2:3
    Christ is the Treasury of all wisdom and knowledge. Every answer you need is hidden in Him. What question are you still trying to answer outside of Christ?

Walk in freedom. Your old nature has been cut off. You are not a slave to sin. Live like a free person.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I have been spiritually circumcised. The old nature has been cut off. The body of sin has been put away. And I choose to put it to death in my daily walk.

Confess this: In Christ I have been circumcised with a circumcision made without hands. My old nature has been cut off. The body of sin has been put away. I am buried with Him in baptism and risen with Him. I put to death the deeds of the flesh. I am free from sin.

devotionals.topic: International Day Of Persons With Disabilities: Every Member Matters
devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Corinthians 12:22 KJV - "Nay, much more those members of the body, which seem to be more feeble, are necessary."
devotionals.devotional:
We pause the In Him series today to mark the International Day of Persons with Disabilities. It is a day when the world turns its attention to the dignity, value, and contribution of people living with disabilities. As believers, we should not treat this day as a secular observance to be ignored. Scripture speaks clearly about the value of every member of the body of Christ, and it calls every believer to honour and include those whom the world often overlooks.

Paul wrote, "And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you. Nay, much more those members of the body, which seem to be more feeble, are necessary: And those members of the body, which we think to be less honourable, upon these we bestow more abundant honour; and our uncomely parts have more abundant comeliness" (1 Corinthians 12:21-23 KJV).

Every member of the body of Christ matters. Every person has value. Every person has a contribution to make. The world may label some people as weak, less useful, or less important, but God does not see them that way. He has placed every member in the body exactly where He wants them. And He has given special honour to those who seem to have less.

You must not look down on anyone. You must not treat people with disabilities as though they are less than you. You must not exclude them, ignore them, or pity them from a distance. Instead, you must honour them. You must include them. You must create a place for them in your church, your community, and your life. You must love them as Christ loves them. On this day — and every day — let every member matter.

Lesson: Every person has value in God's eyes; you must honour, include, and love those with disabilities, for every member of the body matters.

Action: Today, reach out to someone with a disability. Honour them, speak to them, pray with them, and let them know they matter.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the value of every person. I choose today to honour, include, and love those with disabilities. I will not look down on anyone. I will see them as You see them.

Confess this: Every member of the body of Christ matters. I honour those with disabilities. I include them. I value them. I create a place for them. I love them as Christ loves them. I will not exclude anyone. Every member is necessary. I am the body of Christ, and every member belongs.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Colossians 2:13 KJV - "And you, being dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, hath he quickened together with him, having forgiven you all trespasses."
devotionals.devotional:
We resume our In Him series today. You were dead. Not sick, not weak, not struggling — dead. Dead in your sins. Dead in the uncircumcision of your flesh. You had no spiritual life, no connection to God, no ability to respond to Him. But God did something. He made you alive together with Christ. And not only that, He forgave you all trespasses.

Scripture says, "And you, being dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, hath he quickened together with him, having forgiven you all trespasses" (Colossians 2:13 KJV). Notice the two things God did: He quickened you, and He forgave you. He made you alive, and He wiped out your sins. Both are done. Both are complete. Both are yours in Christ.

The Amplified Bible renders Colossians 2:13 this way: "And you who were dead in trespasses and in the uncircumcision of your flesh (your sensuality, your sinful carnal nature), [God] brought to life together with [Christ], having [freely] forgiven us all our transgressions." Freely forgiven. Not reluctantly. Not partially. Freely and completely forgiven. All trespasses. Not some. All.

But the life that was given to you must be lived out. Scripture says, "If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God" (Colossians 3:1 KJV). The one who has been made alive must live in newness of life. And if a believer turns back to the death from which he was saved, Scripture warns that the latter end is worse than the beginning (2 Peter 2:20 KJV).

Lesson: In Christ, you have been made alive and freely forgiven all trespasses; but you must live in newness of life, for turning back brings a worse end.

Action: Today, thank God that you are made alive together with Christ and that all your trespasses are forgiven. Then, walk in newness of life.

Bible Portions — Look Here. You Were Dead. Now You Are Alive.

  • with him: Colossians 2:13
    Christ is the One who quickened you. You were dead, and He made you alive. What dead thing are you still trying to resurrect in your own strength?
  • in him: Colossians 2:10
    Christ is the Fullness of God, and you are complete in Him. What part of your life are you still treating as incomplete?
  • in him: Colossians 2:7
    Christ is the Soil in which you are rooted. You are built up in Him. What are you rooted in right now — the Word, or the world?
  • in him: Colossians 2:6
    Christ is the One you walk in. You received Him, and you walk in Him. Are you walking in Him today, or in your own effort?
  • in whom: Colossians 2:11
    Christ is the One who circumcised your heart. The old nature has been cut off. What old nature are you still living as if it has power over you?

Walk in newness. You were dead. Now you are alive. Live like it.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am made alive and forgiven. You quickened me when I was dead in my sins. You forgave me all trespasses. And I choose to walk in newness of life.

Confess this: I am made alive together with Christ. I am forgiven all trespasses. My sins are wiped away. I am quickened by the power of God. I walk in the freedom of forgiveness and new life. I do not return to death.

devotionals.topic: The Record Nailed To The Cross
devotionals.memoryVerse: Colossians 2:14 KJV - "Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross."
devotionals.devotional:
There was a record against you. It was a legal document, a list of charges. Every sin, every failure, every transgression was written down. And the law demanded payment. But in Christ, that record has been blotted out. It has been wiped away. It has been nailed to His cross.

Scripture says, "Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross; And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it" (Colossians 2:14-15 KJV). The record against you has been blotted out. It has been taken out of the way. And the principalities and powers that held it against you have been spoiled and triumphed over.

The Amplified Bible renders Colossians 2:14 this way: "Having cancelled and blotted out and wiped away the handwriting of the note (bond) with its legal decrees and demands which was in force and stood against us (hostile to us). This [note with its regulations, decrees, and demands] He set aside and cleared completely out of our way by nailing it to [His] cross." Cancelled. Blotted out. Wiped away. Set aside. Cleared completely out of the way.

But this freedom is not for those who return to the slavery. Scripture warns, "Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage" (Galatians 5:1 KJV). The record has been blotted out. Do not go back and write new charges against yourself by returning to sin.

Lesson: In Christ, the record of your sins has been blotted out and nailed to the cross; but you must stand fast in your liberty and not return to bondage.

Action: Today, when the enemy accuses you of past sins, declare: "The handwriting of ordinances has been blotted out. The record has been nailed to the cross. I am free." Then, stand fast in your liberty.

Bible Portions — Look Here. The Record Is Gone.

  • with him: Colossians 2:12
    Christ is the One you were buried with and raised with. Your old life is buried. What old thing are you still trying to keep alive?
  • with him: Colossians 2:13
    Christ is the One who quickened you. You were dead, and He made you alive. What dead thing are you still trying to resurrect?
  • in whom: Colossians 2:11
    Christ is the One who circumcised your heart. The old nature has been cut off. What old nature are you still living as if it has power over you?
  • in him: Colossians 2:10
    Christ is the Fullness of God, and you are complete in Him. What part of your life are you still treating as incomplete?
  • in him: Colossians 2:7
    Christ is the Soil in which you are rooted. You are built up in Him. What are you rooted in right now — the Word, or the world?

Stand fast. The record is gone. The charges are dropped. You are free. Live in that freedom.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ the handwriting of ordinances against me has been blotted out. It has been nailed to the cross. And I choose to stand fast in my liberty.

Confess this: The handwriting of ordinances against me is blotted out. It is nailed to the cross. The principalities and powers are spoiled. The enemy has no legal grounds to accuse me. I am free. I am justified. I stand fast in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made me free.

devotionals.topic: Dead To The World And Alive To God
devotionals.memoryVerse: Colossians 3:3 KJV - "For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God."
devotionals.devotional:
You have died. Not physically, but spiritually. You have died to the world and its ways. You have died to the old nature and its desires. And you have been raised with Christ to a new life. Your life is now hidden with Christ in God. You are no longer of this world, even though you live in it.

Scripture says, "If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God. Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth. For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God. When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory" (Colossians 3:1-4 KJV). You are risen with Christ. You are dead to the world. Your life is hidden with Christ in God.

The Amplified Bible renders Colossians 3:3 this way: "For [as far as this world is concerned] you have died, and your [new, real] life is hidden with Christ in God." As far as this world is concerned, you have died. You are no longer governed by its values, its priorities, or its passions. Your new life is hidden with Christ in God. It is secure, protected, and eternal.

But being dead to the world means putting to death the things of the world. Scripture says, "Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry: For which things' sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience" (Colossians 3:5-6 KJV). You must put to death the deeds of the old nature. Live as one who has been raised.

Lesson: In Christ, you have died to the world and been raised with Him; but you must put to death the deeds of the old nature and set your affection on things above.

Action: Today, set your affection on things above. Put to death one thing in your life that belongs to the old nature.

Bible Portions — Look Up. Your Life Is Hidden With Christ.

  • with Christ: Colossians 3:1
    Christ is the One you are risen with. Your position is above, not beneath. What are you still seeking below that you should be seeking above?
  • with Christ: Colossians 3:3
    Christ is the One your life is hidden with. Your life is secure in Him. What are you trying to protect that is already safe in Christ?
  • with him: Colossians 3:4
    Christ is the One you will appear with in glory. The future is certain because the present is secure. Are you living in the light of that certainty?
  • in Christ: Colossians 2:5
    Christ is the One in whom your faith stands. Your faith is not in your own understanding; it is in Him. What are you still trying to figure out on your own?
  • in him: Colossians 2:6
    Christ is the One you walk in. You received Him, and you walk in Him. Are you walking in Him today, or in your own effort?

Set your affection above. Your life is hidden with Christ in God. Live from that hidden place.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I have died to the world and been raised with Him. My life is hidden with Christ in You. And I choose to put to death the deeds of the old nature.

Confess this: I am dead to the world. My life is hidden with Christ in God. I am risen with Christ. I seek the things that are above. I set my affection on things above, not on things on the earth. I put to death the deeds of the old nature. I live for eternity.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Corinthians 2:14 KJV - "Now thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place."
devotionals.devotional:
You are not just a Christian; you are a fragrance. You carry the scent of Christ wherever you go. You are the aroma of His knowledge, diffused through every place you enter. Your life, your words, your presence — all of it releases the fragrance of Christ to those around you.

Scripture says, "Now thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place. For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish" (2 Corinthians 2:14-15 KJV). God always causes you to triumph in Christ. And He makes manifest the fragrance of His knowledge through you.

The Amplified Bible renders 2 Corinthians 2:14 this way: "But thanks be to God, Who in Christ always leads us in triumph [as trophies of Christ's victory] and through us spreads and makes evident the fragrance of the knowledge of God everywhere." You are a trophy of Christ's victory. You are led in triumph. And through you, the fragrance of His knowledge spreads everywhere.

But this fragrance is only released when you remain in Christ. Scripture says, "Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; so neither can ye, except ye abide in me" (John 15:4 KJV). The fragrance of Christ is not something you manufacture; it is something that flows out of your abiding in Him. Stay close to Him. Abide in Him. And the fragrance will follow.

Lesson: In Christ, you are the sweet fragrance of Christ; but this fragrance is released only as you abide in Him.

Action: Today, be mindful that you carry the fragrance of Christ. Abide in Him, and let your words, actions, and attitude release His aroma to those around you.

Bible Portions — Look Here. You Carry His Fragrance.

  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 2:14
    Christ is the One in whom you triumph. Not sometimes. Always. What place are you carrying His fragrance to today?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 1:21
    Christ is the One in whom you are established. God has confirmed you in Him. Are you living in that confidence?
  • in him: 2 Corinthians 1:20
    Christ is the Yes and Amen of every promise. Every promise of God finds its Yes in Him. What promise are you still doubting?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 3:14
    Christ is the One in whom the veil is taken away. You can see clearly now. What are you still living as if you cannot see?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 5:19
    Christ is the One in whom God was reconciling the world to Himself. You are part of that reconciliation. Who are you carrying that message to?

Release the fragrance. You carry Christ wherever you go. Abide in Him, and let His fragrance flow through you.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am the sweet fragrance of Christ. I carry His aroma. And I choose to abide in Him so that His fragrance is released through me.

Confess this: I am the sweet fragrance of Christ. God always causes me to triumph in Christ. Through me, the fragrance of His knowledge is made manifest in every place. I abide in Him, and His fragrance flows through me. I am a trophy of Christ's victory.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Corinthians 5:20 KJV - "Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ's stead, be ye reconciled to God."
devotionals.devotional:
You are not just a believer; you are an ambassador. You represent the King of kings in a foreign land. You carry His message, His authority, and His character. And in Christ, you have been made the very righteousness of God. You are His representative on the earth.

Scripture says, "Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ's stead, be ye reconciled to God. For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him" (2 Corinthians 5:20-21 KJV). You are an ambassador for Christ. You speak on His behalf. You represent Him to a world that needs to be reconciled to God.

The Amplified Bible renders 2 Corinthians 5:21 this way: "For our sake He made Christ [virtually] to be sin Who knew no sin, so that in and through Him we might become [endued with, viewed as being in, and examples of] the righteousness of God [what we ought to be, approved and acceptable and in right relationship with Him, by His goodness]." You are the righteousness of God in Christ. You are approved, acceptable, and in right relationship with Him.

But an ambassador must live worthy of his calling. Scripture says, "Now then we are ambassadors for Christ... be ye reconciled to God" (2 Corinthians 5:20 KJV). The ambassador's life must reflect the message he carries. Your words carry His message. Your actions reflect His character. Your life is a testimony. Live worthy of your ambassadorship.

Lesson: In Christ, you are an ambassador for Christ and the righteousness of God; you must live worthy of your calling and reflect Him to the world.

Action: Today, live as an ambassador for Christ. Let your words and actions reflect the One you represent.

Bible Portions — Look Here. You Are An Ambassador.

  • in him: 2 Corinthians 5:21
    Christ is your Righteousness. He was made sin so that you might be made the righteousness of God in Him. Are you still trying to become righteous?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 5:17
    Christ is the Source of a new creation. If you are in Christ, you are a new creature. Are you still living as the old person?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 5:19
    Christ is the One in whom God was reconciling the world to Himself. You are part of that reconciliation. Who are you carrying that message to?
  • in him: Philippians 3:9
    Christ is the Righteousness that comes by faith. Paul wanted to be found in Him, not having his own righteousness. Whose righteousness are you actually standing in?
  • in Christ Jesus: 1 Corinthians 1:30
    Christ is your Wisdom, Righteousness, Sanctification, and Redemption. And it is of Him that you are in Christ Jesus. Do you see Christ as your everything?

Live as an ambassador. You represent the King. Let your life reflect Him.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ I am an ambassador and the righteousness of God. I represent You to the world. And I choose to live worthy of my calling.

Confess this: I am an ambassador for Christ. I am the righteousness of God in Him. I represent the King. My words carry His message. My actions reflect His character. I live worthy of my ambassadorship. I live as an ambassador of the Most High.

devotionals.topic: All The Promises Are Yes And Amen
devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Corinthians 1:20 KJV - "For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us."
devotionals.devotional:
Every promise God has ever made is Yes and Amen in Christ. There is no promise too big, no promise too small, no promise that is unavailable to you. In Christ, every promise of God is confirmed, guaranteed, and fulfilled. You are not waiting for God to say yes; He has already said yes in Christ.

Scripture says, "For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us. Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God; Who hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts" (2 Corinthians 1:20-22 KJV). All the promises of God are Yes and Amen in Christ.

The Amplified Bible renders 2 Corinthians 1:20 this way: "For as many as are the promises of God, they all find their Yes [answer] in Him [Christ]. For this reason we also utter the Amen (so be it) to God through Him [in His Person and by His agency] to the glory of God." All the promises of God find their Yes in Christ. Every promise is answered. Every promise is fulfilled.

But claiming the promises requires faith and patience. Scripture says, "For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise" (Hebrews 10:36 KJV). The promises are Yes and Amen, but you must continue in faith, doing the will of God, and waiting patiently for the fulfilment.

Lesson: In Christ, every promise of God is Yes and Amen; but you must claim them by faith and wait patiently, doing the will of God.

Action: Today, choose one promise from God's Word and claim it by faith. Thank God that it is Yes and Amen in Christ, and commit to waiting patiently for it.

Bible Portions — Look Here. Every Promise Is Yes In Him.

    Christ is the Yes and Amen of every promise. Every promise of God finds its Yes in Him. What promise are you still doubting?

    Christ is the One in whom you are established. God has confirmed you in Him. Are you living in that confidence?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 2:14
    Christ is the One in whom you triumph. Not sometimes. Always. What place are you carrying His fragrance to today?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 3:14
    Christ is the One in whom the veil is taken away. You can see clearly now. What are you still living as if you cannot see?
  • in him: 2 Corinthians 5:21
    Christ is your Righteousness. He was made sin so that you might be made the righteousness of God in Him. Are you still trying to become righteous?

Claim the promises. Every promise is Yes and Amen in Christ. Not someday. Now. Claim them by faith.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ all Your promises are Yes and Amen. They are confirmed, guaranteed, and available to me. And I choose to claim them by faith and wait patiently.

Confess this: All the promises of God are Yes and Amen in Christ. Every promise is confirmed to me. Every promise is fulfilled in Him. I claim every promise by faith. I wait patiently, doing the will of God. The promises of God are mine, and they are sure.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Corinthians 1:21 KJV - "Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God."
devotionals.devotional:
God has done three things for you in Christ: He has established you, He has anointed you, and He has sealed you. You are not wavering, you are established. You are not powerless, you are anointed. You are not uncertain, you are sealed. God Himself has done these things for you, and they cannot be undone.

Scripture says, "Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God; Who hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts" (2 Corinthians 1:21-22 KJV). God has established you in Christ. God has anointed you. God has sealed you. God has given you the earnest of the Spirit in your heart.

The Amplified Bible renders 2 Corinthians 1:21 this way: "But it is God Who confirms and makes us steadfast and establishes us [in joint fellowship] with you in Christ, and has consecrated and anointed us [enduing us with the gifts of the Holy Spirit]." God has confirmed you. He has made you steadfast. He has established you. He has anointed you with the Holy Spirit.

But being established does not mean you cannot fall. Scripture says, "Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall" (1 Corinthians 10:12 KJV). The one who is established by God must still walk in humility and watchfulness. God has established you. But you must continue in Him, grounded and settled.

Lesson: In Christ, God has established, anointed, and sealed you; but you must walk in humility and watchfulness, continuing in Him.

Action: Today, rest in the knowledge that God has established, anointed, and sealed you. Then, walk in humility and watchfulness.

Bible Portions — Look Here. You Are Established, Anointed, And Sealed.

  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 1:21
    Christ is the One in whom you are established. God has confirmed you in Him. Are you living in that confidence?
  • in him: 2 Corinthians 1:20
    Christ is the Yes and Amen of every promise. Every promise of God finds its Yes in Him. What promise are you still doubting?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 2:14
    Christ is the One in whom you triumph. Not sometimes. Always. What place are you carrying His fragrance to today?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 5:17
    Christ is the Source of a new creation. If you are in Christ, you are a new creature. Are you still living as the old person?
  • in Christ: 2 Corinthians 5:19
    Christ is the One in whom God was reconciling the world to Himself. You are part of that reconciliation. Who are you carrying that message to?

Rest in this. You are established, anointed, and sealed. Not wavering. Not powerless. Not uncertain. Live in that security.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that in Christ You have established me, anointed me, and sealed me. I am secure in You. And I choose to walk in humility and watchfulness.

Confess this: God has established me in Christ. God has anointed me. God has sealed me. I am steadfast. I am anointed with the Holy Spirit. I am sealed by God. I walk in humility. I take heed lest I fall. I continue in Him.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Corinthians 3:11 KJV - "For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ."
devotionals.devotional:
This is a new journey. For the past 45 devotionals, we walked through the In Him realities — the believer's position and possessions in Christ. Now we turn to Building On The Solid Foundation, a companion series on the foundational truths of the Christian faith. For the next 45 devotionals, we will examine what every believer must know and live: the Word of God, salvation, spiritual growth, the Holy Spirit, prayer, evangelism, stewardship, spiritual warfare, and more. And we will follow the same simple pattern: read, understand, meditate, believe, confess, act, and continue.

Every building is only as strong as its foundation. A house may have beautiful walls, a fine roof, and elegant furnishings, but if the foundation is faulty, the whole structure will collapse when the storm comes. The same is true of your Christian life. Your foundation determines your durability and your stability.

Jesus said, "Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock" (Matthew 7:24-25 KJV). The wise builder did not just hear the Word; he acted on it. His foundation was solid because it was built on obedience to the Word.

The Scripture declares, "For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ" (1 Corinthians 3:11 KJV). The foundation of your Christian life is not a doctrine, not a church, not a pastor, and not a feeling. It is a Person — Jesus Christ Himself. He is the Rock upon which every believer must build. If you build on anything else, your foundation will sink under the storms of life.

Lesson: The only sure foundation for the Christian life is Jesus Christ; you must build your life and faith on Him alone.

Action: Today, examine the foundation of your faith. Ask yourself honestly: am I building on Christ, or on something else? Recommit yourself to building on Him.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that Jesus Christ is my foundation. I choose today to build my life on Him alone, and not on shifting sands.

Confess this: Jesus Christ is my foundation. I build my life on Him. I hear His Word and I do it. I am like the wise builder who built his house on the rock. The storms may come, but I will not fall, because my foundation is Christ.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Timothy 2:19 KJV - "Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity."
devotionals.devotional:
God did not leave the foundation of your faith to chance. He laid it Himself. He did not ask you to find a foundation; He provided one. And what He has laid is sure, unmovable, and eternal. You can build on it with absolute confidence.

Scripture says, "Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste" (Isaiah 28:16 KJV). God Himself laid the foundation. It is a tried stone, a precious corner stone. It has been tested and proven. It will hold under every storm, every trial, and every pressure of life.

The Apostle Paul declared, "Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity" (2 Timothy 2:19 KJV). The foundation of God is secure. It bears a seal, and that seal says two things: the Lord knows those who are His, and those who belong to Him must depart from iniquity.

You must understand that your security rests not in your own strength but in the One who laid the foundation. God knows you. He has sealed you as His own. But you must also live a life that honours the foundation you stand on. Depart from iniquity. Live in holiness and obedience. The foundation is sure, and those who build on it will never be put to shame.

Lesson: God Himself laid the sure foundation in Christ; you can build on it with confidence because it is tried, precious, and eternal.

Action: Today, thank God that He laid the foundation for you. Then, in response, examine your life and depart from anything that dishonours Him.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that You laid a sure foundation in Christ. I do not have to build on sinking sand; I build on the tried and precious Corner Stone.

Confess this: The foundation of God stands sure. I am built on Christ, the tried and precious Corner Stone. The Lord knows me, and I belong to Him. I depart from iniquity. I build on the sure foundation, and I will not be moved.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Peter 2:5 KJV - "Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ."
devotionals.devotional:
Once you have the right foundation, you must build on it. The foundation is laid, but the building must be raised. God has called you to build on Christ, and He has given you clear instructions on how to do it. You are not a passive observer; you are a builder.

When Jesus asked His disciples who they believed He was, Peter answered, "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God" (Matthew 16:16 KJV). Jesus replied, "...upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it" (Matthew 16:18 KJV). The Rock is Christ Himself, and His church is built on that confession of faith.

Paul wrote to the Ephesians, "Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellow citizens with the saints, and of the household of God; And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone; In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord" (Ephesians 2:19-21 KJV). You are a living stone in the building of God, and you are being fitted together with the rest of the body into a dwelling place for Him.

You must build on the foundation by surrendering your life to Christ, hearing and obeying His words, following His example, and holding fast to the teaching of the apostles and prophets. And you must be careful with the materials you use. Paul warned, "...if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire" (1 Corinthians 3:12-13 KJV).

Lesson: You are a living stone in God's building; you must build on Christ with care, using only materials that will endure the fire.

Action: Today, examine the materials you are building into your Christian life. Are you building with gold, silver, and precious stones, or with wood, hay, and stubble?
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that I am a living stone in Your building. I choose today to build carefully on Christ, using materials that will endure.

Confess this: I am built on the foundation of Christ. I am a living stone in God's building. I build with gold, silver, and precious stones. I hear the Word and I obey it. I follow Christ's example. My work will endure the fire.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 11:3 KJV - "If the foundations be destroyed, what can the righteous do?"
devotionals.devotional:
There are two ways to destroy a building. The first is to tamper with the foundation. The second is to build with inferior materials. Both are dangerous, and both carry serious consequences. The same principles apply to your Christian life. You must guard your foundation, and you must build carefully on it.

The Psalmist asked, "If the foundations be destroyed, what can the righteous do?" (Psalm 11:3 KJV). When the foundation is destroyed, the entire structure is in danger. If you allow your foundation in Christ to be undermined by false teaching, unbelief, or compromise, the entire building of your life will be at risk. You must guard your foundation above all else.

Paul warned about building with the wrong materials: "Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire" (1 Corinthians 3:12-15 KJV).

You must guard your foundation by staying rooted in Christ and His Word. And you must build carefully, knowing that one day your work will be tested by fire. The question is not whether you will be saved; the question is whether your work will endure. Build with materials that will last for eternity.

Lesson: You must guard your foundation and build carefully with materials that will endure the fire, because both can be lost if you are not watchful.

Action: Today, identify any area where your foundation is being undermined by doubt, false teaching, or compromise. Take a step to guard and strengthen it.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that You have given me a secure foundation in Christ. I choose today to guard that foundation and to build with materials that will endure.

Confess this: I guard my foundation in Christ. I will not allow it to be undermined by doubt, false teaching, or compromise. I build with gold, silver, and precious stones. My work will endure the fire. I am rooted in Christ.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Hebrews 11:6 KJV - "But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him."
devotionals.devotional:
The existence of God is not a theory to be debated. It is a truth to be embraced. God has revealed Himself to every human being in multiple ways, and the evidence is all around us. The only reason anyone denies His existence is that they have chosen to suppress the truth.

Scripture says, "The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God" (Psalm 14:1 KJV). Notice, it does not say the wise man says there is no God. It is the fool — the one who ignores the evidence and suppresses the truth in his heart. The evidence for God is overwhelming, and it is available to everyone.

The Apostle Paul declared, "Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse" (Romans 1:19-20 KJV). Creation itself is a witness. Your conscience is a witness. Your very existence is a witness. God has made Himself known, and He has left no one without evidence.

You must believe that God exists. Not because you can see Him with your physical eyes, but because His Word declares it, and the evidence surrounds you. Without faith, it is impossible to please Him. But with faith, you can know Him and walk with Him. He is real, and He is a rewarder of those who diligently seek Him.

Lesson: God's existence is clearly revealed in creation, conscience, and His Word; you must believe that He is and that He rewards those who seek Him.

Action: Today, take a moment to look around at creation and thank God for revealing Himself to you. Then, spend time seeking Him in prayer.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that You have revealed Yourself to me. I believe that You exist, and I believe that You are a rewarder of those who diligently seek You.

Confess this: I believe that God exists. I see His hand in creation. I hear His voice in my conscience. I know His truth through His Word. He is real, and He is a rewarder of those who diligently seek Him. I seek Him today.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Psalm 19:1 KJV - "The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork."
devotionals.devotional:
God has not hidden Himself from humanity. He has revealed His existence in ways that are clear, universal, and undeniable. The problem is not a lack of evidence; the problem is a refusal to acknowledge the evidence. God has made Himself known to every person on earth.

The Scripture says, "The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork" (Psalm 19:1 KJV). The universe is a declaration of God's glory. The stars, the planets, the galaxies, the intricate design of creation — all of it points to a Creator. You do not need a telescope or a microscope to find God; He is revealed in the ordinary things of life.

The Apostle Paul, together with Barnabas, declared to the people of Lystra, "...and preach unto you that ye should turn from these vanities unto the living God, which made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and all things that are therein: Who in times past suffered all nations to walk in their own ways. Nevertheless he left not himself without witness, in that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness" (Acts 14:15-17 KJV).

God reveals Himself in three primary ways. First, through existential truth — every soul has a sense of God, whether they acknowledge it or not. Second, through conscience — the moral compass within each person tells us that there is a moral Being who created us. Third, through our existence — the fact that we exist teaches us that God exists as our Creator. You must recognise these witnesses and respond to them with faith.

Lesson: God has revealed His existence through creation, conscience, and our very existence; you must acknowledge these witnesses and respond in faith.

Action: Today, look for God's fingerprints in creation, in your conscience, and in your own existence. Thank Him for revealing Himself to you.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that You have revealed Yourself through creation, through my conscience, and through my very existence. I choose today to acknowledge Your presence in every area of my life.

Confess this: The heavens declare the glory of God. My conscience bears witness to His moral law. My existence points to my Creator. I acknowledge God in all things. He is real, and He has made Himself known to me.

devotionals.memoryVerse: John 4:24 KJV - "God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth."
devotionals.devotional:
To know God, you must understand His nature. God is not a distant, impersonal force. He is a personal, spiritual Being with a character that He has revealed in His Word. The better you understand His nature, the deeper your relationship with Him will become.

Jesus said, "God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth" (John 4:24 KJV). God is spirit. He is invisible, without material substance, without physical parts, and free from all temporal limitations. He is not confined to a place or a form. He is a Spirit, and He must be worshipped in spirit and in truth.

Scripture also says, "He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love" (1 John 4:8 KJV). God is love. Not only does He love, but He is love. Every expression of His nature flows out of His love. His holiness, His justice, His mercy, and His grace are all expressions of His loving character. When you understand that God is love, you can trust Him completely.

God is also a person. He has self-consciousness and self-determination. He thinks, He feels, He chooses, and He acts. He is not an abstract concept; He is a living Being who desires relationship with you. And He is triune — Father, Son, and Holy Spirit — three eternal and co-equal persons in one Godhead. You worship a God who is personal, spiritual, loving, and triune.

Lesson: God is a Spirit, He is love, and He is a personal Being; you must worship Him in spirit and truth and trust His loving nature.

Action: Today, spend time meditating on the nature of God. Thank Him that He is love, that He is Spirit, and that He is a personal God who desires relationship with you.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that You are a Spirit and that You are love. I choose today to worship You in spirit and truth and to trust Your loving nature.

Confess this: God is a Spirit, and I worship Him in spirit and in truth. God is love, and I trust His loving nature. He is personal, and He desires relationship with me. He is Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. I worship Him with all my heart.

devotionals.topic: How We Know That God Exists
devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Peter 1:21 KJV - "For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost."
devotionals.devotional:
How do you know that God exists? The answer is twofold: the Scripture tells you, and faith receives it. The testimony of the Word of God and the response of faith are the two pillars on which your knowledge of God rests. Without either one, your knowledge will be incomplete.

The Scripture says, "Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost" (2 Peter 1:20-21 KJV). The Bible is not a human book. It is the Word of God, spoken through holy men who were moved by the Holy Spirit. When you read the Bible, you are not reading the opinions of men; you are hearing the voice of God.

The Scripture also says, "But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him" (Hebrews 11:6 KJV). You cannot know God by reason alone. You must believe. Faith is the means by which you receive the testimony of Scripture. Faith is not a blind leap; it is a confident trust in the God who has revealed Himself in His Word.

You must understand that the knowledge of God is essential. It governs your lifestyle and determines your eternal destiny. If you know God, you will live for Him. If you do not know Him, you will live for yourself. Take time to know God through His Word. Listen to His testimony. Respond in faith. And as you do, you will know Him more deeply.

Lesson: You know that God exists through the testimony of Scripture and through faith; both are essential for a true knowledge of Him.

Action: Today, read a portion of Scripture and respond to it in faith. Let the Word of God build your knowledge of Him.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that You have given me Your Word as a testimony of Your existence. I choose today to believe Your Word and to know You more deeply.

Confess this: The Scripture is the testimony of God. I believe it. I know that God exists because His Word declares it, and I receive it by faith. He is a rewarder of those who diligently seek Him. I seek Him today.

devotionals.topic: The Word Of God Is Our Authority
devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Timothy 3:16 KJV - "All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness."
devotionals.devotional:
The Bible is not merely a book that contains the words of God; it is the Word of God. Every word, every sentence, every page is inspired by God Himself. This means that the Bible is your final authority in all matters of faith, doctrine, and conduct. If God said it, that settles it.

Scripture says, "All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works" (2 Timothy 3:16-17 KJV). The Bible is God-breathed. It is profitable for teaching, rebuking, correcting, and training in righteousness. It is sufficient for every area of your life.

When you read the Bible, you are not reading the words of men; you are reading the words of God. To disbelieve or disobey any word of the Bible is to disbelieve or disobey God. This is why the authority of Scripture is so important. If you accept the Bible as God's Word, you must submit to its authority in every area of your life.

You must never treat the Word of God lightly. You must read it, study it, meditate on it, and obey it. The Word is your compass, your guide, and your foundation. When you build your life on the Word, you build on solid ground. When you disobey the Word, you build on sand. Choose to submit to the authority of Scripture in every area of your life.

Lesson: The Bible is the inspired Word of God and your final authority; you must read, study, and obey it in every area of your life.

Action: Today, choose one area of your life where you have not been submitting to the authority of Scripture. Bring it into obedience to the Word.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that Your Word is inspired and authoritative. I choose today to submit to its authority in every area of my life.

Confess this: The Bible is the Word of God. It is inspired, authoritative, and sufficient. I read it, I study it, and I obey it. I submit to its authority in every area of my life. When God says it, that settles it.

devotionals.topic: The Truth And Purity Of God's Word
devotionals.memoryVerse: John 17:17 KJV - "Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth."
devotionals.devotional:
The Word of God is completely true and without error. Every word is pure, every promise is reliable, and every command is righteous. Because the Bible is the Word of God, and God cannot lie, you can trust it with your whole heart. There is no mixture of error, no falsehood, and no deception in it.

Scripture says, "For ever, O Lord, thy word is settled in heaven" (Psalm 119:89 KJV). The Word of God is settled. It is not up for debate, and it is not subject to the shifting opinions of men. It stands forever. And again, "Thy word is true from the beginning: and every one of thy righteous judgments endureth for ever" (Psalm 119:160 KJV).

Jesus prayed, "Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth" (John 17:17 KJV). The Word of God is the ultimate definition of what is true and what is not. The truth is not what you feel, what culture says, or what is popular. The truth is what God says in the Bible. This is why the Word is our final authority — it is the only infallible and unfailing rule of faith and practice.

You must build your life on the truth of God's Word. You must believe it, obey it, and stand on it. The Word is your spiritual food, your weapon, and your cleansing. It is your final authority, and it will never fail you. When everything else changes, the Word of God remains the same.

Lesson: The Word of God is completely true, pure, and without error; you can trust it as your final authority and stand on it without fear.

Action: Today, take one promise from the Word of God and stand on it with confidence. Thank God that His Word is true and settled forever.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that Your Word is true and pure. I choose today to build my life on the truth of Your Word and to stand on it without wavering.

Confess this: The Word of God is true. It is settled in heaven forever. It is pure, without error, and completely reliable. I build my life on the truth of Your Word. Your Word is my final authority, and I will stand on it.

devotionals.topic: The Word Of God Is Our Spiritual Food
devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Peter 2:2 KJV - "As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby."
devotionals.devotional:
Just as your physical body needs food to survive and grow, your spirit needs the Word of God. The Word is your spiritual nourishment. Without it, you will remain weak and stunted in your faith. With it, you will grow strong and mature in the things of God.

Scripture says, "As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby" (1 Peter 2:2 KJV). Peter compares the Word to milk for a newborn baby. A baby craves milk because it is necessary for life and growth. In the same way, you must crave the Word. You must long for it, pursue it, and feed on it daily.

Jesus said, "It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God" (Matthew 4:4 KJV). You cannot survive spiritually on one meal a week. You need a daily diet of the Word. The more you feed on it, the stronger you become.

The Psalmist declared, "How sweet are thy words unto my taste! yea, sweeter than honey to my mouth!" (Psalm 119:103 KJV). The Word is not just nourishment; it is a delight. As you read it, meditate on it, and apply it, you will discover that it is sweeter than honey and more precious than gold. Feed on the Word today, and watch your spiritual life flourish.

Lesson: The Word of God is your spiritual food; you must feed on it daily to grow strong and mature in your faith.

Action: Today, set aside time to feed on the Word of God. Read it, meditate on it, and let it nourish your spirit.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that Your Word is my spiritual food. I choose today to feed on it daily, so that I may grow strong in my faith.

Confess this: I desire the sincere milk of the Word. I feed on the Word of God daily. It is sweeter than honey to my taste. It nourishes my spirit. I grow strong in the Lord because I feed on His Word.

devotionals.topic: The Word Of God Is Our Cleansing
devotionals.memoryVerse: John 15:3 KJV - "Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you."
devotionals.devotional:
The Word of God is not only food for your spirit; it is also cleansing for your soul. It washes away the stains of sin, renews your mind, and sanctifies you for God's purposes. The more you apply the Word to your life, the cleaner and more consecrated you become.

Scripture says that Christ loved the church and gave Himself for it, "That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word" (Ephesians 5:26 KJV). The Word is the water that washes you. It cleanses you from the defilement of the world, and it sets you apart for God's use.

Jesus prayed, "Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth" (John 17:17 KJV). Sanctification is not a one-time event; it is an ongoing process. As you continue to apply the Word to your life, you are continually cleansed, continually sanctified, continually set apart for God's purposes.

Jesus said to His disciples, "Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you" (John 15:3 KJV). The Word had cleansed them. The same Word can cleanse you. If you have been defiled by sin, failure, or the world's influence, let the Word wash you. Read it, meditate on it, apply it, and let it do its cleansing work in your heart.

Lesson: The Word of God is your cleansing; as you apply it to your life, you are washed, sanctified, and set apart for God's use.

Action: Today, allow the Word of God to cleanse your heart. Confess any sin to God, and let His Word wash you clean.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that Your Word is my cleansing. I choose today to apply Your Word to my life so that I may be washed and sanctified.

Confess this: The Word of God cleanses me. It washes away my sin and renews my mind. I am clean through the Word which Jesus has spoken to me. I am sanctified by the truth of Your Word.

devotionals.topic: The Word Of God Is Our Weapon
devotionals.memoryVerse: Ephesians 6:17 KJV - "And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God."
devotionals.devotional:
The Word of God is not just a defensive tool; it is an offensive weapon. It is the sword of the Spirit, and it is your primary weapon in spiritual warfare. When the enemy comes against you, the Word is what you use to fight back.

Scripture says, "And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God" (Ephesians 6:17 KJV). The sword is both offensive and defensive. It protects you from the enemy's attacks, and it empowers you to advance against his strongholds. But a sword is only effective if you know how to use it. You must know the Word if you are going to wield it effectively.

The Bible says, "For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart" (Hebrews 4:12 KJV). The Word is alive. It is powerful. It is sharper than any physical sword. It cuts through every lie of the enemy and every deception of the world.

You must fill your heart with the Word so that you are ready to use it when the enemy comes. Jesus demonstrated this when He was tempted in the wilderness. Each time Satan attacked, Jesus responded with, "It is written" (Matthew 4:4 KJV). The Word is your weapon. Use it. Speak it. Stand on it. And the enemy will flee.

Lesson: The Word of God is your offensive and defensive weapon; you must know it and use it to overcome the enemy.

Action: Today, memorise one scripture that addresses a temptation or challenge you are facing. Speak it aloud when the enemy comes against you.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that Your Word is my weapon. I choose today to fill my heart with Your Word and to use it against the enemy.

Confess this: The Word of God is my sword. It is quick and powerful. I use it against the enemy. I speak it, and the enemy flees. I stand on the Word of God, and I overcome every attack of the enemy.

devotionals.topic: Christmas Eve: The Word Became Flesh
devotionals.memoryVerse: John 1:14 KJV - "And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth."
devotionals.devotional:
